articles.title: Puerarin alleviates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury-induced oxidative stress via the Neurl1/JAG1/Notch1 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI) remains a major challenge in stroke therapy, with limited effective neuroprotective interventions. Puerarin (Pue), a major bioactive isoflavone from Pueraria lobata, exhibits promising neuroprotective effects, yet its precise molecular targets and mechanisms remain unclear. PURPOSE: To elucidate the molecular mechanisms of Pue's neuroprotection against CIRI, including its direct protein target and downstream signaling pathways. METHODS: Both in vivo and in vitro models were employed, including transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) in rats and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) in HT22 cells. Neuroprotective effects were assessed by infarct volume, neurological scores, histopathology, oxidative stress markers (SOD, GSH, MDA), reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). An integrated transcriptomic-computational screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used to identify Neuralized E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (Neurl1) as a potential molecular target of Pue. Functional validation of candidate genes was conducted via genetic knockdown and pharmacological modulation (JAG1 peptide, DAPT). RESULTS: Pue dose-dependently reduced cerebral infarct volume, attenuated neurological deficits and histopathological damage, and alleviated oxidative stress in tMCAO rats. In OGD/R HT22 cells, Pue suppressed cytosolic and mitochondrial ROS accumulation and preserved mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). Neuralized E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (Neurl1) was identified as a molecular target of Pue. Mechanistically, Pue restored CIRI-induced suppression of Neurl1 protein expression in both tMCAO rats and OGD/R HT22 cells, accompanied by downregulation of Jagged1 (JAG1) and inhibition of Notch1 signaling. Neurl1 knockdown partially counteracted protective effects of Pue against oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. In vivo, co-administration of a Notch1 activator (JAG1 peptide) partially reversed the neuroprotective effects of Pue, whereas Notch1 inhibition with DAPT showed neuroprotective effects comparable to those of Pue. CONCLUSION: Pue exerts neuroprotective effects against CIRI by restoring Neurl1 expression, which is associated with modulation of the JAG1/Notch1 signaling pathway and attenuation of oxidative stress. These findings identify the Neurl1/JAG1/Notch1 axis as a potential therapeutic target for CIRI.

articles.title: Derivation and characterization of a patient-derived hiPSC line carrying the HCN2 p.G460D variant with neuronal and cardiac differentiation potential.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathogenic variants in HCN2, encoding the hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channel 2, have recently emerged as a cause of developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs). Because HCN2 is expressed in both the central nervous and cardiovascular systems, disease mechanisms may extend beyond neuronal dysfunction and involve both neuronal and cardiac tissues. However, the lack of patient-specific human models has limited the investigation of tissue-specific and shared consequences of HCN2 dysfunction and the development of targeted therapeutic approaches. METHODS: A human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) line was generated via non-integrating Sendai viral vectors from dermal fibroblasts of a patient with severe drug-resistant DEE carrying the HCN2 c.1379G>A (p.G460D) variant. Following validation of genomic integrity, vector clearance, pluripotency, trilineage potential, and retention of the disease-causing variant, hiPSCs were subjected to directed differentiation toward cortical neurons and cardiomyocytes. Neuronal and cardiac lineage specification, subtype marker profiles, and endogenous HCN2 retention were assessed by RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence. In cardiomyocyte monolayers, functional beating kinetics, rhythm stability, and spatial electromechanical coupling were quantified using video-based motion tracking. RESULTS: Reprogramming established a patient hiPSC line carrying the heterozygous HCN2 p. G460D variant with a stable 46,XX karyotype, vector clearance, robust pluripotency, and verified trilineage potential. Directed differentiation yielded deep-layer glutamatergic cortical neurons expressing FOXG1, MAP2, BCL11B, and SLC17A7, forming extensive networks positive for TUBB3, MAP2, and NeuN. In parallel, cardiac differentiation produced functional cardiomyocytes expressing TNNT2, M YH6, and MYH7 with organized cTnT, ACTN2, and RYR2 sarcomeric structures. Both lineages retained endogenous HCN2 expression. Video kinematic profiling demonstrated progressive functional maturation of the beating cardiomyocytes, showing a 59.1% reduction in rhythm variability and enhanced spatial electromechanical coupling over time. CONCLUSION: We established the first patient-derived hiPSC platform carrying a pathogenic HCN2 variant associated with DEE. The ability to generate both neuronal and cardiac lineages from the same genetic background provides a valuable translational resource future mechanistic studies, cell-type-specific functional comparisons, and exploratory evaluation of potential therapeutic approaches in HCN2-related channelopathies.

articles.title: Fructus mume total flavonoids exert neuroprotective effects involving miR-143-3p and CaMKKβ/AMPK/mTOR signaling in experimental models of Parkinson's disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder in the elderly. Dysregulated mitophagy contributes to neuronal damage in PD. Fructus mume total flavonoids (FMF), a flavonoid-enriched extract prepared from Fructus mume, have shown neuroprotective effects in experimental models of PD. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Therefore, this study investigated whether the neuroprotective effects of FMF in rat models of PD were associated with mitophagy and explored the potential underlying mechanisms. METHODS: A rat model of PD was established by stereotaxic injection of 6-OHDA into the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and ventral tegmental area. HE staining, Nissl staining, TUNEL staining, immunohistochemistry staining and Western blotting were used to evaluate the effects of FMF and the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA) on neuronal injury and mitophagy in the SNpc. Additionally, an in vitro PD model was established by treating SH-SY5Y cells with MPP+ to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective effects of FMF. RESULTS: FMF treatment significantly increased the number of Nissl bodies and reduced neuronal apoptosis in the SNpc of PD rats. FMF also increased the expression of tyrosine hydroxylase, LC3-II, Beclin 1, p62, PINK1, Parkin and TOM20, while reducing α-synuclein accumulation in the SNpc. RT-qPCR analysis showed that FMF significantly upregulated miR-143-3p expression in both the SNpc of PD rats and MPP+-treated SH-SY5Y cells. Additionally, FMF promoted cell proliferation and the expression of mitophagy-related proteins and reduced apoptosis in MPP+-treated SH-SY5Y cells, whereas miR-143-3p inhibitor significantly weakened these pharmacological effects of FMF in MPP+-treated SH-SY5Y cells. Dual-luciferase reporter assays suggested a potential interaction between miR-143-3p and the CaMKKβ 3'UTR. Pharmacological inhibition of the CaMKKβ/AMPK/mTOR signaling pathway also weakened the pharmacological effects of FMF in MPP+-treated SH-SY5Y cells, and co-treatment with the miR-143-3p inhibitor further weakened the pharmacological effects of FMF. CONCLUSION: These findings suggested that FMF may exert neuroprotective effects in experimental models of PD, potentially involving miR-143-3p, CaMKKβ/AMPK/mTOR signaling and mitophagy-associated processes. These findings would provide new mechanistic insights into the neuroprotective effects of FMF and support the potential therapeutic application of FM and its flavonoids in PD.

articles.title: Costunolide attenuates neuroinflammation by targeting G3BP1 and APRT.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Costunolide (Cos) is a sesquiterpene lactone isolated from Saussurea lappa with reported anti-inflammatory properties. Its direct molecular targets in neuroinflammatory responses, however, have not been fully defined. METHODS: LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia were used to examine the effect of Cos on neuroinflammatory activation. Candidate binding proteins were screened using MetPro and further assessed by molecular docking. The roles of selected targets were tested by siRNA knockdown, while direct binding was examined using surface plasmon resonance (SPR). Transcriptome sequencing and qPCR were used to evaluate downstream inflammatory gene changes. RESULTS: Cos reduced LPS-induced phosphorylation of NF-κB p65, with little change in total p65 protein levels. MetPro analysis pointed to G3BP1 and APRT as potential Cos-associated proteins, and docking analysis supported possible binding of Cos to both targets. Knockdown of either G3BP1 or APRT reduced the inhibitory effect of Cos on p65 phosphorylation. SPR assays confirmed direct interaction between Cos and G3BP1/APRT. Transcriptomic analysis, together with qPCR validation, showed that Cos affected LPS-responsive inflammatory transcriptional programs. CONCLUSION: Cos suppresses microglial inflammatory activation partly through G3BP1 and APRT, with downstream inhibition of NF-κB-related signaling. These results provide mechanistic evidence for the anti-neuroinflammatory activity of Cos and support further investigation of its therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Retraction: Rubidium chloride targets Jnk/p38-mediated NF-κB activation to attenuate osteoclastogenesis and facilitate osteoblastogenesis.

articles.title: Quality of life and associated psychosocial factors in patients with invasive breast cancer receiving long-term anti-HER2 targeted therapy: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Breast cancer (BC) remains among the most prevalent malignancies in women worldwide, with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive subtypes accounting for approximately 15%-20% of cases. Although targeted therapy has substantially improved outcomes, its prolonged course and associated adverse events, including cardiotoxicity and bone marrow suppression, may considerably undermine patients' quality of life (QoL). We evaluated factors associated with QoL in HER2-positive BC patients receiving anti-HER2 targeted therapy. METHODS: A total of 206 female patients with pathologically confirmed HER2-positive invasive BC receiving anti-HER2 targeted therapy at the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University between July 2024 and June 2025 were consecutively enrolled. Data were collected with standardized instruments: the Acceptance of Illness Scale (AIS), Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS), Strategies Used by People to Promote Health (SUPPH), and Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Breast (FACT-B). Univariate analysis, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression examined factors associated with QoL. Structural equation modeling (SEM) using AMOS 28.0 then examined theory-driven associations grounded in Social Cognitive Theory and the Transactional Model of Stress and Coping. RESULTS: Mean scores were 89.60 ± 27.27 for QoL, 26.87 ± 6.64 for illness acceptance, 39.84 ± 12.21 for social support, and 94.86 ± 23.26 for self-efficacy, all within moderate ranges. QoL correlated positively with all three psychosocial variables (P < 0.01), most strongly with illness acceptance (r = 0.625). In the multivariable regression, infusion modality, illness acceptance, social support, and self-efficacy were independently associated with QoL. The SEM showed excellent fit (χ2/df = 1.257, RMSEA = 0.035, CFI = 0.982), with positive direct paths from illness acceptance (β = 0.558), social support (β = 0.238), and self-efficacy (β = 0.229) to QoL. Social support showed indirect associations with QoL through illness acceptance and self-efficacy. Self-efficacy also showed an indirect association with QoL through illness acceptance within the specified model. DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that QoL in patients receiving long-term anti-HER2 targeted therapy was associated with a combination of clinical and psychosocial factors, with illness acceptance, social support, and self-efficacy appearing particularly relevant. These associations should be regarded as correlational rather than causal, and prospective or interventional studies are needed to confirm them. The model offers a theoretical framework for these relationships and may inform the integration of psychosocial considerations into pharmaceutical care.

articles.title: Favorable performance of DGPR1008, a novel PSMA-targeted near-infrared fluorescent probe, for image-guided prostate cancer surgery in experimental models.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence-guided surgery has shown promise for prostate cancer (PCa). Despite several prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted NIR probes entering clinical trials, none have received approval to date, highlighting the continuing need for novel agents with improved pharmacokinetic and imaging properties to support NIR fluorescence-guided surgery. DGPR1008, a newly designed PSMA-targeted NIR probe, has been proposed as a potential candidate probe. Consequently, this study primarily aimed to characterize the binding specificity of DGPR1008 to PSMA and evaluate its imaging and pharmacological profiles. A secondary aim was to compare its performance with that of the already clinically evaluated probe OTL78 in animal models. METHODS: The PSMA-binding specificity of DGPR1008 was assessed in vitro in three PCa cell lines. Also, in vivo tumor targeting and fluorescence imaging, along with assessment of the biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, excretory clearance, and toxicity of DGPR1008, were performed in animal models. Finally, the pharmacokinetics, tissue distribution, imaging contrast, and tumor-to-background ratios of DGPR1008 were compared with those of the reference probe OTL78 at various time points post-injection. RESULTS: Binding assays performed in the three PCa cell lines demonstrated the high affinity of DGPR1008 for PSMA. Meanwhile, the in vivo tests showed that DGPR1008 achieved selective tumor accumulation and rapid non-target clearance. Compared to the reference probe OTL78, DGPR1008 exhibited stronger, more persistent tumor fluorescence and tumor-to-background contrast in mice bearing subcutaneous xenografts. Furthermore, DGPR1008 displayed favorable pharmacokinetics and excretion profiles, with a notably faster plasma clearance than the reference probe OTL78. CONCLUSION: DGPR1008 demonstrated high PSMA specificity in vitro and favorable imaging performance in a PCa xenograft mouse model. Together with its favorable pharmacokinetic and safety profiles, these findings support the use of DGPR1008 as a promising real-time NIR fluorescence imaging probe for guiding PCa surgery with potential for clinical translation.

articles.title: Bisphenol a is associated with ovarian cancer chemoresistance via ecmCAF-mediated stromal remodeling: an integrative multi-omics study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: BPA is a ubiquitous endocrine disruptor linked to ovarian cancer, yet its effect on chemotherapy efficacy is unknown. CAFs drive drug resistance via microenvironment remodeling. We investigated whether BPA exposure is associated with chemoresistance via CAF-mediated stromal reprogramming. METHODS: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on ovarian cancer samples across treatment-naive, post-chemotherapy, and recurrent states (n = 10). BPA target gene set activity was quantified across cell types using AUCell scoring. Fibroblasts were re-clustered to characterize CAF subtypes. BPA target genes were integrated from public databases, with core targets prioritized through protein-protein interaction networks and molecular docking. Machine learning models were built for chemoresistance prediction, and in vitro validation was performed; CellChat inferred intercellular communication dynamics. RESULTS: Fibroblasts exhibited the highest BPA-driven activity among all tumor cells. The extracellular matrix CAF (ecmCAF) subtype showed elevated BPA scores. Integration of BPA targets, ecmCAF markers, and recurrence signatures yielded hub genes, with molecular docking predicting favorable BPA binding to PTGS2 (-7.7), MMP2 (-7.6), and SERPINE1 (-7.5 kcal/mol). CellChat revealed heightened CAF-to-epithelial pro-EMT and CAF-to-immune suppressive signaling in the recurrent sample. In vitro validation further showed that BPA treatment increased ACTA2 and COL1A1 expression in CAFs and that conditioned medium from BPA-treated CAFs enhanced SKOV3 resistance to cisplatin. CONCLUSION: The BPA-ecmCAF axis represents a novel mechanism linking environmental exposure to ovarian cancer chemoresistance through microenvironment remodeling. These findings identify ecmCAF effectors as candidate exposure biomarkers and suggest that environmental risk assessment should consider the potential of BPA to compromise cancer treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Arctiin attenuates the development of psoriasis-like dermatitis and modulates EGFR-associated ERK signaling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease characterized by keratinocyte hyperproliferation, immune cell infiltration, and increased dermal angiogenesis. Although current therapies provide symptomatic relief, long-term disease control remains challenging. Arctiin (ARC), a major lignan glycoside of Arctii Fructus from Arctium lappa L., exerts anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects on several inflammatory diseases. However, the effects of ARC on psoriasis-like inflammation and the signaling mechanisms involved remain unclear. PURPOSE: To investigate the effects of ARC in psoriasis-related experimental models and elucidate the signaling pathways involved. METHODS: The effects of oral ARC administration were evaluated in an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like dermatitis model. Clinical severity, histopathology, immune cell infiltration, dermal vascular changes, and inflammatory gene expression were assessed. An exploratory network analysis, together with a transcriptomic analysis of publicly available human psoriasis datasets, was used to prioritize signaling nodes for experimental investigation. In primary human keratinocytes, ARC-mediated inflammatory and signaling responses were evaluated using RT‒qPCR and immunoblotting. RESULTS: Oral ARC administration attenuated the development of imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like skin lesions; reduced epidermal hyperplasia, immune cell infiltration, and dermal angiogenesis; and downregulated inflammatory mediator expression. The exploratory network analysis recurrently prioritized epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) among several candidate signaling nodes, whereas human psoriasis transcriptomic data revealed increased expression of multiple EGFR ligands in lesional skin and supported the relevance of EGFR-associated signaling in epidermal keratinocytes. In keratinocytes, ARC reduced the expression of psoriasis-associated inflammatory mediators and suppressed the phosphorylation of EGFR, ERK, and JNK. EGFR knockdown abolished the additional suppressive effect of ARC on ERK phosphorylation, whereas the suppression of JNK phosphorylation persisted. EGFR knockdown also attenuated the inhibitory effects of ARC on the expression of several psoriasis-related inflammatory mediators. Consistent with the cellular findings, ARC administration was associated with reduced EGFR, ERK, and JNK phosphorylation in imiquimod-treated skin. CONCLUSION: ARC attenuates the development of psoriasis-like inflammation and is associated with the modulation of EGFR-associated ERK signaling. These findings suggest that ARC may represent a potential candidate treatment for psoriasis.

articles.title: Development of a mitochondrial fluorescent probe reveals anti-colorectal cancer activity via the ZNF124/YES1/YAP1 axis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Mitochondria are acknowledged to play diverse and critical roles in the development of malignant tumors. Therapeutic agents targeting mitochondria present promising opportunities for cancer treatment. This study aims to synthesize a mitochondrial fluorescent probe, designated MTC-05, and to assess its antitumor efficacy against colorectal cancer (CRC) both in vitro and in vivo. METHODS: The subcellular localization of MTC-05 was investigated using Mito-Tracker Green FM staining. The antitumor effects of MTC-05 on colorectal cancer cells were evaluated in vitro through assays including cell cycle analysis, colony formation, EdU incorporation, apoptosis detection, wound healing, and trans-well migration assays. Additionally, a xenograft mouse model was employed to assess the therapeutic impact of MTC-05 in vivo. RNA sequencing and α-ketoglutarate level measurements were conducted to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: The findings demonstrated that MTC-05 selectively localizes to mitochondria and effectively inhibits malignant phenotypes of CRC. Specifically, MTC-05 markedly suppressed CRC cell proliferation and migration while inducing apoptosis. RNA sequencing analysis revealed that MTC-05 inhibited the activation of several key kinase signaling pathways, including Hippo, Wnt, PI3K/Akt, and MAPK pathways, as well as downregulated the expression of the critical target gene ZNF124. Furthermore, quantification of α-ketoglutarate (α-KG), a metabolite associated with mitochondrial function, showed that MTC-05 significantly elevated α-KG levels. Acting as a second messenger, α-KG inhibited the activation of the ZNF124/YES1/YAP1 signaling axis, thereby impeding CRC progression. In vivo experiments confirmed that MTC-05 effectively suppressed tumor growth and metastasis in CRC models without inducing cytotoxic effects. CONCLUSION: MTC-05 exerts antitumor activity against colorectal cancer by targeting mitochondria and modulating α-ketoglutarate metabolism, which in turn suppresses the activation of the ZNF124/YES1/YAP1 signaling pathway, thereby inhibiting malignant progression.

articles.title: Readiness of pharmacists to support medication use among people with visual impairment in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: People with visual impairment may experience difficulties accessing medication information and managing medications safely, increasing the risk of medication errors. Pharmacists can play an important role in addressing these challenges, yet their readiness to provide accessible medication support in Saudi Arabia remains unclear. This study assessed the readiness of pharmacists to support medication use among people with visual impairment. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among registered pharmacists with direct patient contact in Saudi Arabia between May and August 2026. The questionnaire assessed workplace accessibility resources, awareness of medication-use challenges, current practices, confidence, workplace preparedness, training needs, and perceived barriers. Descriptive statistics analyses were used to summarize quantitative responses. A mean practice score was calculated, and associated factors were examined using univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses, with unstandardized β coefficients and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. Open-ended responses were analyzed using content analysis. RESULTS: A total of 254 pharmacists were included. Most recognized that visual impairment increases the risk of medication errors (91.3%) and that inaccessible medication information may adversely affect adherence (80%). Detailed verbal counselling was the most frequently reported supportive practice (66%), whereas providing alternative medication instructions, such as large-print or audio formats, was least frequent (33%). Although 62.6% reported confidence in providing support, only 39.4% considered their workplaces prepared, and 74.4% indicated a need for additional training. The most commonly reported barriers were time and workload pressures (59%), lack of accessible medication-labelling tools (56%), insufficient training (54%), and limited assistive technologies (47%). In adjusted analysis, confidence was associated with higher practice scores (β = 0.15, 95% CI 0.03-0.27; p = 0.011). CONCLUSION: Pharmacists reported high awareness and confidence, but gaps remained in accessibility-specific practices and workplace preparedness. Strengthening pharmacist training, accessible medication-support tools, and organizational preparedness may help address these gaps and inform future pharmacist-led interventions.

articles.title: Beyond evidence hierarchies: governing clinical uncertainty in ATMP assessment in Europe. A focus group study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products (ATMPs) pose significant challenges for health technology assessment (HTA) due to high levels of clinical uncertainty at the time of assessment. These uncertainties are often driven by reliance on single-arm trials, surrogate endpoints, and limited long-term data. While methodological guidance exists, less is known about how such uncertainty is interpreted and managed in real-world decision-making across stakeholders. This study aims to explore the perspectives of European stakeholders on key evidentiary challenges and approaches to clinical uncertainty management in ATMP assessment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two online focus group discussions were conducted with stakeholders involved in ATMP development and assessment, including representatives from academia, industry, HTA bodies, and payer organisations. The first focus group (n = 7) addressed challenges related to comparator selection, while the second (n = 5) focused on long-term outcomes and surrogate endpoints. Discussions were guided by a semi-structured topic guide informed by a literature review and were audio- and video-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using thematic framework analysis. RESULTS: Across both focus groups, uncertainty emerged as a central and persistent feature of ATMP assessment. According to participants, evidence is evaluated within a broader clinical and contextual framework, where factors such as disease severity, unmet need, and expected treatment effect shape the acceptability of uncertainty. Single-arm trials and surrogate endpoints were considered conditionally acceptable, particularly when randomised evidence is infeasible, but were associated with important limitations. Indirect treatment comparisons were viewed as methodologically constrained yet often necessary in the absence of comparative data. Evidence generation was described as a question-driven and iterative process, balancing methodological rigour with feasibility and ethical considerations. Biological plausibility and anticipated clinical benefit influenced evidence interpretation, while real-world evidence was seen as important but limited in its ability to resolve uncertainty post-launch. Participants noted that uncertainty is rarely eliminated and is instead managed throughout the product lifecycle. CONCLUSION: Clinical uncertainty in ATMP assessment appears to be an inherent feature of decision-making rather than a temporary consequence of incomplete evidence. Addressing this requires more flexible, context-sensitive, and lifecycle-oriented approaches to evidence generation and assessment.

articles.title: Pharmacological inhibition of V-ATPase reduces extracellular ATP and glutamate and delays neural tube closure in Xenopus laevis.
articles.abstract: Neurulation requires coordinated morphogenetic movements and extracellular signals for timely neural tube closure. Although purinergic and glutamatergic signaling has been implicated in this process, whether V-ATPase-dependent vesicular processes contribute to extracellular ATP and glutamate accumulation remains unclear. In Xenopus laevis embryos, we assessed the expression of vesicular-machinery components during neurulation and the effects of pharmacological V-ATPase inhibition with bafilomycin A1 (BafA1). Transcripts of VNUT, VGLUT1-3, V-ATPase subunit c, and SNARE-associated components were detected between stages 12.5 and 20 and VNUT and VGLUT1/2 immunoreactivity was also detected by Western blot. BafA1 exposure increased incomplete neural tube closure at stage 20 in a concentration-dependent manner, consistent with delayed closure, and reduced cumulative path length and mean speed of tracked pigmented cells in the dorsal neuroepithelial region. At stage 18, BafA1 reduced ATP and glutamate accumulation in whole-embryo-conditioned medium without detectable changes in whole-embryo intracellular content. NMDA co-treatment partially rescued incomplete closure at 0.125 and 0.25 µM BafA1 and neural tube opening across 0.125-0.5 µM BafA1, whereas ATP supplementation did not achieve the same effect. These findings are consistent with a contribution of V-ATPase-dependent processes to extracellular ATP and glutamate accumulation and timely neural tube closure, but vesicular loading and release were not measured directly.

articles.title: Anticholinergic prescribing in hospitalised older adults: an uncontrolled before-and-after study of clinician education.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anticholinergic medications are associated with medication-related harm in older adults. Hospitalisation provides an opportunity to review prescribing, but evidence about clinician education alone remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To compare anticholinergic prescribing among hospitalised older adults during periods before and after clinician education. METHODS: This exploratory, single-site, uncontrolled retrospective before-and-after study included unique patients aged ≥65 years admitted for ≥24 h with medications documented at admission and discharge. Patient-level data were obtained for two 3-month periods before and after education was delivered to doctors and pharmacists. Outcomes were admission-to-discharge changes in Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) score and number of anticholinergic medications. Linear regression estimated the adjusted mean between-period difference in discharge ACB. RESULTS: The study included 686 patients (368 pre-intervention; 318 post-intervention). Median ACB score decreased from admission to discharge in both periods (pre: 2 [IQR 1-4] to 1 [IQR 0-3], p = 0.002; post: 2 [IQR 1-3] to 1 [IQR 0-3], p = 0.004). The median number of anticholinergic medications remained 1 in both periods, although paired distributions shifted modestly downward (pre: p = 0.012; post: p = 0.005). The unadjusted mean difference in ACB change between periods was 0.025 points (bootstrap 95% CI -0.18 to 0.23); the Wilcoxon rank-sum p-value was 0.941. In the adjusted model, the post-intervention period was associated with a -0.064-point difference in discharge ACB (95% CI -0.265 to 0.137; p = 0.530). The between-period mean difference in anticholinergic-medication count change was -0.001 medications (bootstrap 95% CI -0.16 to 0.16); the Wilcoxon rank-sum p-value was 0.86. CONCLUSION: Prescribed ACB decreased modestly and anticholinergic-medication count distributions shifted downward from admission to discharge in both periods, without evidence of additional adjusted between-period improvement. The uncontrolled design and incomplete implementation information preclude conclusions about the education program's effectiveness. The findings can inform prospective evaluation of multimodal strategies.

articles.title: Characterisation of calcitonin receptor expression and signalling in iPSC-derived sensory neurons.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived sensory neurons (iPSC-SNs) provide an accessible and physiologically relevant model for studying neuropeptide systems implicated in migraine and chronic pain. The calcitonin peptide family, including calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), amylin, and their receptors, plays key roles in trigeminal and dorsal root ganglia (DRG) sensory neuron function. However, whether iPSC-SNs replicate the calcitonin family expression and signalling reported in trigeminal ganglia (TG) and DRG sensory neurons remains unknown. Therefore, we characterised the expression and function of the CGRP and amylin receptor system in human iPSC-SNs. METHODS: Human iPSCs were differentiated into sensory neurons, then assessed for gene and protein expression using RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence with validated antibodies. Receptor function was evaluated using ligand-evoked cAMP assays and compared with COS-7 cells expressing defined receptor constructs. RESULTS: iPSC-SNs upregulated peripheral and sensory neuron markers (TUBB3, PRPH, SCN10A, SCN11A, POU4F1, TRPV1, NTRK1, and ISL1) and formed extensive β-tubulin III-positive neurite networks. Compared with undifferentiated iPSCs, iPSC-SNs displayed increased gene expression of calcitonin receptor (CTR), calcitonin receptor-like receptor, and RAMP1, reduced RAMP2, and relatively low RAMP3. Immunofluorescence detected CGRP, amylin, and CTR protein, with amylin predominantly localised to neuronal Soma. Functionally, calcitonin produced robust cAMP responses, whereas CGRP, amylin, and adrenomedullin yielded weaker signalling. This potency hierarchy matched that of CTR-expressing COS-7 cells, indicating that iPSC-SNs chiefly signal via the CTR rather than CGRP or AMY1 receptor complexes. CONCLUSION: Human iPSC-SNs recapitulate sensory neuron-like co-expression of CTR, CGRP, and amylin and exhibit dominant CTR-mediated signalling. These findings support their utility as a model translational platform for dissecting neuropeptide-driven pain mechanisms and developing receptor-targeted therapeutics.

articles.title: Mammary and brain pharmacokinetics of licochalcone A after oral and intravenous administration: implications for breast cancer prevention and interception.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Licochalcone A (LicA), a prenylated chalcone from Glycyrrhiza inflata, shows promising anti-tumor activity in breast cancer models, but translation is limited by poor bioavailability and rapid systemic clearance. Oral delivery is the clinically favored route for long-term use of breast cancer prevention drugs in women at elevated risk of developing breast cancer. We report the first validated quantification of LicA in mammary tissue in a prevention context and the first characterization of brain distribution under intact blood-brain barrier (BBB) conditions for intercepting brain metastasis. METHODS: Formulations spanning aqueous (F07), lipid-based (L05), surfactant-rich (L13) and co-solvent (L022, L024) systems were selected by solubility screening and simulated gastrointestinal re-dispersibility. Eight independent pharmacokinetic studies were conducted across two species. Plasma, mammary, brain, and liver were quantified. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Subcutaneous L022 (80 mg/kg/day, 28 days) that suppressed tumor growth in mice, presented a trough plasma LicA of 68 ng/mL (IQR 35-105), below in vitro-effective thresholds. Oral L024 in mice was rapidly absorbed (Tmax 0.25-0.5 h, plasma Cmax 817 ng/mL) and achieved mammary (Cmax 1,093 ng/g), with tissue-to-plasma partitioning (Kp) > 1 by every metric at 100 mg/kg. Brain-to-plasma Kp remained 0.3-0.5 after oral dosing but exceeded 1 from 1 h after intravenous dosing, reaching 3.92 at 8 h, while brain Cmax rose from 378 to 9,925 ng/g. Dose-normalized plasma exposure was 37-fold lower after oral than intravenous administration and brain exposure fell almost proportionally, by 27.5-fold. We interpret this as indicating that limited oral brain exposure reflects pre-systemic loss rather than restricted BBB transfer, although transfer kinetics were not measured directly. In rats, F07 was constrained by low drug-loading, while L05 and L13 achieved higher loading and prolonged T1/2 but were only characterized in plasma. L13 was not tolerated intravenously in pre-study tolerability assessment, and L05 was not advanced on formulation-development grounds rather than on pharmacokinetic performance. L024 was tolerated by both routes and was the only formulation for which tissue distribution data. It was selected as the lead candidate for chronic evaluation on the basis of tissue distribution data and dual-route tolerability. L024s short half-life predicts a low once-daily steady-state trough, addressable by divided dosing.

articles.title: Hybridization between ivabradine and MEL55A results in compounds with improved potency on HCN channel isoforms.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: A new series of phenylalkylamines structurally related to zatebradine and ivabradine was designed and prepared with the aim to find compounds showing preference or selectivity for individual HCN channel isoforms. METHODS: The new compounds are characterized by a different degree of conformational freedom, and by the presence of stereogenic centers in the region connecting the basic nitrogen to the veratrol moieties. Their effects were evaluated on h-current mediated by homomeric mHCN1, mHCN2 and hHCN4 channels expressed in HEK 293 cells. Selected compounds were also assessed for effects on pacemaking activity in cardiomyocytes derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and in zebrafish embryos. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: All new compounds reduced h-current mediated by mHCN1, mHCN2 and hHCN4 channels. The most interesting compounds, derived from hybridization between MEL55A and ivabradine, were (R)-1c and (S)-1c. (R)-1c preferentially inhibited mHCN2/hHCN4 relative to mHCN1, whereas (S)-1c was a more potent but relatively non-selective blocker. Both compounds reduced pacemaking activity in hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and zebrafish embryos, demonstrating functional activity in both cellular and whole-organism models.

articles.title: Phenotype-dependent effects of 2-mercaptoethanol pretreatment on ABO antibody reactivity by automated column agglutination.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To quantify phenotype-dependent effects of 2-mercaptoethanol (2-Me) pretreatment on ABO antibody reactivity measured by automated column agglutination and assess consistency across healthy participants and hematological patients. METHODS: The study included 104 healthy participants and 92 hematological patients, yielding 258 participant-antibody pairs and 516 repeated measurements. Antibody titer score was the primary mixed-effects-model outcome. Dilution-step changes were analyzed using the prespecified local weak-positive endpoint and, as a sensitivity analysis, the conventional ≥1+ endpoint. Crossings of 1:16, 1:32, 1:64, and 1:128 thresholds were summarized by phenotype, and available patient diagnoses, recent exposures, and immunological measurements were characterized. RESULTS: The 2-Me effect differed by antibody phenotype (treatment × phenotype, P < 0.001) but not by population (treatment × population, P = 0.164). Adjusted score reductions were 20.59, 12.81, 7.28, and 7.56 points for A/anti-B, B/anti-A, O/anti-A, and O/anti-B, respectively. Under the local endpoint, at least a one-step reduction or post-2-Me non-reactivity occurred in 90.9%, 72.1%, 37.1%, and 46.8%, respectively; the corresponding ≥1+ sensitivity estimates were 89.4%, 66.2%, 37.1%, and 50.0%. At the 1:16 threshold, 39/54, 25/59, 1/62, and 2/62 initially eligible pairs crossed below the threshold, respectively. CONCLUSION: 2-Me-associated shifts in automated ABO antibody measurements were phenotype dependent and frequently crossed commonly used dilution values, especially for A/anti-B. These data quantify method-dependent changes rather than clinical benefit or analytical accuracy; laboratories should identify the pretreatment and endpoint method and should not transfer decision thresholds across methods without validation.

articles.title: Coix seed polysaccharides modulate gut microbiota and metabolite profiles to ameliorate adjuvant-induced arthritis in rats.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coix seed (Coix lacryma-jobi L.), a widely consumed medicinal and edible food in Asian countries, has attracted growing interest in functional food research. Among its bioactive constituents, coix seed polysaccharides (CSP) have emerged as promising candidates for managing chronic inflammatory disorders. This study aimed to preliminarily evaluate whether CSP could alleviate rheumatoid arthritis (RA) through modulating gut microbiota and their derived metabolites, moving beyond the conventional focus on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). METHODS: An experimental RA model was established in rats using complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA), and the therapeutic potential of CSP was screened through serum inflammatory factor analysis, histopathological evaluation, shotgun metagenomic sequencing-based gut microbiota profiling, and untargeted serum metabolomics. RESULTS: CSP treatment significantly reduced paw swelling and ameliorated synovial injury in CFA-induced rats. Untargeted metabolomics revealed that CSP restored perturbed levels of α-linolenic acid and other host-microbial co-metabolites, while partially reconstituting the disrupted gut microbiota, notably increasing Lactobacillus intestinalis abundance. Correlation analyses linked these alterations to decreased inflammatory factors. KEGG functional prediction suggested a possible involvement of MAPK signaling. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that CSP exerts anti-RA effects in association with systematic modulation of gut microbiota and host metabolism, highlighting the potential of dietary polysaccharides from medicinal food sources as broad-spectrum metabolic regulators for managing chronic inflammatory diseases.

articles.title: Ferulic acid attenuates hepatic steatosis and modulates PTGS2, PPARG, and FADS2 expression: an integrated network pharmacology, molecular dynamics, and experimental study.
articles.abstract: Ferulic acid (FA), a principal phenolic constituent of Angelica sinensis, attenuates hepatic steatosis in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Here, we employed an integrated approach combining network pharmacology, transcriptomics, molecular dynamics (MD), single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) pseudobulk analysis, and in vitro validation in a PA/OA-induced HepG2 model. External validation revealed consistent upregulation of FADS2 across cohorts, whereas PTGS2 exhibited cohort-dependent directionality. Single-cell pseudobulk analysis suggested a hepatocyte-intrinsic trend for FADS2 and PPARG, although donor-level significance was not reached (p = 0.29 and p = 0.10, respectively). Molecular docking predicted favorable binding of FA to FADS2 (-8.539 kcal/mol), PTGS2 (-7.146 kcal/mol), and PPARG (-5.882 kcal/mol). In vitro, FA dose-dependently reduced lipid accumulation (Oil Red O and TC/TG) without cytotoxicity (confirmed by CCK-8). qPCR revealed that FA suppressed lipogenic genes (SREBP-1c, FASN, ACC1) and the desaturase SCD, while restoring the expression of the fatty acid oxidation marker CPT1A and the hepatocyte-intrinsic desaturase FADS2. Western blot confirmed FA suppressed PTGS2 and PPARG protein expression. The coordinated suppression of lipogenesis and restoration of FADS2 expression is consistent with a 'lipid remodeling' hypothesis-FA may shift lipid flux toward less toxic, highly desaturated species-which warrants dedicated mechanistic validation. We identify FADS2 as a novel transcriptional signature of FA, with PTGS2 and PPARG as supported candidate targets.

articles.title: Intranasal deferiprone delivery increases brain exposure and ameliorates abnormal open-field behavior in a mouse model of brain iron dysregulation.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Although brain iron dysregulation has been implicated in neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders, its potential as a therapeutic target remains unclear. Deferiprone (DFP), an oral lipophilic iron chelator approved for systemic iron overload, has been explored for central nervous system (CNS) disorders, but its use has been limited by systemic toxicity and suboptimal brain distribution. In this study, we evaluated intranasal (IN) delivery of DFP as an alternative strategy to modulate impaired neurobehavior in a mouse model of brain iron accumulation. METHODS: Wild-type and H67D mice (male, n = 6-10 per group) received IN or oral DFP daily for 7 days, followed by open field testing and hematological assessment. To determine whether the behavioral effects and hematological tolerability of IN administration were associated with route-dependent exposure, we evaluated pharmacokinetics and compared tissue distribution of DFP following IN and oral administration. RESULTS: In contrast to high-dose oral treatment, IN administration of DFP produced behavioral effects at 20 mg/kg without detectable hematological changes, whereas high-dose oral DFP (100 mg/kg) reduced circulating leukocyte and neutrophil counts without producing comparable behavioral effects. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed increased drug distribution in the olfactory bulb and distinct brain-to-plasma distribution patterns after IN administration relative to oral dosing. CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings demonstrate that intranasal delivery alters regional CNS exposure to DFP and improves open-field behavior associated with brain iron dysregulation.

articles.title: An integrated computational and experimental framework identifies apigenin as a potential therapeutic agent targeting EGFR/STAT3/MMP9 signaling in glioma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glioma is the most common primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system and is characterized by aggressive progression, high recurrence rates, and limited therapeutic options. Apigenin, a naturally occurring flavonoid, exhibits promising anti-tumor properties; however, its molecular mechanisms in glioma remain insufficiently understood. To systematically identify the therapeutic targets and molecular mechanisms underlying apigenin-mediated anti-glioma activity through an integrated computational and experimental approach. METHODS: An integrated bioinformatics framework combining network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, and machine learning algorithms was applied to identify potential therapeutic targets of apigenin in glioma. Differentially expressed genes were screened using TCGA and GTEx datasets, and prognostic genes were identified through LASSO Cox regression, ElasticNet, and stepwise Cox regression analyses, followed by construction and validation of a multigene prognostic model. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), over-representation analysis (ORA), and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were performed to explore functional mechanisms. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET prediction were conducted to evaluate the interaction stability and drug-like properties of apigenin with candidate targets. Furthermore, the predicted regulatory axis was examined in LN229 and U87 glioma cell models through cell viability assays, colony formation assays, and Western blotting. RESULTS: Six prognostic genes, including EGFR, MMP9, HIF1A, STAT3, RELA, and CASP3, were identified and used to construct a prognostic model with robust predictive performance. The model achieved favorable discrimination, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUC values of 0.840, 0.876, and 0.817, respectively, and a cross-validated C-index of 0.78. Functional enrichment analyses indicated that these genes were primarily associated with cancer-related signaling pathways. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted potential stable interactions between apigenin and key targets, particularly EGFR and STAT3. Cellular experiments showed reduced glioma cell viability following apigenin treatment and reduced colony formation after EGFR or MMP9 knockdown, accompanied by suppression of the EGFR/STAT3 signaling pathway and downstream MMP9 expression. CONCLUSION: This study established an integrated computational and experimental framework to investigate potential mechanisms associated with the anti-glioma activity of apigenin. Our findings suggest that apigenin-associated growth inhibition in glioma cells involves changes in EGFR/STAT3 signaling and MMP9 expression, providing new insights into its therapeutic potential and supporting further pre-clinical investigation of apigenin as a potential candidate for glioma treatment based on computational and in vitro cellular evidence.

articles.title: A hierarchical gating hypothesis for GABA-Mediated gut-liver communication: a mechanistic framework.
articles.abstract: γ  -Aminobutyric acid (GABA) can produce divergent outcomes in colitis and liver injury, but the conditions linking exposure to organ responses remain unresolved. We propose a hierarchical gating hypothesis in which compartment-specific GABA exposure is an upstream prerequisite. JAK3-associated immune status and CDK2-associated proliferative status are proposed as parallel effect modifiers, not a fixed linear signaling cascade. Their possible roles as direct intracellular GABA targets represent a separate, unverified mechanistic extension. GABA-producing probiotic strains are considered potential delivery systems that may modify local exposure, while other metabolites and microbiome changes may also contribute to their effects. Exploratory evidence comprises DiffDock-generated poses, 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations of five candidate complexes, and biolayer interferometry (BLI) measurements at GABA concentrations of 25-200 μ M  . The simulations describe conformational behavior but do not establish a ranking of binding affinities. BLI responses increased with GABA concentration and declined during dissociation. The reported fits yielded provisional apparent dissociation constants of 54.6 and 64.1 μ M  for JAK3 and CDK2, respectively. Binding specificity and parameter uncertainty remain unresolved, and these observations do not establish intracellular engagement, kinase regulation, or efficacy in liver disease. We outline disease-specific tests combining exposure measurements, state-dependent response analysis, and independent evaluation of direct target engagement. Discriminating experiments must separate kinase-specific interactions from classical GABA receptor signaling, hepatic GABA production, and microbial cometabolite effects. The framework organizes testable predictions rather than establishing a validated therapeutic mechanism.

articles.title: HSA-Based Delivery of Bivalirudin via Multivalent Modification: A Bifunctional Strategy for Enhanced Antithrombotic Efficacy and Thrombus-Targeting Specificity.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Bivalirudin (BVLD) is a direct thrombin inhibitor that represents a promising alternative to heparin for antithrombotic therapy. However, its clinical utility is limited by a short plasma half-life and bleeding risks associated with systemic administration. Methods: We co-conjugated BVLD and the thrombus-targeting pentapeptide CREKA (Cys-Arg-Glu-Lys-Ala) to human serum albumin (HSA) to synthesize the BVLD/CREKA-HSA conjugate (BC-HSA), aiming to enhance BVLD's pharmacokinetic profile and thrombus-targeting capacity. Results: BC-HSA with an optimized molar ratio of BVLD and CREKA exhibited good colloidal stability and minimal aggregation. In vitro assays confirmed that BC-HSA retains thrombin-inhibitory activity following specific binding to fibrin clots. Pharmacokinetic studies in mice demonstrated a 4.7-fold prolongation of plasma half-life for BC-HSA compared with free BVLD, while APTT and TT assays further confirmed a corresponding extension of anticoagulant activity. Furthermore, in both non-lethal and lethal pulmonary thrombosis models, BC-HSA exerted more sustained antithrombotic effects than BVLD and specifically accumulated within pulmonary microthrombi. Compared with the scrambled-peptide control, CREKA modification showed a trend toward prolonged restricted mean survival time (approximately 17% increase), although this difference did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions: We engineered an HSA-based bifunctional conjugate integrating prolonged antithrombotic activity and thrombus-targeting capacity. Our findings demonstrate that multivalently modified HSA serves as a robust carrier platform for peptide anticoagulants, offering a versatile strategy for the optimization of similar therapeutic agents.

articles.title: Evaluating the Generalizability of Machine Learning Models for Lipid Nanoparticle Physicochemical Properties.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable nucleic acid delivery, but formulation development remains empirical. Methods: We curated 1092 LNP formulations from 63 studies (2005-2025) and trained LightGBM models to predict particle size, encapsulation efficiency (EE%), and polydispersity index (PDI) using ionizable-lipid descriptors and formulation molar fractions. Results: Across random 80/20 splits (10 seeds), R2 values were 0.42 ± 0.06 for size (n = 850), 0.40 ± 0.16 for EE% (n = 523), and 0.43 ± 0.07 for PDI (n = 602), outperforming linear regression (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.002, 0.020, and 0.002). Combining structural and compositional features outperformed either subset. Lipid-identity holdout reduced R2 to 0.10 ± 0.38, 0.01 ± 0.28, and -0.39 ± 0.48 (exact SMILES) and to 0.10 ± 0.27, -0.19 ± 0.55, and -0.32 ± 0.41 (full InChIKey) for particle size, EE%, and PDI, respectively. Repeated scaffold-grouped cross-validation yielded R2 values of -0.16 ± 0.46, -0.27 ± 0.42, and -0.43 ± 1.04; paper-level holdout yielded -0.45 ± 0.31, -1.29 ± 1.74, and -0.86 ± 1.18. SHAP highlighted polar surface area, PEG-lipid fraction, and rotatable bonds. Conclusions: These findings support cautious interpolation within represented lipid chemistries but indicate poor transfer to unseen lipids, scaffolds, and studies.

articles.title: Lavandula stoechas Ethanol Extracts Reduce Cancer Cell Migration and Invasion.
articles.abstract: Background:Lavandula stoechas has been reported to exhibit anticancer activity; however, its effects on cancer cell wound closure and invasion remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the effects of ethanolic extracts obtained from dried (LsDE) and fresh (LsFE) L. stoechas on wound closure, Matrigel invasion, and MMP2 and MMP9 expression in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer, RT4 bladder cancer, and T98G glioblastoma cells. Methods: Cells were treated for 48 h with LsDE or LsFE at their 48-h IC50 concentrations. Wound closure and invasive capacity were evaluated using scratch wound-healing and Matrigel-coated Transwell assays, respectively. MMP2 and MMP9 mRNA and protein expression levels were analyzed by qRT-PCR and Western blotting, respectively. Results: Both extracts significantly reduced wound closure and Matrigel invasion in all three cell lines. Reductions in wound closure were observed at 48 h in MDA-MB-231 and T98G cells and at both 24 and 48 h in RT4 cells. Matrigel invasion was significantly reduced relative to the corresponding dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) vehicle controls in all three cell lines. MMP responses varied according to cell line and extract. LsFE reduced MMP2 mRNA expression in RT4 cells and MMP9 mRNA expression in T98G cells, whereas LsDE reduced MMP9 mRNA expression in RT4 cells. At the protein level, LsDE reduced MMP2 expression in RT4 and T98G cells and MMP9 expression in all three cell lines, while LsFE reduced MMP9 protein expression in T98G cells. Conclusions: Ethanolic extracts of fresh and dried L. stoechas reduced wound closure and Matrigel invasion in three cancer cell models and were associated with distinct changes in MMP2 and MMP9 expression. These findings indicate that the reductions in wound closure and Matrigel invasion were accompanied by cell line- and extract-dependent changes in MMP2 and MMP9 expression, although the functional contribution of these changes remains to be established.

articles.title: Macrophage-Targeted Spermine Nanodelivery Attenuates AECOPD-Associated Lung Inflammation Associated with ZFP36 Upregulation and Reduced Inflammasome-Related Signaling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), frequently triggered by Streptococcus pneumoniae, are major contributors to disease progression and mortality. Although the polyamine spermine exhibits anti-inflammatory properties, its mechanistic role in AECOPD and the limitations imposed by impaired cellular transport remain poorly defined. METHODS: We established in vivo AECOPD mouse models and in vitro alveolar macrophage systems. Integrated metabolomics and proteomics analyses were performed to identify key regulatory pathways. Molecular experiments, including ZFP36 knockdown and pyroptosis-associated protein analyses, were performed to investigate the role of ZFP36 in spermine-mediated inflammatory regulation. To overcome impaired transporter-dependent uptake, a macrophage-targeted nanodelivery system (MSNs/HA-Man) was engineered, and its therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in vivo. RESULTS: Spermine levels were significantly reduced in COPD and AECOPD. Mechanistically, spermine treatment was associated with increased ZFP36 expression and reduced activation of the NLRP3/Caspase-1/IL-1β pyroptosis pathway. Importantly, metabolomic pathway enrichment suggested that SLC-mediated transport may be altered under pathological conditions, raising the possibility that cellular uptake of spermine could be affected. The enhanced therapeutic efficacy of the engineered MSNs/HA-Man nanocarrier may be partly attributable to CD44/CD206-mediated endocytosis, which could reduce dependence on transporter-mediated uptake and improve intracellular delivery compared with free spermine. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that the spermine-ZFP36 axis may represent an important regulatory pathway associated with inflammation in AECOPD. Moreover, macrophage-targeted nanodelivery may improve intracellular delivery efficiency and therapeutic efficacy. This study provides a novel framework integrating metabolic modulation with proof-of-concept nanomedicine strategy for the treatment of COPD exacerbations.

articles.title: Same Carrier, Different Outcomes: Molecular Identity Shapes the Physicochemical and Biological Performance of Curcumin- and Resveratrol-Loaded PCL Nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The molecular identity of encapsulated bioactive compounds may influence nanoparticle performance even when the same polymeric carrier is used. This study compared the physicochemical properties and biological responses of curcumin (CUR)- and resveratrol (RSV)-loaded poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) nanoparticles. Methods: Nanoparticles were prepared via nanoprecipitation using different stabilizer systems and characterized in terms of particle size, polydispersity, zeta potential, encapsulation efficiency, drug loading, thermal behavior, and in vitro release. Antibacterial activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, fibroblast metabolic activity, and zebrafish embryo survival were also evaluated. Results: Drug-loaded nanoparticles exhibited hydrodynamic diameters of approximately 219-285 nm. CUR formulations showed higher encapsulation efficiencies (92.78-96.46%) and drug loading (4.56-4.82%) than RSV formulations (74.52-78.83% and 3.73-3.94%, respectively). After 96 h, cumulative release reached approximately 86% for CUR and 65% for RSV. RSV-loaded nanoparticles exhibited greater antibacterial growth inhibition under the evaluated conditions. Free CUR and RSV showed concentration-dependent inhibition of fibroblast metabolic activity, whereas both nanoparticle formulations maintained relative metabolic activity above approximately 65% across the tested concentrations. In zebrafish embryos, survival remained at least 93.3% at 96 h post-fertilization, without statistically significant concentration-dependent effects in mixed-effects analyses. Conclusions: Molecular identity influenced drug incorporation, release behavior, and biological responses within the same PCL carrier system. These findings underscore the importance of evaluating individual drug-carrier combinations and support further investigation of their therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Development and Characterization of Isomalt-Based Medicated Lollipops Manufactured by Compression and Molding.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medicated lollipops are not yet widely established, although they offer several advantages. They may benefit pediatric patients and those with swallowing difficulties, while providing an alternative to conventional solid dosage forms. Isomalt is suitable for medicated lollipops due to its advantageous properties, including non-cariogenicity and thermal stability. This study aimed to prepare lidocaine hydrochloride-containing lollipops by molding and direct compression (DC) and to develop novel analytical methods for characterization. Methods: Molded lollipops contained isomalt and the active pharmaceutical ingredient, whereas sodium stearyl fumarate (PRUV) was used as a lubricant in DC lollipops. Mass, geometry, disintegration time, and solid state were investigated. Drug content uniformity and drug release were assessed, with the latter compared with changes in mass and surface area. Taste profiles were characterized using electronic tongue. Results: Both technologies produced medicated lollipops with different solid-state characteristics: crystalline isomalt in directly compressed and predominantly amorphous isomalt in molded lollipops. This difference was associated with disintegration properties. All formulations released more than 90% of the drug within 15 min. Electronic tongue analysis differentiated the formulations by their sensor-response patterns, but the effects of composition and manufacturing technology could not be separated. LDA achieved 100% recognition and prediction accuracy in the present dataset. Conclusions: Isomalt was suitable for preparing medicated lollipops using both technologies, providing appropriate drug content uniformity and rapid drug release in freshly prepared formulations. Electronic tongue analysis may complement formulation characterization by identifying formulation-dependent differences in sensor-response patterns, supporting the objective comparison of innovative oral dosage forms.

articles.title: Rapid Strategies for an In-Depth Stability Study of Capecitabine Using Chemometric Resolution of UV Data and Complementary HPLC-DAD Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Capecitabine (CAP) is an oral fluoropyrimidine prodrug widely used for the treatment of several solid tumors, including colorectal and breast cancers. Despite its widespread clinical use, comprehensive data on its stability under forced degradation conditions remains limited. This study aimed to systematically investigate the capecitabine in solution under different stress conditions. Methods: CAP solutions were subjected to thermal, light, and pH-induced stress conditions in accordance with ICH Q1A(R2) and ICH Q1B guidelines. UV absorption spectra were recorded at predefined time intervals (for a total time of 6 h) under different temperatures (40-80 °C), pH (2-12), and light (radiant power in the range of 350-650 W/m2). Degradation kinetics were calculated by applying the Multivariate Curve Resolution (MCR) method to the spectral data. Results: CAP degradation followed first-order kinetics, with degradation profiles varying depending on the experimental stressing conditions. A titration experiment demonstrated the existence of dissociated and non-dissociated forms, the prevalence of which varied with pH. Multivariate analysis showed the formation of a single degradation product under almost all the tested conditions, while two products were detected after exposure to high irradiation power and acid pH. As a complementary analytical procedure, HPLC analysis was used to confirm the formation of two major by-products tentatively assigned to 5'-deoxy-5-fluorocytidine and 5-fluorouracil based on spectral matching with the literature data. Conclusions: The chemometric method combined with UV spectrophotometry represents an effective and reliable strategy for investigating the degradation kinetics and transformation pathways of CAP with a very low relative error percentage under abiotic stress providing valuable baseline data on drug stability and breakdown products.

articles.title: pH-Responsive Alginate-Chitosan Microparticles Incorporating Tenebrio molitor-Derived Chitosan for Gastrointestinal Delivery of Antimicrobial Peptides.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Probiotic-derived peptides are promising multifunctional metabolites with significant potential for disease prevention and treatment. However, their effectiveness is hindered by their susceptibility to gastrointestinal degradation. This study aimed to develop sustainable alginate-chitosan microparticles for oral peptide delivery, using chitosan extracted from Tenebrio molitor residues. Methods: Peptides isolated from Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis ATCC 11454 and Bacillus subtilis subsp. subtilis NCIB 3610 were loaded into the microparticles via the external ionic gelation method. The microparticles were characterized for morphology, size, encapsulation efficiency, Fourier-Transform Infrared (FT-IR) profile, swelling, and pH-dependent release under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. Results: Microparticles had a particle size of approximately 511-576 μm, and encapsulation efficiencies of 74.8-83.3%, comparable to commercial chitosan formulations. FT-IR analysis supported efficient peptide incorporation into the polymer matrix. The formulations exhibited pH-dependent swelling and release, with minimal release at gastric pH 1.2 and substantially greater release at intestinal pH (6.8 and 7.4). Following INFOGEST simulated gastrointestinal digestion, encapsulated peptides retained antimicrobial activity against Enterococcus faecalis and Escherichia coli, while free peptides showed significantly reduced activity (p < 0.05). Empty microparticles maintained Caco-2 cell viability above 90% across the tested concentration range, indicating cytocompatibility, whereas peptide-loaded formulations exhibited dose-dependent cytotoxicity. Conclusions: Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of alginate-chitosan microparticles containing T. molitor-derived chitosan as a sustainable, pH-responsive platform for protecting antimicrobial peptides during gastrointestinal transit and facilitating intestinal delivery.

articles.title: Formulation Strategies to Optimize the In Vitro Release of Fenbendazole from Immediate-Release Tablets Containing Amorphous Hydroxypropyl-β-Cyclodextrin Inclusion Complexes.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The aim of this study is to obtain new inclusion complexes of fenbendazole (FEN) with hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD) in order to optimize the in vitro release profile of fenbendazole from immediate-release tablets. Methods: Inclusion complexes and solid dispersions were prepared by coprecipitation, lyophilization, and kneading at 1:0.25 and 1:0.5 (FEN:HP-β-CD) sub-stoichiometric molar ratios. Physical mixtures were prepared for comparison. Both physical mixtures and inclusion complexes were subsequently evaluated using physicochemical and pharmacotehnical methods. Results: Physicochemical analysis (FTIR, XRD, and TG/DTA) showed that lyophilization successfully induced solid-state amorphization of the drug at both ratios. Directly compressed tablets exhibited excellent mechanical properties, with crushing strength ranging from 65.1 ± 2.4 N (F3) to 87.4 ± 2.9 N (F2) and 98.2 ± 3.5 N (F1), friability below 0.7%, and rapid disintegration (58 ± 3.2 s for F1, 69 ± 4.1 s for F2, and 77 ± 4.5 s for F3). In vitro dissolution was strongly medium-dependent: at pH 1.2, cyclodextrin-based tablets achieved near-complete dissolution within 60 min (Q60 = 96.8 ± 2.1, DE% = 81.8 ± 1.9% for F1; Q60 = 99.5 ± 1.8%, DE% = 71.4 ± 2.3% for F2), compared with the uncomplexed drug (Q60 = 63.3 ± 2.4%, DE% = 47.5 ± 1.7% for F3). At pH 4.5 and 6.8, drug release plateaued below 15% and 38%, respectively, due to non-sink saturation constraints. Conclusions: This study provides in vitro proof of concept that sub-stoichiometric amorphization with HP-β-CD, coupled with direct compression, overcomes the gastric dissolution barrier of fenbendazole, establishing a solid biopharmaceutical basis for future in vivo bioavailability and stability evaluations.

articles.title: A Self-Reinforcing Cu-Based Dual-Network Composite Hydrogel for Effective Bleeding Wound Management.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Extensive skin trauma caused by accidental injury, burns, or surgery presents a clinical challenge due to uncontrolled hemorrhage, high bacterial infection risk, and poor wound healing. It is imperative to develop a multifunctional dressing that integrates robust tissue adhesion, rapid hemostasis, conformability to irregular wounds, and the ability to lessen antibiotic dependence and accelerate wound healing to treat such wounds. Methods: A composite hydrogel (designated IGCu@HA/Gel) was successfully engineered by sequential assembly of gelatin (Gel), hydrazide-modified hyaluronic acid (Tph-HA), glucose oxidase (GOx), indocyanine green (ICG), and Cu2+ via covalent and physical dual cross-linking to meet these critical requirements of traumatic skin wound care. Results: IGCu@HA/Gel not only exhibited robust tissue adhesion by interfacial interactions between the hydrogel and tissue surface, but also achieved rapid hemostasis (within 22 s and 127 s for mouse tail amputation and liver injury model, respectively) by self-expansion and electrostatic aggregation/adhesion of blood cells along with fibrin formation to occlude vascular defects. Under near-infrared light irradiation, the combination of Cu2+, ICG and GOx enabled IGCu@HA/Gel to be an all-in-one antibacterial platform for achieving synergistic photothermal, photodynamic, chemodynamic and starvation therapy, as well as cuproptosis-like cell death along with GSH depletion and O2 supply to effectively eradicate bacteria and mature biofilms. The phototherapeutic IGCu@HA/Gel also exhibited excellent cytocompatibility. Notably, IGCu@HA/Gel alleviated inflammation by effective bacteria/biofilm elimination, promoted angiogenesis and collagen deposition, and regulated the wound microenvironment to accelerate wound tissue remodeling. Conclusions: Collectively, these findings confirmed its promising potential for treating traumatic bleeding wounds.

articles.title: Mixture-Design Optimization of an Intranasal Self-Nanoemulsifying Drug Delivery System Co-Loaded with Olmesartan Medoxomil and Apigenin: Composition Modeling and Ex Vivo Nasal Permeation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ischemic brain injury involves parallel oxidative, inflammatory, and vascular cascades. Olmesartan medoxomil and apigenin act on complementary arms and can serve this purpose. This study developed a self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery system (SNEDDS) co-loaded with both agents for intranasal use. Constrained mixture design was used to determine its actual composition. Methods: Oil and cosolvent were selected by saturation solubility and surfactant by emulsification transmittance. The proportions of Kolliphor EL (40-70% w/w), poly(ethylene glycol) 400 (5-30% w/w), and Imwitor 308 (20-40% w/w) were treated as mixture variables and each drug's solubility as the response. Desirability analysis identified the optimum composition, which was experimentally verified. After that, it was compared with a drug suspension for permeation across excised goat nasal mucosa in Franz diffusion cells. Results: Apigenin solubility followed a linear mixture model and olmesartan medoxomil a quadratic model. The optimum composition (52.33% Kolliphor EL, 27.67% poly(ethylene glycol) 400, 20.00% Imwitor 308) gave observed solubilities of 11.82 and 6.91 mg/g, within the 95% prediction intervals. Steady-state flux rose from 0.85 ± 0.68 to 8.46 ± 2.51 µg/cm2/h for olmesartan medoxomil and from 0.18 ± 0.17 to 10.06 ± 3.63 µg/cm2/h for apigenin. Conclusions: A constrained mixture design identified a SNEDDS composition that accommodated both drugs and markedly increased their transport across excised nasal mucosa relative to a suspension. These findings establish a formulation basis for the intranasal administration of this drug combination.

articles.title: Autoclavation of Aqueous Stannum metallicum 30x Modifies Its Effects in a Cress Seedling-CuCl2 Crystallisation Bioassay.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The widespread use of autoclavation as the preferred terminal sterilisation method for sterile homeopathic preparations, including ophthalmic and parenteral dosage forms, raises the question of whether this standard manufacturing step affects their biological activity. For ultramolecular homeopathic preparations, this question cannot be addressed by conventional physicochemical stability testing, since no original substance remains in measurable quantities. We investigated whether autoclavation of Stannum metallicum 30x affected its response in a previously validated Lepidium sativum CuCl2 crystallisation bioassay with four independent outcome parameters. Methods: The present autoclavation study was conducted within the same experimental series as a parallel microwave irradiation study, providing a well-controlled basis for comparing the effects of two distinct physical treatments on the same preparation. Experiments were performed in parallel at two independent laboratories, and experimental stability was monitored throughout with systematic negative control (SNC) experiments. Results: Autoclavation partially nullified and partially modified the preparation's effects in the bioassay. The significant main treatment effects observed in the untreated condition for two outcome parameters were absent following autoclavation. By contrast, time-modulated day × treatment interactions were preserved in the remaining two parameters, and in one case strengthened. A correlation analysis revealed that the day-to-day pattern of the preserved effects was entirely decoupled from the untreated condition, indicating that autoclavation produced a qualitatively different temporal response pattern rather than preserving the original one. SNC experiments were stable throughout, confirming experimental reliability and the specificity of the observed effects. Conclusions: These findings contrast with those of the companion microwave study, in which all four outcome parameters were nullified, which seems attributable to non-thermal electromagnetic influences given the negligible thermal heating of the samples (ΔT ≈ 0.091 K). The qualitatively different outcome observed here suggests that thermal and electromagnetic stressors interact with potentised homeopathic preparations through distinct mechanisms. These findings cannot be extrapolated to other preparations or biological systems but warrant further investigation into the influence of standard manufacturing processes on the bioassay response of potentised homeopathic preparations.

articles.title: Niflumic Acid-Loaded Aspasomes as a Repurposed Nanoplatform: Antitumor Effects and Modulation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR Pathway-Related Molecular Markers in Solid Ehrlich Carcinoma-Bearing Mice.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Breast cancer remains a major global health challenge, with the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling axis playing a key role in tumor progression. Drug repurposing offers an efficient approach to cancer therapeutics. Niflumic acid (NIF), a selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitor, has demonstrated antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects against breast cancer cells; however, its therapeutic potential is limited by its poor solubility. This study aimed to develop, optimize, and evaluate NIF-loaded aspasomes (NIF-ASPs) against solid Ehrlich carcinoma (SEC). Methods: NIF-ASPs were optimized via a 21.41 full factorial design. The optimum (A2) formulation was evaluated for entrapment efficiency (EE%), vesicle size (VS), polydispersity index (PDI), zeta potential (ZP), and ex vivo permeation, using the skin as a model lipoidal barrier. Following intraperitoneal administration, the antitumor efficacy and associated changes in PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling components were evaluated in SEC-bearing mice through RT-qPCR gene expression, biochemical assays, immunohistochemistry, and histopathology. Results: The optimal A2 formula exhibited an EE% of 94.83 ± 0.16%, VS of 205.55 ± 2.05 nm, PDI of 0.49 ± 0.00, ZP of -23.65 ± 0.35 mV, and about a 2.59-fold increase in skin permeation flux versus free NIF suspension. In vivo, A2 was associated with a tumor inhibition rate of 63% (NIF suspension, 51.56%). Molecular and biochemical investigations demonstrated that A2 treatment was accompanied by significant alterations in PI3K/AKT/mTOR-associated molecular markers, characterized by decreased PI3K and p-AKT levels, together with downregulation of AKT and mTOR expression. Additionally, A2 treatment resulted in significant reductions in BCL-2, p-BAD, COX-2, and MDA levels, accompanied by restoration of total antioxidant capacity and a marked increase in cleaved caspase-3 immunoreactivity. Conclusions: NIF-ASPs serve as an efficient delivery platform that significantly enhances the NIF ex vivo skin permeation and are associated with reduced tumor growth accompanied by alterations in the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway-related molecular markers, COX-2-related inflammation, and oxidative stress.

articles.title: Construction and Biological Evaluation of [177Lu]Lu-Labeled RGD/FA Dual-Targeted Lipid Nanoparticles for Tumor Imaging and Potential Theranostic Applications.
articles.abstract: Background: The development of precision tumor theranostics necessitates a delivery platform that integrates favorable biocompatibility, effective tumor targeting, and imageable traceability. Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are distinguished by their favorable biocompatibility, versatile modifiability, and robust drug delivery capacity. The incorporation of multiple tumor-targeting ligands is a promising strategy to enhance the specific accumulation of nanomedicines in tumor tissues. Arginine-glycine-aspartic acid (RGD) peptides specifically recognize integrin αvβ3, while folic acid (FA) targets the folate receptor (FR), both of which are overexpressed on various tumor cells and tumor neovasculature. In this study, we developed 177Lu-labeled RGD/FA dual-targeted LNPs and systematically evaluated their physicochemical properties, radiolabeling performance, and tumor-targeting characteristics. Methods: LNPs were fabricated via the thin-film hydration method, with RGD and FA ligands conjugated to the nanoparticle surface. The macrocyclic chelator 1,4,7,10-tetraazacyclododecane-1,4,7,10-tetraacetic acid (DOTA) was incorporated to enable subsequent radiolabeling with 177Lu through a post-labeling strategy.
