The resulting nanoparticles were characterized for particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), zeta potential, morphology, and colloidal stability. Radiolabeling yield, radiochemical purity, and labeling stability were determined by instant thin-layer chromatography (ITLC). Cellular uptake of 177Lu-labeled dual-targeted LNPs was assessed using 4T1 murine breast carcinoma cells, and receptor-mediated targeting specificity was evaluated via blocking assays using free RGD, free FA, or a combination of both. In vivo tumor targeting and biodistribution were further investigated by micro-single-photon emission computed tomography (microSPECT/CT) imaging and ex vivo tissue distribution studies in 4T1 tumor-bearing mice. Results: The as-prepared RGD/FA dual-targeted LNPs exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 100 nm, with narrow size distribution and satisfactory colloidal stability. After 177Lu labeling, the radiolabeling yield reached 90%, and the radiochemical purity exceeded 96% following purification, with favorable radiostability over time. In vitro cellular uptake studies demonstrated that the 177Lu-labeled dual-targeted LNPs achieved the highest uptake of up to 25% AD/105 cells (AD%: percentage absorbed dose). Upon blocking with RGD or FA alone, cellular uptake was partially reduced; notably, combined blockade of both RGD- and FA-mediated pathways resulted in a maximum reduction of approximately 80% compared with the non-blocked group, consistent with the cellular internalization of the dual-targeted LNPs being predominantly mediated by receptor-specific interactions. Cytotoxicity evaluation via the Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay revealed that unlabeled LNPs did not induce significant cytotoxicity, with cell viability maintained at 90% ± 3.50% after 12 h of incubation with 4T1 cells. In vivo microSPECT/CT imaging revealed pronounced radioactive accumulation of 177Lu-labeled RGD/FA dual-targeted LNPs at the tumor site, concomitant with moderate uptake in the liver and spleen. Quantitative biodistribution analysis showed a time-dependent increase in tumor uptake, reaching 12.22% ± 1.22% injected dose per gram of tissue (%ID/g) at 12 h post-injection. The tumor-to-blood ratio (T/B) and tumor-to-muscle ratio (T/M) at 12 h were determined to be 2.69 and 4.35, respectively. Conclusions: Collectively, this study successfully constructed 177Lu-labeled RGD/FA dual-targeted LNPs with favorable physicochemical properties and radiolabeling characteristics. In vitro assays confirmed the potent cellular uptake capacity of the dual-targeted platform, and the significant reduction in uptake upon combined receptor blockade substantiated the specificity conferred by RGD/FA dual targeting. In vivo SPECT imaging and biodistribution data further corroborated its favorable tumor-homing ability. These findings indicate that 177Lu-labeled RGD/FA dual-targeted LNPs hold considerable promise as a tumor-targeted radioactive imaging-guided theranostic platform with potential for future therapy, providing a solid experimental foundation for further investigations toward integrated tumor theranostics.

articles.title: Development of an Electrospun Nanofibrous Wound Dressing Combining Arginine and Chlorhexidine for Targeted Management of Partial-Thickness Burns.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Partial-thickness burns require prompt infection control without compromising the cells that drive tissue repair. We report a fully electrospun bilayer dressing that assigns chlorhexidine digluconate (CHX) and L-arginine hydrochloride (ARG) to two separately formulated nanofibrous layers according to their different exposure requirements. Methods: CHX was incorporated into a rapidly dissolving poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)-chitosan wound-contact layer and ARG into a more water-resistant PVA-silica hybrid layer obtained by sol-gel electrospinning of a tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS)-derived sol. Fibers were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray powder diffraction (XRPD); release profiles were fitted with the Weibull model. Antibacterial activity was screened against four reference strains and nine clinical isolates, including multidrug-resistant strains; cytocompatibility was evaluated in 3T3 fibroblasts with the use of formulation-specific exposure protocols, and wound-healing potential with the use of an in vitro scratch assay. Results: Drug loading preserved continuous nanofibrous morphology and XRPD showed no detectable crystalline drug fraction. CHX release was immediate, reaching 98.04 ± 0.41% within 5 min (t90 = 2.25 min), whereas ARG release was gradual, reaching 94.08 ± 2.14% at 120 min (t90 = 71.4 min). Full- and half-dose CHX fibers inhibited every strain tested, whereas ARG-containing and drug-free formulations showed no detectable antibacterial activity. The ARG-loaded layer maintained fibroblast viability comparable to the untreated control after 72 h of continuous exposure, while the CHX-loaded layer was well tolerated after single and repeated 5 min exposures. The ARG-loaded layer also increased fibroblast migration in the scratch assay. Conclusions: Spatial and temporal compartmentalization therefore offers a rational basis for multifunctional partial-thickness burn dressings.

articles.title: Preconditioning the Ocular Surface with UCMSC-Derived Exosomes Preserves Corneal Integrity in Experimental Dry Eye.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Dry eye disease (DED) disrupts corneal epithelial homeostasis and may cause progressive ocular surface injury. Although MSC-derived exosomes have shown therapeutic efficacy after the establishment of DED, their prophylactic potential remains unclear. This study evaluated whether topical UCMSC-derived exosome preconditioning protects the cornea against subsequent aqueous-deficient DED. Methods: Forty female Sprague-Dawley rats aged six to eight weeks were allocated to the prophylactic exosome treatment (PTE) or untreated control groups. PTE rats received low-concentration UCMSC-derived exosome eye drops once daily for 14 days before unilateral lacrimal gland excision; treatment ceased immediately after surgery. Clinical, AS-OCT, histological, ZO-1, Ki-67, and TUNEL assessments were conducted before induction and through Day 14. Corneal TNF-α, IL-1β, TGF-β, and IL-10 expression was measured via qPCR at Day 0. Results: PTE reduced overall corneal neovascularization (mean vessel length, 46.91 vs. 117.06 µm; p = 0.015) and epithelial thickening (54.01 vs. 71.80 µm; p = 0.006). ZO-1 immunoreactivity was significantly greater in the PTE group (D14: 0.678 vs. 0.154; p < 0.001), while there were significantly fewer TUNEL-positive cells at D0 (17.5 vs. 59.5; p < 0.001) and D7 (16.25 vs. 57.25; p < 0.001). Fluorescein staining, stromal thickness, Ki-67 immunoreactivity, and cytokine transcription did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusions: Preconditioning with topical UCMSC-derived exosomes conferred selective corneal protection after dosing ended, characterized by reduced angiogenesis and apoptosis and better preservation of epithelial thickness and tight-junction integrity. These findings support prophylactic exosome exposure as a proof-of-concept strategy for enhancing corneal resilience before predictable ocular surface injury in this severe experimental model; however, the absence of a vehicle-treated control and limited mechanistic characterization warrant further investigation before clinical translation.

articles.title: Population Pharmacokinetic Modeling and Exposure Assessment for Doxycycline in Chinese Pediatric Patients with Severe Refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae Pneumonia.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Severe refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (SRMPP) remains a significant threat to pediatric patients. Doxycycline is recommended as an alternative treatment for pediatric SRMPP, while its pharmacokinetic (PK) profile in this specific population is still poorly characterized. This study aimed to characterize the PK profile of intravenous doxycycline by developing a population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model in Chinese pediatric patients with SRMPP and to evaluate its exposure across different age groups. Methods: The residual blood samples were prospectively collected from patients aged ≤ 18 years receiving intravenous doxycycline for the treatment of SRMPP between April 2023 and April 2025 at the Children's Hospital Affiliated to Zhengzhou University using the opportunistic sampling approach. Plasma concentrations of doxycycline were determined by high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS) and PopPK analysis was performed with the Phoenix NLME software. The steady-state areas under the concentration-time curve from 0 to 24 h (AUCss,0-24 h) of doxycycline were calculated based on Monte Carlo simulation results and compared between groups by geometric mean ratios (GMRs) with 90% confidence intervals (90% CIs). Results: A total of 81 doxycycline plasma concentrations from 68 pediatric patients aged 1.8 to 13.2 years with SRMPP receiving intravenous doxycycline were collected and included for the final PopPK analysis. A one-compartment PopPK model with first-order elimination best described the current data. Body weight was incorporated as the a priori covariate using allometric scaling (fixed exponents of 0.75 for CL and 1.0 for V) and no other screened covariates were identified to have a significant impact on CL or V. For the final model, the estimated typical values were 5.08 L/h/70 kg for CL and 56.57 L/70 kg for V, respectively. Using the 2 to <8 years group as the reference, the GMRs of AUCss,0-24 h in the 8 to 14 years group with BW < 45 kg and BW ≥ 45 kg were 1.10 (90% CI: 1.09-1.11) and 1.04 (90% CI: 1.03-1.05), among which the 90% CIs were fully contained within the prespecified equivalence margins (0.80, 1.25). Conclusions: This final PopPK model characterizes intravenous doxycycline PK profile in Chinese pediatric patients with SRMPP aged 2 to 14 years. Model-based simulations found that the currently recommended dosing regimens of intravenous doxycycline at 2.2 mg/kg every 12 h (a maximum of 200 mg/day every 12 h) yield comparable exposure across the 2 to <8 years group and the 8 to 14 years group.

articles.title: Co-Administration of Fluvoxamine and Morphine: Effects on Nociception and Central Nervous System Function in Healthy Volunteers.
articles.abstract: Background: Combining opioids with non-opioid analgesics is a potential strategy to improve pain management and reduce opioid requirements, but few such combinations have been systematically characterized in humans. Preclinical studies have shown that the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor fluvoxamine can potentiate morphine-induced antinociception. We explored the interactive effects of fluvoxamine and morphine on a battery of evoked pain tests, central nervous system (CNS) function (including electroencephalography (EEG)), and adverse effects. Methods: In a randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, four-way crossover study, 24 healthy volunteers received placebo, morphine (3 mg intravenous (IV) at 2 h plus 7 mg IV at 5 h), fluvoxamine (100 mg oral at 0 h), or the combination. Outcomes included responses to evoked pain tests, CNS function tests, and resting-state EEG. Results: The combination produced greater antinociceptive effects than placebo on cold pressor, electrical-burst, and pressure pain tolerance, but did not significantly enhance pain detection or tolerance thresholds compared with morphine alone. In contrast, the combination significantly reduced capsaicin-induced secondary mechanical allodynia compared with placebo and fluvoxamine monotherapy. These findings were accompanied by distinct reductions in frontal-midline beta- and delta-power on EEG that were not observed with either monotherapy. No significant effects on conditioned pain modulation (CPM) were observed, and additional CNS effects were generally modest. Conclusions: In conclusion, combination therapy with morphine and fluvoxamine was associated with reduced experimentally induced secondary mechanical allodynia and distinct EEG alterations, without additional effects on pain detection or tolerance thresholds compared with morphine alone.

articles.title: A Drug-Excipient Unity Chitosan-Decorated Lipid Nanocarrier Co-Delivering Zedoary Turmeric Oil and Mint Oil for Oropharyngeal Candidiasis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Oropharyngeal candidiasis (OPC), caused mainly by Candida albicans, remains difficult to manage when salivary clearance limits local drug exposure and azole tolerance compromises treatment. Zedoary turmeric oil (ZTO) and mint oil contain antifungal sesqui- and monoterpenes, but their volatility, poor dispersibility, and inefficient membrane delivery limit their use. We developed a "drug-excipient unity" chitosan-decorated lipid nanocarrier (ZTO-NE) to improve the delivery and performance of this combination. Methods: Representative terpenes were evaluated computationally for predicted interactions with ERG11 (CYP51), and coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) was used to examine terpene-lipid-chitosan assembly. ZTO-NE (soybean phosphatidylcholine/cholesterol/low-molecular-weight chitosan; ZTO/mint oil 10:1) was prepared by ethanol injection-sonication and characterized for size, morphology, and stability. Antifungal performance was assessed by MIC, time-kill kinetics, agar diffusion, membrane integrity staining, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and a mouse OPC model. Results: ZTO-NE (77.71 nm; PDI 0.178; +8.52 mV) was stable for 30 days at 4 °C and 25 °C and under light and tolerated three freeze-thaw cycles (germacrone 98.4 ± 0.7% to 96.3 ± 0.3%). Modeling predicted partially complementary ERG11 interaction regions for sesqui- and monoterpenes, and CG-MD supported terpene partitioning into the lipid-chitosan assembly with a positively charged surface. ZTO-NE reduced the MIC from 0.53 ± 0.06 to 0.019 ± 0.012 mg/mL versus the unformulated oil mixture, lowered viable counts below the detection limit within 0.5 h without subsequent regrowth, whereas miconazole showed regrowth; retained its inhibition zone at 48 h; and compromised membrane integrity, with PI fluorescence accounting for >90% of the stained area in fixed-field analysis. In the OPC model, ZTO-NE reduced fungal burden and tongue lesions to an extent comparable with miconazole, with preserved epithelial architecture on qualitative PAS examination. Conclusions: Lipid formulation converted the intrinsically additive (non-antagonistic) ZTO-mint oil combination into a fast, persistent, and cidal antifungal preparation, supporting further development of ZTO-NE for OPC.

articles.title: Longitudinal Effectiveness and Laboratory Safety Profile of Janus Kinase Inhibitors in Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis: A Real-World Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKis) are effective treatments for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD), although longitudinal real-world data on their laboratory safety profile remain limited and there is scarce information regarding whether laboratory changes differ according to JAKi use. So, the main objective of this study was to evaluate longitudinal laboratory changes in patients with AD treated with JAKis in routine clinical practice and to evaluate these changes across different types of JAKis. Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational study including patients with moderate-to-severe AD who initiated treatment with abrocitinib, upadacitinib, or baricitinib. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and patient-reported outcome data were collected at baseline and after 4, 12-16, 24-32, and 48-52 weeks. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using REML mixed-effects models with categorical visit and a patient-specific random intercept, using logarithmic transformations for skewed laboratory parameters. Results: Forty-three patients were included. EASI decreased from 21.18 ± 8.82 at baseline to 6.06 ± 8.27 at week 4 and 7.85 ± 8.63 at weeks 48-52, while pruritus NRS decreased from 7.15 ± 2.48 to 2.23 ± 2.78 and 4.34 ± 3.28, respectively (p < 0.001). At weeks 24-32, total cholesterol (+29.26), LDL cholesterol (+16.09), HDL cholesterol (+6.57), and MCV (+2.12) increased significantly, whereas CRP (-2.87), leukocyte (-1.07), and neutrophil counts (-1.07) decreased significantly. Mean creatinine changes were small. No significant longitudinal changes were observed in AST, ALT, triglycerides or hemoglobin. Few between-treatment differences were identified. No MACE, VTE or changes in lipid-lowering treatment were documented during recorded follow-up. Conclusions: JAKis provided substantial clinical benefit with a favorable longitudinal laboratory safety profile. Laboratory abnormalities were generally mild and consistent with the known safety profile of this class.

articles.title: Exploring Variability in Infliximab Target Attainment and Implications for Concentration-Guided Dosing (CGD) in Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD).
articles.abstract: Background: Substantial interindividual variability in infliximab pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics (PKPD) complicates dose optimization in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Infliximab concentration-guided dosing (CGD) mostly relies on the Therapeutic Window Approach (TWA). Although this approach is widely used in clinical practice, its implications in the setting of substantial variability remain insufficiently characterized. Methods: Model-based simulations evaluated the probability of target (non)-attainment across standard and intensified dosing strategies for intravenous and subcutaneous infliximab. Target attainment was predefined using a therapeutic window (3-7 mg/L) for intravenous infliximab and a threshold (≥12 mg/L) for subcutaneous infliximab. Results: Across dosing strategies, substantial exposure variability resulted in a proportion of patients remaining below the predefined targets. For intravenous infliximab, interval shortening achieved a greater probability of target attainment than dose escalation alone; for example, among patients receiving 5 mg/kg, 50.5% achieved concentrations ≥3 mg/L with Q6W versus 24.5% with Q8W. For subcutaneous infliximab, simulated 180 and 240 mg doses increased the probability of target attainment (≥12 mg/L) versus the approved 120 mg dose, in higher body weight cohorts (72.0% and 86.5%, respectively, vs. 35.5%), potentially highlighting limitations of the current "one-size-fits-all" dosing paradigm. Conclusions: In the presence of substantial infliximab PKPD variability and IBD dynamics, the predefined therapeutic window and fixed threshold may not adequately account for individual variability, potentially contributing to clinical discordance between drug exposure, predefined target attainment, and clinical outcomes. These considerations support evaluating the Target Concentration Approach (TCA) in clinical trials and routine IBD management, given its potential to dynamically adapt dosing to achieve patient-specific target concentration.

articles.title: PreS1-Derived Peptide-Engineered Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoparticles Enhance Liver-Directed Curcumin Delivery in Acute Liver Injury.
articles.abstract: Background: Liver injury remains a major clinical challenge, and the therapeutic performance of many candidate drugs is limited by poor bioavailability and insufficient tissue selectivity. Methods: This study proposes a biomimetic delivery strategy based on genetically engineered cell membrane camouflage. Briefly, curcumin-loaded PLGA nanoparticles were co-ultrasonicated with genetically modified 293T cell membranes displaying a hepatocyte-binding peptide that originates from the preS1 region of the hepatitis B virus large surface protein, allowing the membrane-coated particles to self-assemble into a core-shell structure designated HBVP-MPNs, thereby achieving active hepatocyte-targeted delivery of curcumin. The resulting HBVP-MPNs were designed to engage sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP) and improve liver-directed delivery. Results: HBVP-MPNs exhibited a mean particle diameter of approximately 197.9 nm, a core-shell morphology, high curcumin encapsulation efficiency, and slower cumulative curcumin release over 24 h than uncoated PNs (35.1% versus 51.6%). They showed approximately threefold higher cell-associated fluorescence in HepG2-NTCP cells and approximately 50% lower fluorescence in RAW264.7 macrophages than PNs in vitro. Following intravenous administration in mice, HBVP-MPNs displayed prolonged blood-associated fluorescence and increased liver accumulation. Upon therapeutic evaluation in a CCl4-triggered murine model of acute hepatic injury, HBVP-MPNs elicited markedly lower circulating ALT and AST activities and conferred superior protection against histopathological abnormalities in liver tissue relative to free curcumin and non-targeted control formulations. Cytotoxicity, hemolysis, hematological, serum biochemical, and histological assessments indicated favorable tolerability within the present experimental settings. Conclusions: Collectively, these data warrant further investigation of preS1 peptide-engineered cell membrane-coated nanoparticles as a biomimetic platform for liver-directed curcumin delivery in acute liver injury.

articles.title: Innovative Topical Formulations Incorporating Bioactive Compounds for Enhanced Pressure Ulcer Management: Mechanisms, Efficacies, and Translational Advances.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pressure ulcers (PUs) are chronic wounds associated with sustained mechanical loading, ischemia-reperfusion injury, oxidative stress, dysregulated inflammation, microbial colonization, and impaired tissue repair. Bioactive compounds such as curcumin, resveratrol, asiaticoside, epigallocatechin gallate, and quercetin have attracted interest because of their reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, pro-angiogenic, and extracellular-matrix-modulating activities. Their therapeutic development is frequently limited by poor aqueous solubility, chemical instability, degradation, and inadequate local retention. Advanced topical systems, including liposomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, hydrogels, electrospun systems, and stimuli-responsive formulations, have therefore been investigated to improve formulation stability, local deposition, wound-bed retention, and controlled release. Methods: This critical narrative review evaluates these approaches using an evidence-to-translation framework that distinguishes mechanistic and formulation evidence, indirect evidence from other wound models, pressure-ulcer-specific preclinical evidence, and human pressure-ulcer evidence. Particular attention is given to formulation performance, biological plausibility, model relevance, safety, reproducibility, manufacturing feasibility, regulatory considerations, and clinical readiness. Molecular pathways involving nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) are discussed according to the experimental contexts in which they were investigated, rather than assumed to represent universally demonstrated pressure-ulcer mechanisms. Results: The available evidence suggests that advanced formulations may improve selected pharmaceutical and biological endpoints; however, much of the literature remains mechanistic or preclinical, and findings from non-pressure-ulcer wound models should not be interpreted as direct evidence of clinical efficacy in pressure-ulcer treatment. Human pressure-ulcer evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Conclusions: Future development should therefore prioritize pressure-ulcer-specific validation, standardized formulation and quality attributes, rigorous safety assessment, adequately powered clinical trials, patient-centred outcomes, and health-economic evaluation. This evidence-to-translation framework provides a basis for distinguishing promising experimental formulations from approaches that have progressed sufficiently toward clinical validation.

articles.title: Phosphatidylcholine-Based Nanoformulation of Ergosterol Peroxide Enhances Anticancer Efficacy in Cervical Cancer Models.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: As a fungus-sourced sterol endoperoxide, ergosterol peroxide possesses extensive antitumor properties. However, unfavorable aqueous solubility, rapid in vivo clearance, and poor accumulation within tumor sites constitute major obstacles restricting its progression toward clinical application. Methods: Herein, we constructed a novel phospholipid nanoformulation by supramolecular self-assembly of ergosterol peroxide with soybean phosphatidylcholine via a thin-film dispersion method. Results: The optimized ergosterol peroxide-soybean phosphatidylcholine nanoformulation exhibited a uniform spherical morphology (~98 nm), excellent colloidal stability in serum-containing medium, and pH-responsive drug release behavior. In vitro, the ergosterol peroxide-soybean phosphatidylcholine nanoformulation demonstrated significantly enhanced cellular uptake in HeLa cervical cancer cells compared with free ergosterol peroxide, achieving markedly superior antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic efficacy through amplified reactive oxygen species generation. Furthermore, the ergosterol peroxide-soybean phosphatidylcholine nanoformulation effectively induced immunogenic-cell-death-associated damage-associated molecular patterns. In TC-1 tumor-bearing mice, intravenous administration of the ergosterol peroxide-soybean phosphatidylcholine nanoformulation exhibited potent dose-dependent antitumor efficacy, with biodistribution analysis confirming enhanced intratumoral ergosterol peroxide accumulation via the enhanced permeability and retention effect. Of particular note, ergosterol peroxide-soybean phosphatidylcholine nanoformulation treatment led to a substantial increase in the abundance of splenic B cells, NK cells, CD4+ helper T-cells and CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells; hematology testing together with histopathological examination further demonstrated only marginal systemic toxicity after treatment. Conclusions: Collectively, this soybean phosphatidylcholine-based nanoplatform provides a feasible and promising pharmaceutical strategy for overcoming the inherent delivery limitations of ergosterol peroxide, offering a potential candidate for cervical cancer treatment.

articles.title: Attack on Varroa: Wet Silica Gel Carriers for Controlled Thymol Release in Honey Bee Varroosis Control.
articles.abstract: Background: Rapid evaporation limits the use of volatile natural products for pest control. This study aimed to develop a wet sol-gel silica formulation for sustained delivery of thymol, a volatile natural acaricide used to control Varroa destructor in honeybee colonies. Methods: Co-solvents were screened for thymol solubilization and compatibility with the silica network. The optimized formulation was evaluated for physical stability under ambient conditions and thymol release at 33 °C. Field trials in naturally infested Apis mellifera colonies assessed acaricidal efficacy under different temperature conditions in comparison with a commercial thymol formulation. Results: Triacetin, a non-volatile co-solvent, enabled the preparation of a homogeneous wet silica gel containing 25% w/w thymol, with no phase separation or thymol crystallization for at least 28 days. At 33 °C, the formulation reduced thymol volatilization compared with free thymol. Release was proportional to the square root of time, consistent with a diffusion-controlled mechanism within the triacetin-filled silica network. Estimated thymol depletion times were 62.5 ± 3.4 days for the formulation and 24.6 ± 2.6 days for free thymol. In summer trials, a single administration of 12.5 g thymol per hive yielded acaricidal efficacy comparable to that of a commercial formulation administered twice, with no macroscopically detectable adverse effects on colony health. Performance was reduced under cooler conditions. Conclusions: Wet sol-gel silica prolonged thymol release and showed potential to reduce administration frequency under summer field conditions. Temperature-dependent performance highlights the need to match release kinetics to environmental conditions to maintain acaricidal exposure.

articles.title: Development of Terpene-Containing Polymeric Micelles and Evaluation of Their Potential Skin Penetration Pathways for Improving Dermal Delivery of Resveratrol.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to develop a novel polymeric micelle formulation using poloxamer 184 with ethanol and various terpenes to improve the skin penetration of resveratrol. Methods: The terpenes used in this study were monoterpenes, namely, d-limonene, citral, and cineole. Polymeric micelles were prepared by direct dissolution method. The prepared polymeric micelles were composed of 1% terpenes, 25% poloxamer 184, 5% ethanol, and 69% water. Resveratrol was successfully loaded into the polymeric micelles at a concentration of 0.24 mg/mL. The obtained polymeric micelles were characterized for their size, surface charge, and size distribution. The skin penetration pathway of the micelles was investigated using dual fluorescently labeled particles and observed via confocal laser scanning microscopy. Results: The average particle size of the prepared polymeric micelles ranged from 29.02 ± 2.28 to 57.16 ± 8.32 nm, exhibiting a neutral surface charge and an acceptable size distribution. The in vitro skin penetration study revealed that polymeric micelles with ethanol and d-limonene significantly increased the skin penetration of resveratrol compared with the resveratrol ethanolic solution as control. These polymeric micelles penetrated the skin primarily via the intercellular and transcellular pathways, whereas the transfollicular pathway served as a minor route. The particles also penetrated the skin through the intercluster pathway. Conclusions: The polymeric micelles with d-limonene effectively enhanced dermal delivery of resveratrol by facilitating its penetration through the skin via intercellular and transcellular pathway as major penetration pathway.

articles.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Tablet Weight Uniformity in High Drug Load Continuous Wet Granulation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Tablet weight uniformity is a critical quality attribute of high drug load tablets because weight relative standard deviation (RSD) is closely related to dose variation. This study applied machine learning to predict tablet weight variability from granule attributes after continuous wet granulation and milling. Methods: A high drug load acetaminophen formulation without filler, containing one of three glidant grades, was granulated using a ConsiGmaTM-1 continuous twin-screw wet granulation system. The dried granules were milled using two impeller geometries at three speeds, giving 18 formulation-milling conditions, and compressed under fixed conditions. Tablet weight RSD was modeled using adaptive elastic net regression with linear and quadratic terms and evaluated by nested leave-one-out cross-validation, permutation testing, and bootstrap analysis. Results: Glidant addition improved powder feeding, and milling speed was the main factor affecting granule properties. Tablet weight RSD ranged from 0.45% to 2.09% under identical compression conditions. The granule-attribute model predicted tablet weight RSD better than the process-variable model (Q2 = 0.764 vs. 0.480; permutation p = 0.002). Basic flowability energy (BFE) was the most consistently selected attribute and showed a U-shaped relationship with tablet weight RSD. Conclusions: Granule attributes measured before compression may serve as practical indicators of tablet weight variability in high drug load acetaminophen formulations without filler.

articles.title: Design of Experiments-Guided Development of Gallic Acid-Loaded Transethosomal Chitosan Gels.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gallic acid (GA) is a natural phenolic acid with reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial properties, but its limited skin permeation restricts its topical application. Although previous studies have demonstrated the potential of transethosomal formulations to enhance dermal GA delivery, their liquid dispersion form hinders practical topical use. Methods: The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of chitosan molecular weight, chitosan concentration, and transethosome proportion on the GA release, pH, and spreadability of GA-loaded transethosomal chitosan gel using a Design of Experiments (DoE)-guided approach. First, transethosomes were synthesized using the cold method and assessed for physicochemical properties, in vitro permeability, and physical stability. Next, transethosomal gels were prepared based on a three-level full factorial DoE model. The results were analyzed using polynomial regression modeling and sweet spot analysis. The model-predicted exploratory sweet-spot region was experimentally verified, followed by additional assessments of drug content and content uniformity, rheological properties, and short-term physical stability. Results: GA-loaded transethosomes had a diameter of 167.3 ± 9.9 nm, an encapsulation efficiency of 71.6 ± 5.7%, and substantially higher in vitro permeability across Strat-M® synthetic membranes (2520.77 ± 66.93 µg/cm2 within 24 h) compared to aqueous GA solution. After incorporation into chitosan gel, GA release at 6 h ranged from 65.5% to 93.2%. Formulations showed pH values of 3.93-4.46 and spreadability of 12.6-122.7 cm2. Increased chitosan concentration reduced GA release and increased pH toward the target range, while higher chitosan concentration and molecular weight restricted spreading. Rheological characterization revealed shear-thinning behavior. Conclusions: The DoE-guided approach supported exploratory screening of GA-loaded transethosomal chitosan gels and provided insights into the relationships between formulation composition, GA release, pH, and spreadability.

articles.title: Real-World Medication Utilization and Potential Pharmacokinetic Drug-Drug Interaction Liabilities in Patients with Heart Failure and Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Patients with heart failure (HF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) frequently receive complex multidrug regimens, increasing the potential for pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions (DDIs). Methods: This study used U.S. Optum® claims data from the period 2019-2024 to characterize medication use prevalence in adults with HF or CKD and identify potential DDI liabilities by mapping commonly used medications to established cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzyme and transporter pathways. Potential mechanistic interactions with guideline-directed medical therapy were further prioritized using a semi-quantitative framework based on perpetrator strength and substrate sensitivity, with Tier 1 and Tier 2 representing higher-priority CYP-mediated interaction candidates. Results: The analysis included 856,041 patients with HF and 1,893,827 patients with CKD, with median ages of 75 and 72 years, respectively. In CKD, atorvastatin (25.7%) and metformin (19.1%) were among the most prevalent medications, while metoprolol (33.2%) and furosemide (31.9%) were highly prevalent in HF. Many commonly used medications had established substrate or inhibitor liabilities involving CYP3A, CYP2D6, and transporters including P-gp, OATP1B, MATE, OCT2, and BCRP. CYP3A liabilities were identified in 13 of the 25 most frequently used medications in each population. Higher-priority potential interactions were pathway-specific, with Tier 1 and Tier 2 candidates primarily involving CYP3A in CKD and CYP2D6 in HF. Integrating real-world medication prevalence with established mechanistic DDI information provides a practical, hypothesis-generating framework for identifying and prioritizing potential pharmacokinetic DDI liabilities in HF and CKD. Conclusions: These findings may inform subsequent DDI evaluations and clinical pharmacology study planning to support drug development and future risk-mitigation strategies, although actual co-exposure, clinical DDIs, and associated outcomes were not assessed.

articles.title: In Vitro Killing of Gram-Negative Bacilli Using Ciprofloxacin Based on Dry Powder Inhaled Drug Concentrations.
articles.abstract: Background: Inhaled drug formulations are reported to deliver high airway pulmonary drug concentrations with minimal systemic adverse effects. High drug concentrations with fluoroquinolones are desirable as they are concentration-dependent antibacterial agents. Methods: We exposed drug-susceptible strains of Escherichia coli, Enterobacter cloacae, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa to the measured minimum inhibitory and mutant prevention drug concentrations and to the mean reported pulmonary drug concentrations of ciprofloxacin in vitro by incubation in 3 h and 24 h kill assays. Results: Using 105 cfu/mL in the 3 h kill assay, ciprofloxacin at a 409 µg/mL pulmonary drug concentration killed 89.6 (1.4 log10)-99.9% (4.4 log10) of cells across all tested species following 5 min of drug exposure. For 106-109 cfu/mL in the 24 h kill assay, ciprofloxacin at 409 µg/mL killed 93.6 (1.3 log10)-99.7% (2.7 log10) of P. aeruginosa cells following 6 h of drug exposure across all bacterial densities; 97.4 (1.3 log10)-100% (6.4 log10) of E. coli, 99.4 (2.9 log10)-99.9% (5.9 log10) of E. cloacae and 98.7 (2.1 log10)-100% (7.5 log10) of K. pneumoniae following 24 h of drug exposure. Conclusions: The ciprofloxacin pulmonary drug concentration was bactericidal over all bacterial densities with the high drug concentration rapidly reducing viable bacterial cells. Clinical correlation of these in vitro observations is warranted. Additionally, in vitro testing using the drug powder formation may further validate these observations.

articles.title: IRW-Functionalized Milk-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Promote Osteogenic Recovery in Inflammatory Osteolysis via Modulation of the TXNIP-NRF2 Axis.
articles.abstract: Background: Inflammatory osteolysis features persistent inflammation and impaired bone formation, requiring therapeutics that concurrently suppress inflammation and promote osteogenesis. Ile-Arg-Trp (IRW), a bioactive tripeptide with anti-inflammatory and pro-osteogenic properties, suffers from poor cellular delivery. Milk-derived extracellular vesicles (MEVs) provide a biocompatible delivery platform to enhance intracellular bioavailability of IRW. We engineered IRW-functionalized MEVs (M-IRW), tested whether MEV delivery amplifies IRW's dual bioactivity, and elucidated the molecular mechanism. Methods: The therapeutic effects of M-IRW were evaluated in LPS-stimulated MC3T3-E1 cells and a murine calvarial osteolysis model. Transcriptomic analysis and Geneformer-based virtual knockout identified candidate regulatory pathways, validated by gene silencing, rescue experiments, and reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation. A chronic apical periodontitis model assessed the disease relevance of this pathway. Results: Nano-flow cytometry and quantitative fluorescence analysis confirmed successful preparation and IRW loading of M-IRW, and M-IRW achieved enhanced cellular association with intracellular accumulation of the labeled IRW formulation relative to free peptide. In LPS-treated MC3T3-E1 cells, M-IRW more potently elevated ALP, RUNX2, and OPN expression than free IRW (p < 0.05). In vivo, M-IRW significantly enhanced osteogenic recovery in calvarial osteolysis, surpassing free IRW (p < 0.05). Transcriptomic analysis identified thioredoxin-interacting protein (Txnip) as a candidate mediator; virtual Txnip knockout predicted NRF2-associated transcriptional enrichment (p < 0.05). Depletion of NRF2 attenuated the osteogenic benefit conferred by both TXNIP knockdown and M-IRW treatment. Conclusions: M-IRW enables efficient intracellular delivery of IRW and promotes osteogenic repair in inflammatory osteolysis, at least partly through modulation of the TXNIP-NRF2 axis.

articles.title: Formulation and Evaluation of a Self-Emulsifying Emulsion as an Effective Adjuvant for Inactivated Foot-and-Mouth Disease Vaccine in Mice.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) is an acute and febrile infectious disease that spreads rapidly among cloven-hoofed animals. Vaccination is one of the most effective methods for controlling FMD. However, commercially available FMD vaccines often have limitations in terms of stability, safety, and efficacy. Methods: In this study, a novel self-emulsifying oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion (SEEX2-17) was developed, characterized, and evaluated as an adjuvant against the inactivated FMD vaccine in mice. Results: The data revealed that SEEX2-17 was a homogeneous nanoemulsion with a small particle size (~25 nm) and excellent stability (for at least 2 months at 37 °C). Toxicity evaluation of SEEX2-17 showed that it had good safety and tolerability in mice. Moreover, the SEEX2-17-adjuvanted inactivated FMD vaccine induced significantly higher titers of FMDV-specific IgG antibodies when administered to mice subcutaneously and prolonged the duration of high-titer antibodies compared with the commercial ISA206-adjuvanted vaccine or antigen alone, respectively, within 12 weeks after immunization (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the vaccine adjuvanted with SEEX2-17 elicited significantly higher levels of IgG1 and IgG2a antibodies, as well as higher concentrations of cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2, IL-4, and IL-6) than the antigen alone, indicating that the SEEX2-17-adjuvanted vaccine stimulated vigorous humoral and cellular immunity in mice. Moreover, SEEX2-17 promoted the maturation and activation of dendritic cells (DCs) in the lymph nodes as well as the proliferation of lymphocytes in the spleen. Conclusions: Collectively, SEEX2-17 could trigger enhanced immunity and provide a promising and easy-to-use adjuvant platform for inactivated FMD vaccines with favorable stability and safety.

articles.title: An Oral ROS-Responsive Nanoparticle-Hydrogel System for Intestinal Epithelial Regeneration and Barrier Restoration in Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
articles.abstract: Background: Intestinal epithelial barrier disruption contributes to persistent inflammation in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). CHIR99021 (CHIR) can promote epithelial regeneration and barrier repair, but its oral use is limited by premature gastric release and insufficient intestinal retention. This study aimed to develop an oral formulation that improves intestinal delivery of CHIR and supports barrier restoration. Methods: CHIR-loaded lipid nanoparticles (LNPs@CHIR) were prepared using glyceryl monostearate and Eudragit L100 and incorporated into a thiolated hyaluronic acid (HS) precursor to form HS/LNPs@CHIR (HSL@C). The system was characterized for particle size, mucoadhesion, and drug release, and its therapeutic effects were evaluated in IEC-6 cells and a mouse model of colitis. Results: LNP encapsulation reduced premature CHIR release under simulated gastric conditions, whereas the HS component enabled reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive gelation and ROS-scavenging activity. After oral administration, HSL@C exhibited prolonged colonic retention for up to 24 h. HSL@C promoted intestinal epithelial regeneration and barrier restoration while alleviating tissue injury and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. Conclusions: HSL@C integrates gastric protection, prolonged intestinal retention, ROS-responsive gelation, and epithelial regeneration within an oral delivery system, collectively supporting its potential as a promising barrier-restorative nanoparticle-hydrogel platform for the treatment of IBD.

articles.title: Cotinus coggygria Flower Extract-Loaded Liposomes: Physicochemical Characterization, Antimicrobial Activity, Biocompatibility, and Rheological Evaluation of the Developed Topical Emulgel.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives:Cotinus coggygria Scop. is a polyphenol-rich medicinal plant with antioxidant and antimicrobial properties. This study aimed to develop a liposomal formulation containing aqueous C. coggygria flower extract, evaluate its physicochemical characteristics, antimicrobial activity, and in vitro biocompatibility, and incorporate it into a topical emulgel. Methods: The aqueous extract was characterized by HPLC analysis and subsequently incorporated into soybean phospholipid liposomes prepared by an in situ method followed by membrane extrusion. Vesicle size, polydispersity index (PDI), and zeta potential were determined. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated against clinically relevant skin-associated bacterial and fungal isolates, while biocompatibility was assessed in MRC-5 fibroblasts and HaCaT keratinocytes using the MTT assay. The liposomal dispersion was subsequently incorporated into an emulgel and characterized with respect to organoleptic properties, pH, and rheological behavior. Results: The aqueous extract was particularly rich in gallic acid (74.52 mg/g DW). The developed liposomes showed a mean diameter of 127.48 ± 1.33 nm, PDI of 0.224 ± 0.008, and zeta potential of -29.39 ± 0.95 mV. Extract-loaded liposomes exhibited antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Citrobacter koseri, Proteus mirabilis, and Candida albicans, with measurable activity retained during prolonged incubation. Empty liposomes were non-cytotoxic, while extract-loaded liposomes maintained cell viability above the cytotoxicity threshold across the entire tested concentration range in both cell lines. The final emulgel was homogeneous, mildly acidic, shear-thinning, predominantly elastic, and structurally more resistant than the placebo formulation. Conclusions: The developed C. coggygria flower extract-loaded liposomal emulgel combines nanoscale delivery, relevant antimicrobial activity, excellent in vitro biocompatibility, and suitable topical rheology. These findings support further investigation of the developed system as a multifunctional topical formulation.

articles.title: Prevention of Experimental Severe Malaria.
articles.abstract: Background: Severe malaria, including cerebral malaria and malaria-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome, remains associated with high mortality despite anti-plasmodial and supportive therapies. This study evaluates whether a drug combination can prevent severe malaria complications in a well-defined experimental model. The combination includes an anti-plasmodial artemisinin derivative, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor originally developed for anti-angiogenic cancer therapy, and the general immunosuppressant dexamethasone. Methods: C57BL/6 mice were infected with Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA sub1a strain). Disease progression was assessed using MRI, histology, and liver enzyme analysis and by monitoring parasitemia and survival. The drugs administered included the anti-plasmodial agent artemisone (Art), dexamethasone (Dex), a systemic immunosuppressant, and apatinib (Apa) and sunitinib, both angiogenesis inhibitors. Additional experiments were performed in infected Ncr1-deficient and Tigit-KO transgenic mice (which show decreased or increased activation of NK cells, respectively). Results: PbA infection in C57bl/6 mice induced mild cerebral pathology, severe pulmonary inflammation with edema and microhemorrhages, and elevated liver enzymes, followed by death within a week post-infection, despite relatively low parasitemia on the day of death. Early treatment with Art, starting two- or three days post-infection (PI), killed the parasites and led to complete recovery. Dex, Apa, and sunitinib, initiated at the same early time points PI, prevented acute mortality. However, about two weeks later, these mice developed high parasitemia and succumbed to the disease. Late treatment (starting five days PI) with the individual compounds was ineffective. In contrast, late combined treatment with Dex, Apa, and Art eliminated the plasmodia and rescued most mice. Infection of Ncr1-deficient or Tigit-KO mice resulted in rapidly fatal disease with a course similar to that in mice with the same genetic background, indicating that partial immunosuppression or immune enhancement is insufficient to inhibit malaria progression and that NK cells do not necessarily play a role in the pathology. Conclusions: Multi-target therapy using anti-plasmodial, immunomodulatory, and anti-angiogenic agents has the potential to prevent severe malaria complications and improve survival outcomes.

articles.title: Urea-Based Prodrugs Improve Systemic Mebendazole Exposure After Oral Administration.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mebendazole (MBZ) is an established anthelmintic drug with emerging therapeutic potential in oncology and immunology, but its broader clinical utility is constrained by poor aqueous solubility and extensive first-pass metabolism, resulting in low and variable systemic exposure. Methods: Here, we synthesized and profiled in vitro a series of solubility-enhanced, urea-based MBZ prodrugs designed to favor intact absorption across the intestinal epithelium followed by systemic release of parent MBZ. Results: Optimized candidates exhibited markedly improved solubility under simulated intestinal conditions and a favorable metabolic profile, including reduced intestinal metabolism compared with MBZ. In mouse pharmacokinetic studies, oral administration of selected prodrugs increased systemic MBZ exposure relative to equimolar doses of MBZ. Administration of the lead prodrug 2i resulted in an approximately 10-fold higher peak MBZ concentration (Cmax) and approximately 2-fold higher MBZ exposure (area under the plasma concentration-time curve, AUC) compared with an equimolar dose of MBZ. These differences should be interpreted in light of the different dosing formulations, with the prodrug administered as a solution and MBZ as a suspension. Conclusions: These findings provide in vivo proof-of-concept that urea-based prodrugs may improve systemic MBZ exposure following oral administration and support further evaluation of this strategy for indications requiring systemic drug exposure.

articles.title: Multi-Task Learning of Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability and hERG Cardiotoxicity: A Random- and Scaffold-Split Evaluation on Experimental Data.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability and cardiac hERG liability share physicochemical determinants, motivating the hypothesis that multi-task learning could improve BBB prediction. Methods: We tested this hypothesis using B3DB logBB regression (n = 1058) and a curated hERG dataset (n = 8960). A shared-encoder multi-task neural network was compared with a matched single-task network and Bayesian-optimized gradient boosting under ten random splits, 30 Murcko scaffold splits, and held-out classification sets. Results: Multi-task learning did not improve random-split R2 (0.485 ± 0.016 vs. 0.482 ± 0.015). Under scaffold splitting, its mean R2 was higher (-0.054 vs. -0.817) only because its failures were less severe (the same number of partitions had negative R2); medians were nearly identical (0.394 vs. 0.398). Neither loss weighting, network tuning, nor removal of 39.6% of test compounds sharing a parent structure with hERG training data changed this. Gradient boosting was more robust (scaffold R2 = 0.388 ± 0.188; better in 28-29 of 30 partitions), although not significantly so under a dependence-corrected test. Conclusions: Network failures occurred only when a scaffold group containing 18 atypical compounds (e.g., xenon) entered the test set; after removing 20 such compounds, multi-task R2 (0.409) matched gradient boosting (0.420). On 3031 held-out parent structures, AUCs were similar (0.764-0.772).

articles.title: TNFR2-Specific P20 Peptide-Conjugated Lipid Nanoprobe Enables Dual-Modal PET/CT Molecular Imaging for Precise Detection of Colon Cancer.
articles.abstract: Background: Tumor necrosis factor receptor 2 (TNFR2) is a pivotal immune checkpoint that is highly expressed within the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly on regulatory T cells (Tregs). The P20 peptide specifically binds TNFR2, but its rapid enzymatic degradation in vivo severely limits its clinical translation as an imaging tracer. Methods: Here, we developed a P20-conjugated lipid nanoprobe (DPP) via thin-film hydration and systematically evaluated its physicochemical properties, receptor-binding specificity, biosafety, and in vivo positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) imaging performance in male C57BL/6J mice bearing subcutaneous MC38 wild-type (WT) or TNFR2-knockout (KO) colon tumors. Results: DPP exhibited a near-spherical morphology, a predominant particle-size distribution peak at approximately 125.6 nm, a negative surface charge, and relatively stable hydrodynamic diameters over 7 days. In vitro assays supported TNFR2-associated cellular recognition and showed negligible cytotoxicity under the tested conditions. Micro-PET/CT imaging revealed that DPP markedly improved tumor retention (tumor SUVmean at 4 h: 0.577 ± 0.314) compared with free P20 (SUVmean at 4 h: 0.065 ± 0.011; n = 6 per group; two-sided Welch's unpaired t-test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, adjusted q = 0.010298) in MC38-WT tumors. Tumor SUVmean was higher in WT than in KO tumors at 7 h (0.677 ± 0.181 vs. 0.381 ± 0.191; p = 0.02942) and 12 h (0.428 ± 0.121 vs. 0.224 ± 0.108; p = 0.01588), with both adjusted q values equal to 0.05885 (n = 6 and n = 5, respectively). Notably, tumor-to-muscle uptake ratios were also higher in WT tumors at 7 h (13.11 ± 5.10 vs. 6.86 ± 2.97; p = 0.03459; adjusted q = 0.13836). Conclusions: These results demonstrate that the liposomal formulation enhances tumor-associated uptake of the P20-based tracer, while TNFR2-dependent uptake and the non-invasive monitoring of Treg compartments remain to be validated.

articles.title: Calcium Carbonate-Core Liposome-Embedded Thermosensitive PLGA-PEG-PLGA Hydrogel Combined with Ultrasound for Eradication of Residual Hepatocellular Carcinoma After Radiofrequency Ablation.
articles.abstract: Background: Residual cancer cells stay on the ablation edge after radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). These leftover cells often bring local tumor recurrence. A pH and temperature dual-sensitive drug delivery system was built to handle this issue. Doxorubicin-filled calcium carbonate nanoparticles get wrapped by liposomes (DOX@CaCO3@Lip). These particles sit inside thermosensitive PLGA-PEG-PLGA hydrogel to form DCL-Gel. External ultrasound (US) pairs with this gel to wipe out the remaining HCC cells. Methods: DOX@CaCO3@Lip nanoparticles were produced using gas diffusion. The particles spread evenly in 20 wt% PLGA-PEG-PLGA copolymer liquid. Researchers checked particle size, zeta potential, TEM shape, drug loading (DL%) and encapsulation efficiency (EE%). DCL-Gel was tested for liquid-gel shift, rheological behavior, stickiness, SEM appearance, stability and drug release triggered by pH or US. Heat-exposed HepG2 cells and an orthotopic HCC mouse model that mimics incomplete RFA were used to fully assess the combined treatment effects of DCL-Gel + US. Results: PLGA-PEG-PLGA shifts from liquid to gel at 34-35 °C. DOX@CaCO3@Lip shows an average size of 148 nm and zeta potential of -8.65 mV. Its encapsulation efficiency hits 81.4% and drug loading reaches 11.5%. DCL-Gel can release doxorubicin slowly for as long as 14 days. Mild acidic surroundings (pH 6.2) and US both quicken drug release. The DCL-Gel + US group cuts HepG2 cell viability down to 18.6% and raises apoptosis rate to 71.3%. In animal tests, this group produces the best suppression of tumor growth. It lengthens median survival and lowers systemic drug toxicity. Conclusions: The DCL-Gel + US setup relies on pH-sensitive calcium carbonate carriers, liposome fusion, thermosensitive hydrogel anchoring and US-aided drug penetration. It offers a safe and effective route to clear residual HCC after RFA. This strategy serves as a helpful auxiliary therapy to stop local relapse after thermal ablation.

articles.title: Surface Engineering of Organosilica Nanoparticles Modulates Cellular Uptake, Cytotoxicity, and Mechanobiological Responses.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Surface chemistry is a major determinant of nanoparticle-cell interactions, yet their influence on mechanobiological properties of cells remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the cytotoxic and mechanobiological effects of thiolated and PEGylated organosilica nanoparticles and evaluated whether cortical stiffness could serve as a complementary measure of nanoparticle-cell interactions. Methods: We evaluated thiolated organosilica nanoparticles (Si NP-SH) and two PEGylated nanoparticles (Si NP-PEG750 and Si NP-PEG5000) in non-cancerous human pulmonary fibroblasts (HPF) and cancerous human pulmonary adenocarcinoma (A549) cells. We assessed cellular viability and nanoparticle uptake after exposure and used atomic force microscopy to measure cellular cortical stiffness. Additionally, nanoparticle effects on neuroblast proliferation and mitotic progression were examined in Drosophila melanogaster larval brain explants. Results: HPF cells were markedly less sensitive to all nanoparticle formulations across the tested concentration range, whereas A549 cells showed dose-dependent sensitivity, with thiolated nanoparticles producing the earliest and greatest reduction in viability. Despite a comparable uptake of Si NP-SH and Si NP-PEG750, the thiolated nanoparticles produced greater toxicity, whereas Si NP-PEG5000 showed lower uptake but intermediate toxicity. Atomic force microscopy measurements demonstrated significant cortical softening in Si NP-SH-treated A549 cells, while HPF cells were unaffected. All nanoparticles reduced Drosophila melanogaster neuroblast proliferation in a similar order: Si NP-SH > Si NP-PEG750 > Si NP-PEG5000. Conclusions: The biological activity of organosilica nanoparticles is predominantly dependent on accessibility and intracellular reactivity of surface thiols rather than uptake alone. PEGylation shields thiol reactivity, with higher PEG molecular weight additionally reducing nanoparticle uptake. The consistency of viability, uptake, cortical stiffness, and neuroblast proliferation identifies AFM-derived cortical stiffness as a valuable complementary measurement of nanoparticle-induced stress.

articles.title: Exploration of Alternative Brittle Fillers/Diluents for the Development of Lactose-Free, Vegan-Friendly Tablets by Direct Compression.
articles.abstract: Background: An increasing number of patients and consumers using health-related products are affected by lactose intolerance or follow vegan diets. These individuals seek pharmaceutical products, nutraceuticals, and dietary supplements that are free from animal-derived ingredients. Lactose is one of the most widely used pharmaceutical excipients, particularly in direct compression technology. Therefore, the use of alternative brittle fillers/diluents is justified from both technological and market perspectives. Methods: Formulations comprising 94.0-98.0% w/w of the selected brittle fillers/diluents, 1.0-5.0% w/w lubricant, and 1.0% w/w disintegrant were prepared. The tablet blends were characterized in terms of their physical properties and subsequently compressed into tablets at compression forces ranging from 10 to 25 kN, while ejection forces were simultaneously measured and recorded. The resulting tablets were evaluated with respect to selected physical properties. Results/Conclusions: This study demonstrated that the tested lactose grades could be replaced by alternative brittle fillers/diluents in direct compression formulations. Under the investigated conditions, dibasic calcium phosphates exhibited a distinctive combination of technological properties, with the anhydrous form showing good tabletability and the dihydrate form demonstrating relatively high process robustness. Spray-dried mannitol also exhibited favorable tableting performance.

articles.title: Graph Neural Networks Versus Descriptor-Based Machine Learning for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction: A Matched-Split Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability from structure remains challenging. We evaluated whether graph neural networks (GNNs) improve experimental logBB prediction over descriptor-based machine learning and whether GNN attention agrees with earlier descriptor-based findings. Methods: Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) and Graph Attention Network (GAT) models were trained on 1058 B3DB compounds and compared with LightGBM using 209 RDKit 2D descriptors under identical random and Murcko scaffold splits. Analyses comprised a primary split, 10 repeated random and scaffold splits with nested hyperparameter optimization and paired tests, descriptor-augmented GNNs, classification, external evaluation on the Martins benchmark, and GAT attention analysis. Results and Discussion: In the primary split, LightGBM achieved the highest R2 (random 0.673; scaffold 0.604) versus GCN (0.514; 0.133) and GAT (0.430; 0.310). Across repeated splits with nested hyperparameter optimization, LightGBM outperformed both GNNs under both protocols (paired t-test p < 0.001). GCN and GAT did not differ significantly under scaffold splitting in either the original repeated-split evaluation (p = 0.49) or the optimized comparison (p = 0.184). Descriptor augmentation improved both GNNs (p < 0.001); under scaffold splitting, augmented GCN (R2 = 0.463 ± 0.084) was not significantly different from LightGBM (0.494 ± 0.093; p = 0.22). Using thresholded regression predictions, LightGBM had the highest mean AUC in every condition (≈0.87 versus 0.77-0.84). On 1627 compounds from the independently curated Martins benchmark, mean AUC was 0.84 (LightGBM), 0.83 (GCN) and 0.81 (GAT). GAT attention was higher on nitrogen/oxygen than carbon in 82 of 98 eligible molecules, but halogen, sulfur, and phosphorus atoms received even more attention. Conclusions: Under the evaluated conditions, 2D descriptors outperformed basic GCN and GAT models across splits; descriptor augmentation substantially narrowed the gap. GAT attention provides hypothesis-generating, not causal, insight.

articles.title: Visualizing Disintegration Pathways of Orally Disintegrating Tablets in Water and Thickened Media Using Cryo-FIB-SEM and X-Ray CT.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Orally disintegrating tablets (ODTs) are often used for patients with dysphagia; however, their co-administration with "thickened water" in clinical settings can delay disintegration and potentially reduce therapeutic efficacy. While wicking networks formed by superdisintegrants facilitate rapid disintegration, we hypothesized that viscous polymers in thickened water cause "pore clogging" within these networks. Although conventional macroscopic evaluations have demonstrated this delay, direct visualization of the underlying microstructural changes remains unexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to elucidate the microstructural mechanisms of disintegration delay. Methods: Simplified model ODTs containing either a wicking-type (crospovidone [CP]) or a swelling-type (sodium starch glycolate [SSG]) disintegrant were prepared. Their microstructures and disintegration behaviors were evaluated by cryogenic focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (Cryo-FIB-SEM), three-dimensional (3D) X-ray computed tomography (CT), and disintegration tests under simulated gastric conditions (pH 1.2). Results: Cryo-FIB-SEM revealed that CP-containing tablets formed numerous channel-like pores that promoted capillary action upon contact with water, whereas SSG-containing tablets formed larger, isolated macropores. X-ray CT analysis demonstrated distinct low-density regions associated with penetration-induced structural changes in both formulations. In CP-containing tablets, these regions extended throughout the channel network, whereas in SSG-containing tablets they were largely confined to the tablet surface. Consequently, the disintegration of CP-containing tablets in simulated gastric fluid was significantly delayed compared to that of SSG-containing tablets. Conclusions: The findings are consistent with a pore-clogging mechanism in which penetration of a viscous medium interferes with the liquid transport pathways responsible for rapid tablet disintegration. Combined Cryo-FIB-SEM and X-ray CT imaging provided direct morphological evidence of disintegrant-dependent structural responses in viscous media and offers a new framework for mechanistic investigation of tablet disintegration processes.

articles.title: Exploratory Preclinical Evaluation and Model-Based Pharmacokinetics of a Dual-Drug Biodegradable Intracameral Implant in Rabbits.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Postoperative management after cataract surgery involves topical anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial treatments, whose clinical performance may be affected by adherence, administration technique, and intraocular exposure. This study evaluated a biodegradable poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) intracameral implant containing moxifloxacin hydrochloride and dexamethasone, designed for intraoperative placement. Methods: Clinical tolerability, anti-inflammatory activity in a uveitis model, and antibacterial performance following a low-inoculum intravitreal challenge with Pseudomonas aeruginosa were evaluated in New Zealand White rabbits. Aqueous humor pharmacokinetic profiles were also assessed in phakic and aphakic eyes. Clinical follow-up included slit-lamp biomicroscopy and intraocular pressure measurements. Concentration-time data were analyzed by means of nonlinear mixed-effects models and model-based simulations. Results: No visible implant material remained four weeks after insertion. A transient pseudo-membrane was observed shortly after implantation in some implanted eyes, but it resolved spontaneously and was not accompanied by clinical inflammatory signs. No sustained increase in intraocular pressure was observed during follow-up. Untreated bacterially challenged eyes rapidly developed severe endophthalmitis, whereas implant-treated eyes showed no clinical evidence of endophthalmitis. In the exploratory uveitis experiment, implant-treated eyes showed lower clinical inflammatory scores and faster recovery than matched eyes without the implant. Model-based simulations suggested persistent dexamethasone exposure through day 30, whereas moxifloxacin reached an early peak and was predominantly below the limit of quantification from day 7 onward. Conclusions: These findings provide preliminary preclinical proof-of-concept evidence supporting the clinical tolerability and pharmacological activity of the implant under the experimental conditions evaluated. The results are hypothesis-generating, should not be extrapolated to clinical safety or efficacy, and do not demonstrate microbiological eradication. Further studies with larger cohorts, pseudophakic models, microbiological and histopathological endpoints, and optimized pharmacokinetic sampling are required.

articles.title: Preformulation Study of Aqueous Extracts of Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) Seed from Criollo and Hass Cultivars for Solid Dosage Forms.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) seed is an agro-industrial by-product with significant pharmacological potential. This study aimed to conduct a preformulation assessment of aqueous seed extracts from Criollo (M1) and Hass (M2) cultivars. Methods: The extracts were characterized for total phenolic content (TPC) and ABTS•+ scavenging capacity, and their compatibility with pharmaceutical excipients was evaluated in binary mixtures by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy with Pearson correlation and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and isothermal stress testing (50 °C, 15 days) with HPLC quantification of epicatechin (IST-HPLC). Results: M2 showed significantly higher TPC (192.80 ± 4.90 µg GAE/mg) than M1 (27.08 ± 0.51 µg GAE/mg; p < 0.0001). ABTS•+ inhibition was 59.92 ± 1.76% for M1 (0.05 mg/mL) and 50.79 ± 1.19% for M2 (0.01 mg/mL). The DSC transition enthalpies of both extracts did not differ significantly (p = 0.1271). Maltodextrin and gum arabic were compatible with both extracts, suggesting that they could serve as common excipients for both cultivars, whereas the chemical stability of five M2 mixtures could not be determined by IST-HPLC. Sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) was incompatible with M1, as shown by a 29.44 percentage-point decrease in epicatechin recovery (p < 0.0001), separate HCA clustering (Euclidean distance > 0.009), and the lowest FTIR spectral correlation (r = 0.990). Conclusions: These findings provide a scientific basis for the rational development of solid dosage forms from avocado seed extracts.

articles.title: Thermoreversible Chitosan/β-Glycerophosphate Depot for Sustained Localized Delivery of Doxorubicin in Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Direct intratumoral injection of doxorubicin (DOX) can increase local drug exposure, but rapid escape from the tumor limits retention and contributes to systemic toxicity. This study developed a thermoreversible chitosan/β-glycerophosphate (CS/β-GP) hydrogel designed to form an in situ depot and prolong local DOX delivery. Methods: A three-factor Box-Behnken design was used to optimize CS, β-GP, and DOX concentrations against gelation temperature, gelation time, viscosity, and 7-day cumulative release. The optimized formulation was characterized by rheology, injectability, degradation, swelling, porosity, and 4T1 cytotoxicity. Intratumoral retention, plasma and organ biodistribution, antitumor efficacy, body-weight changes, and cardiac toxicity were then evaluated in 4T1 tumor-bearing BALB/c mice. Results: The optimized hydrogel contained 1.684% w/v CS, 6.601% w/v β-GP, and 0.200% w/v DOX, gelled at 36.3 ± 0.55 °C within 1.65 ± 0.28 min, and released 84.66 ± 8.38% of DOX over 7 days. DOX-loaded hydrogel preserved concentration-dependent cytotoxicity. During in vivo studies, hydrogel delivery lowered the observed plasma DOX peak by approximately 55% and retained measurable intratumoral DOX for 168 h, whereas free DOX solution was no longer detectable. Tumor growth suppression was sustained, with tumor volumes of 205.62 ± 36.85 versus 701.69 ± 69.35 mm3 for free DOX solution on day 24. Repeated hydrogel treatment also markedly attenuated cardiac troponin-I (cTnI) and creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) elevations relative to free DOX solution. Conclusions: Thermoreversible CS/β-GP delivery reshaped DOX exposure from a rapidly dispersing intratumoral dose into a sustained local depot, improving tumor control while reducing the early plasma peak and attenuating cardiac-injury biomarker elevations.

articles.title: Engineering a Stable Tegoprazan Nanosuspension System for Enhanced Dissolution and Oral Bioavailability.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The aim of this study was to design a nanosuspension (NS) of tegoprazan (TPZ), a novel potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB), to overcome its low aqueous solubility and improve oral absorption. Methods: TPZ NSs were prepared using a lab-scale bead-milling technique. Subsequently, their physicochemical properties, in vitro dissolution profiles, storage stability, and in vivo pharmacokinetic profiles were evaluated. Results: Among various screened stabilizers, polyvinyl alcohol was selected as the suspending agent due to its favorable physicochemical stability. The optimized NS exhibited a mean particle size of approximately 270 nm and a zeta potential of -12.1 mV, preserving the crystalline state of TPZ. In vitro dissolution studies revealed that the NS and its freeze-dried form (NS-FD) markedly enhanced drug dissolution across all tested dissolution media (pH 1.2, 4.0, 6.8, and distilled water) compared to the raw drug material. Furthermore, the NS formulations remained physically and chemically stable for up to 12 weeks under long-term and accelerated storage conditions (25 °C/60% relative humidity (RH) and 40 °C/75% RH). In vivo pharmacokinetic studies in male Sprague-Dawley rats revealed that the oral TPZ NS resulted in approximately a 2.1-fold increase in systemic exposure compared to the raw material and microsuspension. Conclusions: These findings suggest that TPZ NS is a promising strategy to enhance the oral absorption of P-CAB, using a simple, organic-solvent-free fabrication process.

articles.title: Chitosan-Coated Pirfenidone/Azithromycin Coloaded Liposomal Inhalation Platform for Synergistic Treatment of Acute Exacerbation of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Background: Acute exacerbation of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (AE-IPF), frequently triggered by infections, is characterized by acute inflammation occurring on top of progressive fibrosis, resulting in high mortality rates and a lack of effective treatments. This study aimed to disrupt the "infection-inflammation-fibrosis" cascade through a chitosan-coated liposomal formulation that co-loads pirfenidone (PFD) and azithromycin (AZM) for nebulized inhalation (CS-PFD/AZM-Lip). Methods: The formulation utilized a dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC)/cholesterol lipid backbone that closely resembles the endogenous pulmonary surfactant. The liposomal surface was electrostatically coated with chitosan to enhance mucoadhesion, antibacterial synergy, and aerosolization stability. We characterized particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), zeta potential, and encapsulation efficiency, alongside stability assessments during nebulization and storage at 4 °C. In vitro release was evaluated in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from bleomycin/lipopolysaccharide-challenged mice, simulating the pathological microenvironment. Cellular uptake and antifibrotic effects were examined in TGF-β1-activated fibroblasts, while efficacy and safety were tested in a bleomycin- and lipopolysaccharide-induced AE-IPF mouse model. Results: CS-PFD/AZM-Lip demonstrated a uniform size of 138.83 ± 0.31 nm (PDI 0.251 ± 0.009), a zeta potential of +23.67 ± 1.27 mV, and encapsulation efficiencies of 83.7% (PFD) and 86.0% (AZM), all of which remained unchanged following nebulization, with an 8-week stability at 4 °C. Both drugs exhibited enhanced release in the simulated pathological microenvironment. The formulation was efficiently internalized by activated fibroblasts, significantly suppressing migration, myofibroblast differentiation, and collagen production at both transcriptional and protein levels. In AE-IPF mice, nebulized CS-PFD/AZM-Lip attenuated pulmonary inflammation and collagen deposition compared to oral free drugs, improved lung function and survival, and showed no detectable toxicity in major organs or in hematological, serum biochemical, and hemolysis assessments. Conclusions: This study successfully synthesized the CS-PFD/AZM-Lip nano-liposome for nebulized inhalation. By integrating clinically established therapeutic regimens with an inhalable nanocarrier platform, CS-PFD/AZM-Lip presents a highly promising novel strategy for the treatment of AE-IPF.

articles.title: Minocycline-Collagen Coatings on Textile Surgical Mesh.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Synthetic mesh repair of abdominal wall hernias can be complicated by infection, often requiring mesh removal. Bioactive coatings may enable local antimicrobial delivery while preserving mesh properties. This study developed a synthetic surgical mesh coated with a minocycline hydrochloride (MH)-loaded type I fibrillar collagen gel, evaluated MH concentration and coating layer effects, optimized the formulation, and assessed preliminary in vivo tolerability and wound healing. Methods: Collagen gel containing MH was applied to meshes by repeated immersion/drying (1-3 layers) using a Mitchell-Bayne 32 design. Meshes were characterized by optical microscopy, SEM, contact angle, enzymatic degradation, and MH release, and in vivo clinical trials were conducted in 20 Wistar rats using superficial excisional and thermal injury models. Results: SEM proved collagen/MH deposition. The meshes with 0.6% MH showed the highest enzymatic resistance. Release was rapid in the first 60 min and then gradual; the Power law model fitted best (R2 > 0.97), indicating non-Fickian release. The mesh coated with two layers of collagen consisting of 0.6% MH promoted faster wound closure than controls: complete re-epithelialization by day 5 for superficial wounds, and complete thermal wound healing by day 10. No macroscopic local intolerance or systemic adverse reactions occurred. Conclusions: The MH-loaded collagen-coated textile mesh provided controlled local drug delivery, enzymatic stability, and preliminary wound-healing benefits with good local tolerability.

articles.title: Development and Optimization of Tacrolimus-Loaded Solid Lipid Nanoparticle Gels Using a Box-Behnken Design: Comparison of Three Lipid Matrices and In Vivo Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Tacrolimus has poor aqueous solubility and limited skin permeation, necessitating formulation strategies for effective topical therapy. This study aimed to develop tacrolimus-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) and an SLN-gel, comparing optimized SLNs prepared with three lipids-Compritol 888 ATO (C888), Compritol HD5 ATO (CHD5), and Stearic acid (St.a). Methods: Each SLN was optimized via Box-Behnken design (BBD) using factors X1 (lipid amount), X2 (surfactant amount), and X3 (homogenization speed). Morphological analysis was conducted using SEM and TEM, while the solid-state properties were evaluated by XRD and FT-IR. In vitro drug release was assessed using the dialysis bag method, and permeation was evaluated using Franz diffusion cells. The SLNs showing the highest cumulative permeation with a consistent release profile were tested in a 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (DNCB)-induced atopic dermatitis mouse model. Results: Optimized SLNs obtained from the BBD demonstrated particle sizes of 275.8, 190.9, 308.9 nm, PDIs of 0.35, 0.26, 0.14, zeta potentials of -15.2, -12.9, -24.0 mV, and encapsulation efficiencies of 84.6, 91.8, 92.5% for C888, CHD5, and St.a, respectively. In dialysis-bag studies, all SLNs showed higher cumulative release than drug solution and Protopic® 0.1%. SEM/TEM revealed spherical morphology, while FT-IR/XRD confirmed drug incorporation within the lipid matrix. Franz diffusion showed higher permeation than API-gel and Protopic® 0.1%, ranked St.a > C888 > CHD5, with 48 h cumulative amounts of 127.2, 96.8, 87.5 μg/cm2. The St.a-SLN-gel significantly improved atopic dermatitis lesions in the DNCB-induced mouse model in vivo (score 14.5→1.75, n = 6, p < 0.001). Conclusions: Box-Behnken optimization produced an SLN-gel surpassing existing formulations in release, permeation, and in vivo efficacy, demonstrating tunable performance via lipid selection and offering a reproducible, translatable approach for topical tacrolimus.
