articles.title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of a Bisphosphonate-Tazobactam Conjugate for Bone-Targeted β-Lactamase Inhibition.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Osteomyelitis and implant-associated bone infections remain difficult to treat because of persistent bacterial colonization, biofilm formation, limited antibiotic exposure in infected bone, and antimicrobial resistance. Bisphosphonate conjugation has been explored for bone-targeted antibiotic delivery, but targeting a β-lactamase inhibitor itself to our knowledge has not been established. This study aimed to synthesize and evaluate an ester-linked bisphosphonate-tazobactam (BP-Tazo-ester) conjugate as a putative bone-targeted β-lactamase inhibitor prodrug. Methods: BP-Tazo-ester (compound 5) was synthesized and characterized by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and mass spectrometry. β-lactamase inhibition was assessed using a nitrocefin-based in vitro assay. Hydroxyapatite binding was evaluated using a sample derived from compound 5. Piperacillin combinations were evaluated against β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli HS and planktonic Staphylococcus aureus CCUG 25925. The same S. aureus strain was used in an ex vivo bone-slice early-colonization model. Results: Compound 5 was obtained in 61% yield and retained measurable β-lactamase inhibitory activity, although its observed activity was lower than that of free tazobactam. TMSBr-treated material derived from compound 5 exhibited high apparent hydroxyapatite binding. Compound 5 supported piperacillin-mediated growth inhibition against E. coli HS. Against S. aureus CCUG 25925, piperacillin-compound 5 and piperacillin-tazobactam showed the same observed MIC, both lower than that of piperacillin alone, while compound 5 alone exhibited limited antibacterial activity. In the bone-slice model, piperacillin-compound 5 reduced recoverable S. aureus counts below the assay limit of detection during 24 h of treatment co-initiated with inoculation. Conclusions: These findings provide preliminary proof-of-concept for a bisphosphonate-based strategy targeting a β-lactamase inhibitor rather than the antibiotic partner. Further research on linker-cleavage kinetics, bone biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, and in vivo efficacy is warranted.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Multianalyte LC-MS/MS Method for Quantification of BRAF and MEK Inhibitors and Cannabidiol in Cell Lysates and Cell Culture Media.
articles.abstract: Background: BRAF and MEK inhibitors are established targeted therapies for melanoma and are frequently administered in combination regimens (dabrafenib/trametinib, encorafenib/binimetinib, and vemurafenib/cobimetinib). The non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid cannabidiol (CBD) is currently under investigation as a potential anticancer compound. As CBD may be combined with targeted anticancer therapies, potential effects on intracellular drug exposure require further investigation. Methods: A rapid and sensitive LC-MS/MS method was developed and validated with reference to the relevant principles of the ICH M10 guideline for the simultaneous quantification of three BRAF inhibitors, three MEK inhibitors, and CBD in cell lysates and cell culture media. The method was applied to determine intracellular drug levels in A375 melanoma cells following single-agent and combined treatments. Results: The method showed robust analytical performance across the evaluated validation parameters, including selectivity, calibration performance, precision, accuracy, recovery, and stability, and met the predefined acceptance criteria where applicable. Because of limited apparent analyte recovery in protein-free aqueous solutions, most likely resulting from nonspecific surface adsorption of the lipophilic compounds, 1% (w/v) bovine serum albumin was added for analyte stabilization. Application of the method to A375 melanoma cells enabled the reliable detection of treatment-dependent alterations in protein-normalized cell-associated analyte levels. Conclusions: This validated LC-MS/MS method enables reliable simultaneous quantification of BRAF inhibitors, MEK inhibitors, and CBD in cellular models. It provides a valuable tool for investigating intracellular drug concentrations and potential drug-drug interactions affecting intracellular drug levels.

articles.title: Atomic Force Microscopy Investigation of an Algorithm for Calculation of Targeted Liposomal Binding Force Based on Affinity Measurements.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ligand-target binding force is a valuable quality control parameter for evaluation of targeted nanoparticulate formulations. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) is the method of choice for measuring this parameter, but AFM instruments are expensive and not available to researchers outside of universities, large medical centers, and technology hubs. We have developed a computational method for determining binding force from enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) affinity measurements, which may also be obtained by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and isothermal titrating calorimetry (ITC) measurements. We have tested a series of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA)-loaded echogenic liposome (TELIP) preparations, in which the tPA fibrin-binding sites are exposed, with AFM to confirm the accuracy and to validate the computational method. Methods: Plastic culture dishes (35 mm) were coated with monoclonal anti-tPA antibodies (5 µg/mL) overnight at 4 °C. After blocking of unoccupied sites with 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA), dishes were incubated with 1.5 mL of TELIP (1 mg lipid/mL 0.02 M phosphate-buffered saline, pH 7.4) for 2 h at 37 °C. After washing with PBS, dishes were scanned with fibrin-coated AFM probes. Binding force was expressed as pN/molecule. Results: The computed binding force of seven TELIP batches ranged from 407 to 441 pN/molecule. AFM values compared favorably with the computed values, but varied over a wider range. AFM measurements were made on four TELIP batches. Conclusions: The computational algorithm has been validated and can be used as a translational tool.

articles.title: Development and Physicochemical Characterization of a Novel HPMC-Based Wound-Dressing Film Containing Betonica bulgarica: Phytochemical Profiling of the Plant Extract.
articles.abstract: Background:Betonica bulgarica Degen et Neič is an endemic Balkan species with reported antioxidant, antimicrobial, antitumor, immunomodulatory, and hypoglycemic effects. Despite its promising biological potential, its phytochemical composition remains incompletely characterized, and its application in advanced wound-healing medications has not been investigated. Therefore, the aim of the present study is to develop hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC)-based wound dressings incorporating B. bulgarica bioactive compounds as a biocompatible delivery platform with promising physical and chemical properties suitable for further biological evaluation in wound-care applications. Methods: The phytochemical composition of the extract was investigated using Ultra-High-Performance Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (UHPLC-MS). Results: The putative analysis led to the identification of 81 compounds in positive and negative ionization mode. Predominant classes included flavonoids, phenolic acids, terpenes, organic acids, fatty acids, sugars, nucleobases and amino acids. HPMC-based films containing B. bulgarica extract were prepared and characterized with key physicochemical and mechanical properties. Mechanical evaluation demonstrated that high-molecular-weight HPMC films exhibited higher tensile strength (73 ± 9 MPa) than low-molecular-weight formulations (44 ± 8 MPa). Increasing the Betonica bulgarica extract loading up to 8.8 mg/cm2 was associated with concentration-dependent decreases in tensile strength, elongation at break, and Young's modulus across all film types. These changes indicate an alteration of the mechanical behavior of the films, although the individual contributions of the extract and the varying PEG-to-HPMC ratio cannot be distinguished. Incorporation of Betonica bulgarica extract reduced the water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) of the HPMC films, promoting a denser polymer matrix structure. Additionally, high-molecular-weight HPMC films displayed higher WVTR values than low-molecular-weight formulations due to increased free volume within the entangled matrix. The release profiles of Betonica bulgarica extract from the HPMC films were fitted to the Korsmeyer-Peppas model using data from the first 8 h of the release study (R2 = 0.9811-0.9989). The release exponent values indicated anomalous transport behaviour for the low-MW HPMC films (n = 0.68-0.70), whereas the values obtained for the high-MW HPMC films (n = 0.404-0.438) were closer to the range commonly associated with Fickian diffusion in planar matrices. The high-MW HPMC films showed more gradual release profiles, supporting their further investigation as matrices for the delivery of plant-derived extracts. Conclusions: The findings provide further insight into the phytochemical profile of the endemic species B. bulgarica and demonstrate the feasibility of incorporating its bioactive compounds into HPMC-based wound-dressing film for future biological evaluation. The developed formulations represent a promising natural-based platform for wound-healing applications, although further studies are required to establish their therapeutic efficacy and mechanism of action.

articles.title: Development of Electrostatically Stabilized siRNA-Peptide Complexes for Anti-Angiogenic Treatment of Endometriosis.
articles.abstract: Background: Endometriosis (EM) is a benign gynecological disorder characterized by the hyperproliferation of endometrial cells outside the uterus. This abnormal proliferation followed by neoangiogenesis leads to the formation of EM lesions, which often require surgical removal. Contemporary pharmacological treatment of EM involves hormonal therapies, which are frequently accompanied by adverse effects and a high rate of symptom recurrence following cessation of treatment. Consequently, the development of innovative pharmaceuticals is crucial for the effective management of EM. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics are evolving from a niche modality into a major pharmaceutical platform applicable for the therapy of inherited and multifactorial diseases. However, a major obstacle hindering broader clinical use is the challenge of delivering siRNA to tissues beyond the liver. Peptide-based nanoparticles mediating siRNA delivery hold potential to overcome this limitation through receptor targeting and by shielding excessive positive charges. Methods: In the current study, we developed ternary polyplexes composed of anti-VEGFA siRNA, a cationic arginine-rich polymer, and an anionic glutamate-rich polymer modified with a cyclic RGD (cRGD) moiety for αVβ3-integrin binding. The polyplexes were characterized physicochemically, and their toxicity and GFP marker gene silencing properties were studied in vitro. Anti-angiogenic effects were evaluated in vivo using a surgically induced EM model in female Wistar rats. Results: A significant reduction in the volume of modeled EM lesions, along with decreased VEGFA gene expression and apparent reduction in endothelial marker CD34 immunostaining in representative sections, was observed following intralesional administration of anti-VEGFA siRNA-loaded peptide-based nanoparticles decorated with the cRGD ligand, compared to control ligand-free nanoparticles. Conclusions: The results provide evidence that electrostatically stabilized siRNA-peptide nanoparticles can exert anti-angiogenic effects in EM lesions following intralesional administration, warranting further investigation of their targeting properties, safety, and therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Engineered Streptococcus salivarius K12-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Functionalized with an Anti-PD-L1 Nanobody to Promote Recurrent Aphthous Ulcer Healing.
articles.abstract: Background: Recurrent aphthous ulcer (RAU) is a common inflammatory disorder of the oral mucosa characterized by painful ulceration and delayed tissue repair, while rapid salivary clearance and mechanical stimulation limit the efficacy of conventional topical therapies. Streptococcus salivarius K12-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are potential cell-free agents for inflammatory oral mucosal disease. We investigated whether surface functionalization with a nanobody selected against human PD-L1 (αPDL1-VHH) could improve their biological activity. Methods: K12-derived EVs were surface-functionalized through a sequential enzymatic ligation strategy, in which endogenous Sortase A-associated machinery was exploited for linker anchoring, followed by OaAEP1-mediated site-specific conjugation of αPDL1-VHH. Proteomic profiling was performed to identify Sortase A and the LPXTG cell wall anchor motif in K12-EVs. The cellular association of EV-αPDL1-VHH was evaluated in PD-L1-expressing cells. Anti-inflammatory activity was assessed in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, and therapeutic effects were evaluated in an acetic acid-induced mouse oral ulcer model. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to investigate the molecular responses to treatment. Results: Proteomic profiling identified Sortase A in K12-EVs and revealed enrichment of the LPXTG cell wall anchor motif, supporting the molecular basis of the endogenous enzymatic ligation strategy. EV-αPDL1-VHH exhibited enhanced association with PD-L1-expressing cells compared with unmodified EVs. In LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, EV-αPDL1-VHH markedly suppressed the expression and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines and showed greater anti-inflammatory activity than unmodified EVs or free αPDL1-VHH. In an acetic acid-induced mouse oral ulcer model, EV-αPDL1-VHH accelerated wound closure, increased epithelial thickness, and improved histological recovery. Transcriptomic analysis revealed broad transcriptional remodeling and modulation of inflammatory and mTOR-associated pathways, accompanied by increased expression of the stress-responsive regulators DDIT4 and SESN2. Conclusions: PD-L1-targeted engineering enhanced the therapeutic activity of K12-derived EVs and promoted oral mucosal healing, highlighting EV-αPDL1-VHH as a promising targeted probiotic-derived EV platform for inflammatory oral mucosal diseases.

articles.title: Population Pharmacokinetics of Linezolid in Healthy Chinese Adults: Absorption Characteristics and Exploratory ABCB1-Related Variability.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Linezolid has almost complete oral bioavailability, yet systemic exposure varies substantially between individuals. Food delays absorption, and genetic variation in ABCB1 may also contribute. We developed a population pharmacokinetic model to characterize these sources of variability. Methods: Plasma concentration-time data were analyzed after a single 600 mg oral dose of the reference product ZYVOX® in 48 healthy Chinese adults from two independent fasting and fed cohorts (n = 24 each) of a randomized crossover bioequivalence study. Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling (Monolix 2024R1) was used to characterize linezolid absorption and disposition and to evaluate covariates, including food status, sex, and ABCB1 variants. Model adequacy was assessed using standard diagnostics, including prediction-corrected visual predictive checks. Results: A one-compartment model with linear elimination and sequential zero- to first-order absorption with a lag time best described the data. Food status was retained as a covariate on absorption lag time (Tlag; 0.075 h fasting vs. 0.25 h fed), whereas effects on the other absorption parameters were not retained. ABCB1 C1236T genotype was associated with apparent oral clearance (CL/F; 5.00 L/h in T/T, 5.77 L/h in C/T, and 7.36 L/h in C/C carriers). The reference estimates of CL/F and V/F were 5.00 L/h (RSE 3.78%) and 43.78 L (RSE 2.03%). Conclusions: The sequential absorption model identified a food-related difference in Tlag and an association between ABCB1 C1236T genotype and apparent oral clearance. These findings may help interpret food-related changes in bioequivalence data and provide a candidate model for future evaluation in patients.

articles.title: Pharmaceutical Salts vs. Ionic Cocrystals: A Combined Structural and Solubility Study of Fluoxetine Multicomponent Crystals.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The present work constitutes the comparative study of solubility and dissolution parameters of pharmaceutical salts and ionic cocrystals using the ternary system (fluoxetine:hydrochloric acid:fumaric acid) as an example. Methods: A multi-stage synthesis based on extraction of fluoxetine (FXT) free base into the diethyl ether layer was used to isolate two stable fumaric acid (FumAc) salts with (1:1) and (2:1) stoichiometry and a metastable polymorph of the (1:1) salt. The solvent-dependent solubility of FXT∙HCl, [FXT+FumAc] (1:1) salt and [FXT∙HCl+FumAc] (2:1) ionic cocrystal was rationalized in terms of acid-base equilibria, common ion effect, activity coefficients and surfactant-like activity of FXT supported by crystal packing analysis. Different kinetic models were applied to fit the experimental dissolution profiles in blank and supplemented biorelevant FaSSGF and FaSSIF media. Results: The crystal structure of fluoxetine hydrogen fumarate was found to feature the robust layered packing involving 2D hydrogen-bonded sheets separated by FXTH+ bilayers. The highest solubility advantage with respect to commercial FXT∙HCl in acidic media (4.8 times) was confirmed for [FXT+FumAc] (1:1) in pH 1.2 buffer solution, while the [FXT∙HCl+FumAc] (2:1) ionic cocrystal demonstrates the highest solubility (1.9 times) in blank FaSSIF medium (pH 6.5). The dissolution kinetic of studied solid forms was best modeled by zero-order and Korsmeyer-Peppas models. Conclusions: The solubility and dissolution rate were established to be inversely dependent on the solid form stability in specific media. The ionic cocrystal was observed to be the only solid form to demonstrate improved dissolution rate in complemented FaSSGF due to the un-ionized state of fumaric acid resulting in formation of mixed micelles with solubilizers. The [FXT+FumAc] (1:1) salt and the [FXT∙HCl+FumAc] ionic cocrystal can be recommended as soluble solid forms of fluoxetine, respectively, for gastro-soluble and enteric-coated formulations.

articles.title: Development of cRGD-Functionalized Fe3O4 Nanoparticles for Glioblastoma Targeting and Evaluation of Magnetic Hyperthermia Using a Planar Coil in Tumor Spheroids.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is the most aggressive primary tumor of the central nervous system and remains associated with poor prognosis despite current therapies. Magnetic hyperthermia (MHT) mediated by superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) is a promising therapeutic approach; however, improvements in tumor targeting, colloidal stability, and translational applicability are still needed. This study aimed to develop dopamine-functionalized SPION conjugated with the cyclic cRGD peptide (SPION-DOPA/cRGD) to promote preferential association with GBM cells and evaluate their physicochemical properties, cellular affinity, and therapeutic performance for MHT using a planar coil system. Methods: SPIONs were synthesized by thermal decomposition, functionalized with dopamine, and conjugated with cRGD. Their morphological, structural, magnetic, colloidal, and magnetothermal properties were characterized. Cellular affinity was evaluated in U87MG and HUVECs by Prussian Blue staining and Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS), and free-cRGD competition was used to assess RGD-integrin-mediated association. Biocompatibility and therapeutic efficacy were assessed by bioluminescence assays in U87MG spheroids following MHT. Results: SPION-DOPA/cRGD exhibited quasi-spherical morphology, cores below 10 nm, superparamagnetic behavior, and relatively consistent hydrodynamic diameters over 120 min in both water and DMEM/F12. The cRGD-containing formulation exhibited enhanced cellular association with U87MG cells while maintaining low interaction with HUVECs; free-cRGD competition reduced nanoparticle association, supporting RGD-integrin interactions. Under a 300 G field, nanoparticles reached 42-45 °C, with a specific absorption rate of 210 ± 19 W g-1. The nanoformulation showed low cytotoxicity from 20 to 5000 μg Fe mL-1, with viability above 96%. SPION-DOPA/cRGD-mediated MHT reduced U87MG spheroid viability to 14.76 ± 1.02%, whereas AMF alone did not affect viability compared with controls. Conclusions: SPION-DOPA/cRGD combines preferential cellular association with U87MG cells, efficient magnetic heating, and a substantial reduction in spheroid viability in a three-dimensional tumor model. Together with a planar coil, these findings support the translational potential of this nanoplatform for preclinical MHT applications in GBM.

articles.title: Cannabidiol-Loaded Mesoporous Silica SBA-15: Physicochemical Characterization and Biological Evaluation in 2D and 3D Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Models.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cannabidiol (CBD) exhibits cytotoxic activity against cancer cells, but its poor aqueous solubility may limit its pharmaceutical application. This study investigated Santa Barbara Amorphous No. 15 (SBA-15) mesoporous silica as a CBD carrier and evaluated its biological effects in A549 and HCC827 non-small cell lung cancer cell lines using 2D and 3D culture models. Methods: SBA-15 was loaded with 40 or 50 wt% CBD by melt infiltration and characterized by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Free and SBA-15-loaded CBD were evaluated using the PrestoBlue assay in 2D cultures, live/dead fluorescence imaging in 3D spheroids, and YO-PRO-1/PI flow cytometry. Preliminary short-term survival was assessed in Galleria mellonella larvae at a single dose, with five larvae per group. Results: The mesoporous structure of SBA-15 was preserved after CBD loading. At 40 wt%, CBD was predominantly amorphous and confined within the pores, whereas at 50 wt%, partial crystallization outside the silica matrix was observed. The PrestoBlue results indicated that A549 cells were more sensitive than HCC827 cells to the CBD-containing formulations. SBA-15 alone did not reduce cell viability. Both cell lines were less sensitive under 3D conditions. Flow cytometry demonstrated increased membrane permeabilization, with limited YO-PRO-1-positive/PI-negative populations. No reduction in larval survival was observed under the tested conditions. Conclusions: CBD loading affected its physical state within SBA-15 but did not substantially alter its cytotoxic activity in 2D cultures. Whether SBA-15 improves CBD dissolution remains to be determined. Biological responses depended on the cell line and culture dimensionality. Unloaded SBA-15 did not markedly reduce cellular metabolic activity, and no larval mortality was observed at the single tested dose. Cancer selectivity could not be assessed because non-malignant lung cells were not included.

articles.title: 3p-C-NETA: A Versatile Theranostic Chelator Platform Enabling Al18F- and 177Lu-Labeled SSTR2-Targeted Radioligands.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The FDA and EMA approvals of the theranostic radiopharmaceuticals [68Ga]Ga-/[177Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE represent milestones in SSTR2-targeted radioligand development. The use of a single precursor for both diagnostic and therapeutic applications facilitates the development of matched theranostic agents. However, the DOTA chelator is not compatible with fluorine-18 (Al18F) labeling, which offers advantages in terms of imaging quality and clinical logistics. Here, we evaluated 3p-C-NETA-TATE, a precursor capable of incorporating either Al18F or lutetium-177, building on previous work establishing 3p-C-NETA as a versatile theranostic chelator platform. Methods: The precursor 3p-C-NETA-TATE was labeled with Al18F or lutetium-177, and both compounds were evaluated in a preclinical setting. Both radioligands were assessed in vitro (binding affinity) and ex vivo (biodistribution) to determine their equivalent biological behavior. [177Lu]Lu-3p-C-NETA-TATE was compared with [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE in terms of labeling efficiency, stability and cytotoxicity. Additionally, [18F]AlF-3p-C-NETA-TATE was used in a PET imaging study with tumor-bearing mice. Results: [177Lu]Lu-3p-C-NETA-TATE was obtained in quantitative radiolabeling yields (>95%) at a lower temperature and precursor concentration compared with [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE, albeit with reduced stability in serum. In vitro, [177Lu]Lu-3p-C-NETA-TATE demonstrated comparable or improved characteristics. Both in vitro affinity experiments and ex vivo biodistribution studies indicated a similar biological profile for [18F]AlF-/[177Lu]Lu-3p-C-NETA-TATE. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the theranostic potential of the 3p-C-NETA platform using TATE as a model targeting vector. The ability to support both Al18F and lutetium-177 labeling, combined with the comparable biological behavior of the resulting radioligands, highlights its potential as a versatile platform for the development of next-generation diagnostic and therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Development and Optimization of Phoenix dactylifera Flavonoid-Loaded Mucoadhesive Nanoparticles for Mucosal Administration and Oral Cancer Cytotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Background and Objective: Mucosal cancers present significant therapeutic challenges due to limited drug permeation, rapid clearance and poor retention at epithelial sites. To overcome these limitations, this study developed and optimized Ajwa Extract Flavonoids Chitosan Mucoadhesive Nanoparticles (AEF-CMNP) from Phoenix dactylifera L. for localized mucosal delivery. Methods: Flavonoids were extracted from Ajwa dates and characterized using LC-MS, FTIR, and 1H/13C-NMR techniques. Nanoparticles were formulated via the ionic gelation method using chitosan and sodium tripolyphosphate (TPP), followed by systematic optimization using a Box-Behnken design (BBD) based Design of Experiments (DoE) approach. In vitro release profiles and 3-month stability studies were conducted. Cytotoxicity was evaluated via MTT assay across primary human oral keratinocytes (HOK), fibroblasts, and malignant cell lines including TR146 (buccal), CAL-27 (tongue), and HEp-2. Results: Characterization confirmed quercetin as the major flavonoid component. The optimized AEF-CMNP formulation exhibited a particle size of 226 nm, a PDI of 0.201 ± 0.01, a zeta potential of +24.8 mV and an encapsulation efficiency of 79.2%. Physicochemical analyses indicated non-covalent interactions and partial amorphization of the encapsulated compounds. In vitro drug release followed a controlled, biphasic pattern, characterized by an initial burst release of surface-associated flavonoids followed by sustained diffusion-controlled release from the chitosan matrix, achieving 93.50 ± 1.68 cumulative release within 48 h. Stability studies confirmed minimal variation in nanoparticle properties over three months, particularly under refrigerated conditions. Comparative cytotoxicity assays demonstrated significantly enhanced efficacy for AEF-CMNP compared to free flavonoids and control groups, yielding IC50 values of 54.9 µg/mL in TR146 cells and 43.7 µg/mL in CAL-27 cells. Conclusions: The developed AEF-CMNP system offers an effective and stable platform for delivering plant-derived bioactive, demonstrating strong potential for localized mucosal cancer therapy through improved cellular uptake and sustained retention. Further in vivo mechanism-based studies are warranted to validate clinical utility.

articles.title: Machine-Learning-Guided Identification of Potent Osimertinib Analogues Targeting the EGFR Triple Mutant.
articles.abstract: Background: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations, including exon 19 deletions and L858R, are major drivers of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although osimertinib is an established EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), the emergence of T790M and C797S mutations can reduce its effectiveness. This study aimed to identify and computationally prioritize osimertinib analogues with potential activity against the EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S triple mutant using an integrated machine-learning-assisted cheminformatics and structure-based approach. Methods: A library of 297,420 osimertinib analogues retrieved from PubChem was represented using physicochemical descriptors and 2048-bit Morgan fingerprints. Principal component analysis, t-SNE, UMAP, K-means clustering, and HDBSCAN were used to characterize chemical space, while Tanimoto similarity and Isolation Forest analysis were applied to assess structural similarity and scaffold novelty. Shortlisted compounds were subsequently evaluated using Glide extra-precision (XP) docking, induced-fit docking (IFD), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Results: K-means analysis identified an osimertinib-containing cluster comprising 17,149 compounds, providing a focused chemical space for analogue prioritization. A clear inverse relationship was observed between Tanimoto similarity to osimertinib and quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED) among the top 30 compounds (Pearson's r = -0.86). Three compounds satisfied the predefined combination of Tanimoto similarity ≥ 0.4 and QED ≥ 0.5. Subsequent molecular modelling highlighted compounds 155515815 and 122474632, together with osimertinib, as compounds exhibiting favorable and stable interactions with key EGFR residues. MD simulations further supported the stability of the protein-ligand complexes, while DFT analysis provided additional insight into their electronic and molecular properties. Conclusions: The integrated machine-learning-assisted and structure-based workflow enabled systematic exploration of a large osimertinib analogue library and identified computationally prioritized candidates for further investigation against the EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S triple mutant. Compounds 155515815 and 122474632 showed favorable computational profiles across multiple analyses and may serve as starting points for further scaffold optimization. Experimental studies are required to determine their biological activity and potential to address osimertinib resistance.

articles.title: Validation-Dependent Accuracy and Limited Zero-Shot Transfer: A Cross-Database Audit of Lipid Nanoparticle Performance Prediction.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Machine learning models are increasingly used to prioritize lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations, but apparent accuracy may depend strongly on dataset heterogeneity and validation design. This study audited two public LNP resources to determine how database consistency, source study signatures, chemical similarity, and experimental-domain shift affect predictive transportability. Methods: LNPDB and LNP Atlas were harmonized using a provenance-preserving canonical schema, standardized molecular structures, and conservative cross-database formulation matching. Source publication identity was predicted after direct bibliographic identifiers were removed. Biological-performance modeling used 17,420 study-normalized gene expression/luminescence records from 37 LNPDB studies and fixed LightGBM models evaluated under random-row, formulation-held-out, ionizable-lipid-connectivity-held-out, structural-similarity-cluster-held-out, study-held-out, and temporal validation. Results: Only 29 of 217 Atlas formulation clusters from shared publications were confirmed as complete-formulation matches. Source publication was identified with 99.94% accuracy in LNPDB, while experimental context alone achieved 99.05% accuracy in LNP Atlas. Random-row validation yielded R2 = 0.317 and ROC-AUC = 0.815. Performance decreased under connectivity holdout (R2 = 0.239; ROC-AUC = 0.761) and structural-similarity holdout (R2 = 0.035; ROC-AUC = 0.654) and was poor for unseen studies (R2 = 22120.070; ROC-AUC = 0.531) and later studies (R2 = -0.217; ROC-AUC = 0.528). Test-independent binary endpoint sensitivity reproduced the same hierarchy. Conclusions: Public LNP datasets contain strong source study signatures and substantial chemical and experimental heterogeneity. In the evaluated LightGBM and Ridge baseline models, predictive performance was strongly dependent on validation design, with limited zero-shot generalization to unseen publications and later experimental domains. These findings do not establish that the same degree of performance deterioration would occur with pretrained, graph-based, or domain-adapted LNP models. Structure-aware, publication-grouped, and temporal validation should therefore accompany claims of predictive generalization beyond the training domain.

articles.title: Phytochemical Characterization, Electronic Reactivity and Anticancer Evaluation of Symphyotrichum novi-belgii.
articles.abstract: Background: Symphyotrichum novi-belgii (syn. Aster novi-belgii) belongs to the Asteraceae family and remains comparatively underexplored from a phytochemical and pharmacological perspective. Symphyotrichum novi-belgii remains poorly characterized in terms of organ-specific phytochemistry and anticancer relevance. Methods: In this study, methanolic extracts of the leaves, stems and roots of Symphyotrichum novi-belgii were characterized using FTIR and GC-MS. Selected phytoconstituents were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and molecular docking against HPV16 E6, while the effects of the crude extracts on HeLa cervical cancer cells were assessed using the MTT cell-viability assay following treatment with each extract at 100 µg/mL for 48 h. The chemical and computational findings were considered alongside the MTT cell-viability results to compare the leaf (Lf), stem (St) and root (Rt) extracts of S. novi-belgii and identify phytoconstituents warranting further investigation. Results: FTIR spectra revealed hydroxyl, carbonyl, aromatic, aliphatic, and C-O/C-O-C functionalities. GC-MS detected nine chromatographic features each in the Lf and St extracts and seven in the Rt extract, representing chemical classes such as organic and phenolic acids, flavonoid-type compounds, terpenoids, an alkaloid, nitrogen-containing heterocycles, lactones, ethers, and a fatty-acid ester. DFT calculations on selected proposed molecular structures indicated the highest calculated molecular softness for the sanguinarine model (Lf8; 0.831 eV-1) and the highest electrophilicity index for the caftaric-acid model (Rt6; 4.356 eV). Separately, the proposed flavonol-type molecular structure represented by Lf5 (leaf), St6 (stem), and Rt4 (root) was distinct from the sanguinarine model (Lf8). The original docking calculations reported predicted binding scores of -10.4 kcal/mol for the Lf5 and Rt4 model entries. However, discrepancies between the original library-search results and the corresponding literature-assisted GC-MS assignments prevent confirmation that these molecular structures were present in the extracts. The computational results therefore represent theoretical predictions for the selected structures rather than verified properties of experimentally identified plant constituents. In the preliminary MTT evaluation at 100 µg/mL following 48 h of exposure, the Lf extract showed 31.03% inhibition, whereas the Rt and St extracts yielded -12.98% and -10.61%, respectively. None of the extracts reached 50% inhibition at the concentration tested. Because no concentration-response series was performed, extract-specific IC50 values could not be determined. Doxorubicin, included as the positive drug control, showed 81.81% apparent MTT inhibition under the reported single-concentration conditions. Conclusions: FTIR and exploratory GC-MS analyses revealed differences in the detectable chemical features of the three extracts, while DFT and molecular docking provided theoretical predictions for selected proposed molecular structures. At 100 µg/mL following 48 h of exposure, the leaf (Lf) extract showed a higher apparent MTT percentage-inhibition value than the root (Rt) and stem (St) extracts. This single-concentration observation is descriptive and does not establish statistically significant differences, cytotoxicity, or anticancer efficacy.

articles.title: Formulation of Glycerol-Based Emulsion Containing Myrica gale L. Essential Oil for Enhanced Repellent Activity.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Glycerol-based emulsions containing Myrica gale L. essential oils (EOs) were developed and evaluated for stability, volatilisation behaviour and in vivo mosquito repellent activity. Preliminary GC-MS characterisation of the oils demonstrated complex chemical profiles comprised mainly of a mixture of mono- and sesquiterpenes. Methods: Emulsions containing 10% oil were prepared at two surfactant concentrations (2.5 and 5%) and differing ratios of glycerol to water as the non-polar phase. The optimal system was determined to be 10% oil and 2.5% surfactant (i.e., cetearyl alcohol and cetearyl glucoside) in 100% glycerol as assessed over a 91-day storage period by changes in particle size, polydispersity and zeta potential. This formulation approach was subsequently applied to three proven insect repellent M. gale EOs. Volatilisation behaviour was investigated using headspace GC-MS analysis of selected marker compounds (α-pinene, camphene, β-pinene, myrcene, α-phellandrene, 3-carene, p-cymene, γ-terpinene). Results: M. gale-based emulsions demonstrated significantly improved volatilisation over time, compared with the EO coarsely dispersed in a lotion base. This enhanced partitioning behaviour correlated well with increased protection times observed in an arm-in-cage repellent assay against Aedes aegypti mosquitos. It was found that all formulated M.gale EOs, F_EO15M (CPT = 40.05 min, p = 0.032), F_EO21C (CPT = 42.023 min, p = 0.01) and F_EO15C (CPT = 99.478 min, p < 0.0001), performed significantly better than their non-formulated counterparts EO15M (CPT = 11.45 min), EO21C (CPT = 13.053 min) and EO15C (CPT = 33.02 min). Conclusion: This study describes for the first time an effective, topical M. gale-loaded emulsion for the improvement of insect repellent activity.

articles.title: Biological Activities of the Biochanin A Inclusion Complex with 2-Hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin and Molecular Modeling.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Biochanin A belongs to the isoflavone group of phytoestrogens with numerous beneficial effects on human health. Its application in therapy is significantly limited by low aqueous solubility and bioavailability. Cyclodextrin inclusion complexes are used in pharmaceutical formulations to improve the unfavorable properties of the active substance while maintaining its activity. The aim of this work was to examine the influence of complexation with 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) on the biological activities of biochanin A. The antimicrobial activity of biochanin A and the inclusion complex against Helicobacter pylori was tested using disc diffusion and micro-well dilution assays. Methods: The antioxidant activity of biochanin A and its inclusion complex was examined using radical scavenging (DPPH and ABTS), reducing power (CUPRAC and FRAP), phosphomolybdenum, and metal-chelating assays. The inhibitory activity on enzymes α-amylase, α-glucosidase, tyrosinase, and cholinesterases was also evaluated. Results: The inclusion complex showed stronger antimicrobial activity against H. pylori (MIC = 1.9 mg/mL) than biochanin A itself (MIC = 7.5 mg/mL). Both biochanin A and its inclusion complex showed weak, dose-dependent radical-scavenging activity. The inclusion complex inhibited cholinesterases, whereas free biochanin A did not; the possible contribution of HPβCD itself requires further study. Conclusions: The enhanced activity of biochanin A after complexation may enable the development of more effective formulations.

articles.title: In Situ Salt Formation in a Solid SNEDDS: A Triple Solubilizing, Stabilizing, and Dose-Reducing Strategy Enabling Single-Capsule Glibenclamide Administration.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Liquid self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery systems (L-SNEDDSs) efficiently improve oral bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs. However, adsorption onto mesoporous carriers often doubles the formulation mass and locks patients into multi-capsule regimens. This study aimed to develop a solid SNEDDS for glibenclamide (GLB), a weakly acidic, acid-labile, poorly soluble antidiabetic drug, using sodium carbonate as a multifunctional alkalizing excipient to enhance drug loading, improve chemical stability, and enable single-capsule administration. Methods: L-SNEDDSs were prepared using Tween 80, PEG 400, and Imwitor 308 (4:3:3, w/w). Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) was benchmarked against triethanolamine as an alkalizing agent intended to promote in situ ionization (salt formation) of GLB. The optimized liquid was adsorbed onto Syloid (mesoporous silica) at a 1:1 (w/w) ratio to produce a free-flowing solid SNEDDS. Drug loading, dissolution, degradation kinetics at 40 °C and chemical stability at room temperature were evaluated. Results: Sodium carbonate incorporation significantly increased GLB solubility from 5.97 to 17.42 mg/g (2.9-fold increase, p < 0.01), outperforming triethanolamine (1.1-fold). The alkalized formulation extended the drug half-life at 40 °C from 12.4 to 30.1 days (2.4-fold, p < 0.01). Increasing drug loading in L-SNEDDSs from 5 to 15 mg/g maintained rapid in vitro dissolution, with >84% drug released within 10 min and similar dissolution efficiency (DE) across 5-15 mg/g despite tripling the drug content. The optimized solid (15 mg/g) achieved a 21.9-fold improvement in dissolution efficiency (p < 0.01) vs. raw drug. Moreover, it reduced total powder mass from 1000 to 333 mg and enabled single-capsule administration. Both liquid and solid alkalized SNEDDSs significantly enhanced GLB stability compared to the plain liquid SNEDDS. Conclusions: Overall, Na2CO3-enabled in situ ionization offers a practical, single-step approach to simultaneously mitigate poor solubility, acid-lability, and dose-volume limitations in solid SNEDDSs, providing a promising platform for improved oral delivery and potentially better patient adherence for weakly acidic, acid-labile drugs.

articles.title: An Exploratory Model-Informed Precision Dosing Strategy for Atomoxetine Treatment in Chinese Children with ADHD: Integrating Body Weight and CYP2D6 Pharmacogenetics Across Potential Real-World Clinical Scenarios.
articles.abstract: Objective: We aimed to develop and evaluate population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) models of atomoxetine incorporating clinically available patient information and to explore model-informed dose selection in Chinese children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Methods: This retrospective single-center study included a model-building dataset of 102 patients (247 concentrations) and a patient-level holdout dataset of 65 patients (65 concentrations collected approximately 2 h post-dose). A one-compartment model with first-order absorption and elimination was developed. Body weight (BW) and alternative representations of CYP2D6 genetic information-rs1065852 genotype, activity score (AS), and predicted phenotype-were evaluated. Monte Carlo simulations evaluated steady-state 2 h post-dose concentrations (C2h) across doses of 0.5-1.4 mg/kg/day; the model-informed dose was the lowest evaluated dose, achieving ≥75% probability of reaching the exploratory C2h threshold of 268 ng/mL. Results: BW affected apparent clearance (CL/F) and volume of distribution, whereas rs1065852 genotype and AS additionally explained CL/F variability. In the holdout dataset, population predictions had limited bias (MdPE, 1.41-3.09%) but modest precision (MdAPE, 33.75-37.83%); CYP2D6-informed models improved selected performance measures. Simulation-derived doses ranged from 1.0 to 1.4 mg/kg/day across subgroups. No evaluated dose achieved the probability of target attainment (PTA) criterion for AS = 2 at any BW, or for the CC+CT and AS = 1.5 subgroups weighing 17-<30 kg. Alternative Ka assumptions changed median C2h by at most 3.99% and PTA by 3.58 percentage points. Conclusions: BW and CYP2D6 genetic information explained part of atomoxetine pharmacokinetic variability and influenced simulated concentration attainment. These model-informed findings are exploratory and require prospective, multicenter validation against efficacy, tolerability, and safety outcomes before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Tailoring Immediate-Release Tablet Dissolution via Geometrically Tunable 3D-Printed Polymeric Coats.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Conventional modification of drug release often requires reformulation of the drug-containing dosage form. This study investigated fused deposition modelling (FDM) 3D-printed polymeric coats as external barriers for modifying the dissolution of intact immediate-release tablets without reformulating the drug-containing core. Methods: Commercial tablets were encapsulated within 3D-printed polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) or polylactic acid (PLA) coats incorporating a continuous axial channel with surface apertures of 0, 4.5, or 9 mm diameter. Printing accuracy and dimensional fidelity were evaluated, followed by dissolution testing. Release profiles were characterized using zero-order, first-order, Higuchi, Weibull, and Korsmeyer-Peppas models. Results: Printed coats showed high dimensional fidelity. Fully enclosed PVA coats produced a prolonged lag phase followed by rapid release associated with coat hydration and loss of structural integrity, whereas fully enclosed PLA coats showed no detectable drug release over 6 h. Increasing aperture diameter increased release from both polymers, although the magnitude and pattern of release differed markedly between PVA and PLA. At 2 h, PVA coats with 4.5 and 9 mm apertures released 89.5 ± 10.4% and 97.0 ± 15.6%, respectively, compared with 1.90 ± 0.13% and 58.8 ± 9.5% from the corresponding PLA designs. Korsmeyer-Peppas analysis indicated apparent anomalous release for PVA 4.5 mm (n = 0.647) and PLA 9 mm (n = 0.711), while PVA 9 mm exhibited Super Case-II-like behavior (n = 1.214). Conclusions: FDM-printed external polymeric coats can substantially modify dissolution from intact immediate-release tablets. Release behavior depended on the interaction between aperture geometry and polymer properties, demonstrating the potential of external 3D-printed barriers as a flexible approach for tailoring drug-release profiles without reformulating the tablet core.

articles.title: A Novel Salcaprozate Sodium Deep Eutectic System for Oral Semaglutide Delivery and Enhanced Skin Penetration.
articles.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes is a chronic metabolic disease increasingly treated with peptide therapeutics, yet their clinical use remains largely dependent on subcutaneous injection, compromising adherence and causing injection-related complications. Here, we developed a novel formulation to enhance oral semaglutide delivery and its penetration into skin tissue. Methods: This novel system was composed of betaine, glycerol, and sodium salcaprozate (SNAC) and was termed BGS, forming a deep eutectic solvent. Results: The BGS drug delivery system markedly suppressed semaglutide aggregation, shifting the peak particle size from 125.9 nm in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to 51.7 nm. It also enhanced semaglutide transport across Caco-2 monolayers, increasing the apparent permeability by 4.22-fold relative to PBS. In ex vivo porcine skin, BGS enhanced semaglutide penetration and accumulation, with the amount retained in skin reaching 86.34 ± 6.12 μg/cm2 at 24 h, approximately 4.51 times that with PBS. Following oral administration, BGS-formulated semaglutide achieved 1.02 ± 0.05% bioavailability, 14.57 times that of oral semaglutide. Compared with commercial formulation, oral semaglutide reached similar bioavailability, with a 74.5% SNAC decrease helping the formation of BGS via supramolecular interactions. In obese and diabetic mice, BGS effectively suppressed body weight gain and ameliorated hyperglycemia. BGS also showed favorable biocompatibility, with 0.25 ± 0.29% hemolysis and cell viability above 83% at 500 μg/mL. Conclusions: Overall, these findings demonstrate that BGS combines peptide stabilization, enhanced intestinal transport, and improved semaglutide accumulation within skin tissue, highlighting its potential for peptide delivery.

articles.title: Using Advanced Cubic Modeling to Explore the Formulation Design Space of Nanostructured Lipid Carriers: An Exploratory Retrospective Approach.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) are promising systems for targeted drug delivery; however, tailoring their formulation frequently requires resource-intensive empirical methods. In this study, a retrospective Quality-by-Design (QbD) approach was applied to systematically evaluate the NLC design space. Methods: Using a pooled historical dataset of 99 experimental runs, cubic and reduced quadratic models were constructed to assess the effects of solid lipid (X1), liquid lipid (X2), and surfactant (X3) concentrations on critical quality attributes: particle size (Y1), polydispersity index (Y2), and encapsulation efficiency (Y3). Results: Due to the inherent heterogeneity of the retrospective data, statistical assessment indicated certain limitations in exact point predictability. Nevertheless, the models effectively identified major macroscopic trends and key factor interactions, serving as practical tools with which to outline the broad boundaries of the design space. Specifically, the polydispersity index (PDI) model exhibited limited estimation capacity (predicted R2 = 0.36) and a significant lack of fit, indicating that it captures general macroscopic variations rather than providing precise mathematical estimations. The generated 3D response surfaces demonstrated the importance of high surfactant concentrations in maintaining nanoscale dimensions by counteracting viscosity-induced particle growth as well as the synergistic effect of the solid-liquid lipid matrix in promoting the formation of lattice defects and thus enhancing drug entrapment. A desirability approach (0.939) identified a targeted formulation composition (approximately 3.5% solid lipid, 2.1% liquid lipid, and 11.3% surfactant), which is presented as an exploratory candidate region requiring experimental confirmation. Under these parameters, the model estimated a particle size of approximately 88 nm, a narrow size distribution (PDI = 0.20), and an encapsulation efficiency enhanced within the thermodynamic limits of the lipid matrix. Conclusions: In conclusion, integrating historical data analysis with advanced polynomial modeling yielded a systematically evaluated framework for the preliminary design of NLCs. This framework offers a preliminary computational perspective that may complement traditional formulation strategies in the early stages of nanocarrier development.

articles.title: A Biopredictive Fed-State Dissolution Method Incorporating High-Viscosity Media and Hydrodynamic Stress.
articles.abstract: Background: Postprandial gastric conditions such as changed motility and increased viscosity of gastric content can interact with an ingested dosage form, such as a tablet. This can affect the mechanisms of disintegration and dissolution and result in the altered performance of the tablet. Hereby, the individual characteristics of the tablet play a crucial role, since they determine the interaction potential with hydrodynamic and physico-chemical properties of the gastric environment. Excipient properties such as solubility, swellability, or gelling tendency can have an influence. Further, tablet characteristics such as porosity or pore size can affect its breakdown by regulating water uptake or determining its physical stability. Methods: Four midodrine hydrochloride generic products with known in vivo bioequivalence, but different formulations, were used as references to improve the simulated fed-state disintegration and dissolution testing methods involving highly viscous media. The tablet samples were evaluated towards the aforementioned characteristics, estimating which parameters of the testing method influence their dissolution performance under highly viscous conditions. Hereby, different hydrodynamic and mechanical stresses were simulated by a previously presented computed numerical controlled apparatus, as well as a novel flow-through cell for viscous media. By a mechanistic biopharmaceutics modeling approach, the convoluted dissolution data were compared to in vivo plasma profiles. Results: A sequential motion method yielded similar dissolution profiles as assessed by the similarity factor (f2). Convoluted plasma profiles showed good approximation with the in vivo profiles. Conclusions: The sequential dissolution method was established as a biopredictive tool for simulating the fed state by incorporating physiologically increased postprandial chyme viscosity and hydrodynamic stress.

articles.title: Isoliquiritigenin-Loaded Solid Nanoparticles Embedded in Sodium Alginate/Chitosan/Squid Ink Polysaccharide Hydrogel for Oral Colon-Targeted Therapy of Colitis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Isoliquiritigenin (ISL) possesses excellent anti-inflammatory and colonic mucosal repair activities, showing promising potential for colitis treatment. However, the clinical application of native ISL is severely restricted by its poor water solubility, low in vivo bioavailability, and insufficient colon tissue accumulation. To solve these inherent delivery defects of free ISL, this study aimed to construct a novel oral colon-targeted solid nanoparticle-hydrogel composite delivery system and explore its therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms for colitis therapy. Methods: ISL-loaded poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid)/polycaprolactone solid nanoparticles (IPP NPs) were first fabricated to improve the water solubility and in vivo delivery efficiency of free ISL. Thereafter, IPP NPs were encapsulated into a composite hydrogel network consisting of sodium alginate, chitosan, and squid ink polysaccharide to prepare the colon-targeted IPP@Gels. The pH-responsive drug release behavior of the composite system in the upper gastrointestinal tract was verified via in vitro characterization experiments. A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced murine colitis model was established to evaluate the in vivo therapeutic effects of IPP@Gels. The regulatory effects of the delivery system on intestinal tight junction protein expression, proinflammatory cytokine levels, gut microbiota composition, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) content were further investigated. Results: The constructed IPP@Gels exhibited favorable pH-responsive performance, which effectively inhibited the premature release of ISL in the upper gastrointestinal tract and achieved precise colon localization and sustained drug release. In vivo experimental results demonstrated that IPP@Gels significantly alleviated the pathological symptoms of colitis in model mice. Mechanistically, the composite system prominently upregulated the expression of intestinal tight junction proteins, reduced the secretion of proinflammatory cytokines, effectively enriched ISL accumulation in colon tissues, reversed gut microbiota dysbiosis, and increased the content of intestinal SCFAs, thereby producing synergistic anti-colitis therapeutic effects. Conclusions: The constructed SA/CS/SIP composite hydrogel (IPP@Gels), embedded with ISL-loaded nanoparticles, exhibits favorable biocompatibility and pH-responsive release behavior, enabling colon-localized retention of ISL. This novel oral drug delivery system mitigates several delivery-related drawbacks of free ISL and confers beneficial therapeutic effects in experimental colitis. It provides a feasible oral formulation strategy for colon-localized delivery of poorly soluble drugs and offers promising prospects for the management of colitis.

articles.title: Direct Surface Engineering of Oncolytic Adenovirus with Targeted Antibody and Chemotherapeutics for HER2-Targeted Chemo-Virotherapy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Systemic delivery of oncolytic adenovirus (oAd) remains a major challenge due to rapid immune clearance, hepatic sequestration, and off-target toxicity. To overcome these barriers and enhance tumor-targeting efficacy, we developed Ad-DTX/HER, a novel viral complex engineered by directly co-conjugating the cytotoxic agent docetaxel (DTX) and the site-specifically modified HER2-targeting antibody trastuzumab (Herceptin, HER) onto the oAd surface. Methods: DTX and trastuzumab were site-specifically conjugated onto the naked viral capsid in a polymer-free manner, and the resulting Ad-DTX/HER complex was characterized for size distribution and structural integrity. Its HER2 selectivity and oncolytic activity were evaluated in cancer cells, and its biodistribution and organ toxicity were assessed following systemic administration in tumor-bearing mice. Results: Ad-DTX/HER exhibited a uniform size distribution, sustained structural integrity, and remarkable selectivity toward HER2-overexpressing cancer cells without compromising viral oncolytic activity. Systemic administration in tumor-bearing mice drastically minimized non-specific hepatic uptake while significantly enhancing tumor accumulation, achieving a marked ~2800-fold increase in the tumor-to-liver ratio compared to naked oAd. Histopathological analysis of major organs indicated that systemic administration of Ad-DTX/HER is not associated with overt off-target organ toxicity. Conclusions: This polymer-free, direct capsid-engineering platform provides an effective systemic delivery paradigm, offering potent synergistic chemo-virotherapy for HER2-positive tumor.

articles.title: Biomimetic Cascade Nanozymes: Superoxide Dismutase-Templated Ultrasmall Iron Oxide for Liver Fibrosis Therapy and MRI-Assisted Staging.
articles.abstract: Background: Liver fibrosis represents a critical pathological juncture in the progression of chronic liver disease toward irreversible cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma; however, early diagnosis and effective therapeutic intervention remain significant clinical challenges. Methods: Herein, we report a biomimetic cascade nanozyme platform (termed iSOD) featuring a core-shell nanostructure for the accurate diagnosis and therapy of liver fibrosis. Synthesized via a green, one-pot coprecipitation method utilizing natural superoxide dismutase (SOD) as a structural template, the iSOD comprises an ultrasmall Fe3O4 core (approximately 4.04 nm in diameter) seamlessly enveloped by an active SOD protein shell. Results: This unique architecture provides the SOD-mediated superoxide-scavenging activity and catalase (CAT)-like activity from the ultrasmall iron oxide core. This sequential dual-enzyme cascade can eliminate deleterious reactive oxygen species (ROS) by dismutating superoxide anions and decomposing intermediate hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) into water and oxygen. In vitro evaluations demonstrate that iSOD significantly diminishes intracellular ROS in HSC-T6 cells and protects them against oxidative stress-induced injury. Relaxivity measurements revealed longitudinal (r1) and transverse (r2) relaxivities of 2.874 and 13.878 mM-1 s-1, respectively, indicating the ability of iSOD to influence both T1 and T2 relaxation. In vivo, T1-weighted MRI revealed changes in hepatic signal intensity and spatial distribution 30 min after iSOD administration, with distinct signal patterns observed among healthy, moderately fibrotic, and severely fibrotic rat livers. Histological analyses further demonstrated reduced collagen deposition and improved hepatic tissue morphology following iSOD treatment. Short-term biocompatibility evaluations revealed no obvious adverse effects under the investigated conditions. Conclusions: Collectively, these findings highlight the potential of iSOD as a multifunctional nanoplatform integrating antioxidant therapy with MRI-based assessment of liver fibrosis.

articles.title: Enhancing Thermal Longevity and Transdermal Delivery of High-Dose Vitamin C: The Role of Particle-Reinforced Thixotropic Networks in Anhydrous Matrices.
articles.abstract: Background: Topical delivery of high-dose L-ascorbic acid (AA) is limited by rapid oxidative degradation in water and physical particle aggregation in lipophilic vehicles. Here, we engineered an anhydrous delivery system combining a structured wax-oil matrix with high-shear roll-milling process to stabilize up to 40% AA. Methods: Dispersion morphology and 3D ultrastructure were evaluated via optical microscopy and Cryo-SEM. Rheological flow profiles and thixotropic recovery were measured using a rotational rheometer. Accelerated chemical stability was monitored at 0-50 °C for 4 weeks via RP-HPLC. Percutaneous delivery kinetics were investigated across synthetic biomimetic membranes (Strat-M®) using a sequential toner-application regimen. Biological efficacy was clinically assessed in 15 human volunteers over 4 weeks using 3D optical skin analysis (ANTERA 3D®). Results: The high-shear roll-milling process homogenized AA aggregates into micro-dispersions, establishing an apparent yield-stress network with an ultra-high zero-shear plateau (105 P) and shear-thinning thixotropy. The milled formulation retained highly stable chemical potency (93.99%) at 50 °C for 4 weeks. Sequential application with an aqueous toner facilitated in situ active dissolution at the barrier interface, increasing the absolute delivered payload from the 20% system by >10.5-fold relative to the 5% formulation. A 4-week clinical evaluation confirmed measurable improvements in skin brightness (∆L* = 1.66%), and reductions in hyper-pigmentation (25.65%), wrinkle area (31.17%), and pore area (26.00%). Conclusions: The milling-integrated anhydrous matrix provides a robust formulation framework that resolves physical sedimentation and oxidative instability while enabling the stable delivery of high-dose payloads via enhanced thermodynamic concentration gradients for enhanced dermatological rejuvenation.

articles.title: A Shorter Switching Interval from Intravitreal Dexamethasone Implant to Intravitreal Fluocinolone Acetonide Implant Improves Clinical Outcomes in Diabetic Macular Edema.
articles.abstract: Background: This study aimed to evaluate whether a shorter switching interval from intravitreal dexamethasone implant (DEXi) to intravitreal fluocinolone acetonide implant (FAci) improves anatomical and functional outcomes in patients with diabetic macular edema. Methods: This was a retrospective, multicenter, observational extension study including 260 eyes, with a mean follow-up of 141.6 ± 55.4 weeks. Results: Prior to FAci injection, 100% of eyes had received DEXi. The mean interval between the last DEXi and the first FAci was 24.2 ± 41.6 weeks (n = 188), i.e., 0-8 weeks in 54 eyes (28.7%) and >8 weeks in 134 eyes (71.3%). Mean BCVA was comparable between patients receiving their last DEXi ≤8 weeks and those receiving it >8 weeks prior to FAci. Compared to baseline, the ≤8-week group consistently and significantly showed lower central macular thickness (CMT) values at months 1-3, 6, 7, 9-11, 14, 16, 19, and 20 (p < 0.05). At months 12 and 24, 90 (34.6%) and 117 (45.0%) eyes required additional treatments, after a median time of 118 weeks (95% CI: 87.7-191.4). In the ≤8-week group, the normalized cumulative incidence of additional treatments was 0.33 treatments per eye at week 52 and 0.72 at week 104, versus 0.66 and 1.38 in the >8-week group, respectively. Intraocular pressure (IOP) elevation incidence did not significantly differ between the ≤8-week and >8-week groups, regardless of the IOP threshold used (≥25, ≥30, or ≥35 mmHg; all p > 0.05). Conclusions: A shorter interval between DEXi and FAci was associated with greater and sustained macular drying, along with a reduced need for additional treatments.

articles.title: Lipid Nanoparticles Enhance the Antichlamydial Efficacy of Ciprofloxacin and Sulfamethoxazole-Trimethoprim.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives:Chlamydia trachomatis (C. trachomatis) infections represent a major global public health concern, with over 100 million new cases annually. Although commonly used antibiotics like azithromycin and doxycycline are generally effective, increasing antibiotic resistance and therapeutic failures highlight the need for alternative treatments and innovative delivery systems. Methods: The efficacy of alternative antimicrobial agents, including ciprofloxacin and the combination of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim, was evaluated in both free and nano-formulated states. Drug encapsulation was achieved using liposomes as well as niosomal and aspasomal delivery systems. In vitro experiments were conducted on HeLa cells infected with C. trachomatis serovar D. Host cell viability and cytotoxicity were assessed using the MTT assay, while bacterial genomic load was quantified by qPCR. Results: Encapsulation significantly enhanced antimicrobial activity, with certain antibiotic-loaded lipid nanoparticles demonstrating 2-4 times greater effectiveness compared to their free counterparts. The prepared formulations exhibited no cytotoxic effects and did not interfere with PCR-based detection, confirming that observed outcomes reflect true antimicrobial activity. Conclusions: Nanocarrier-based drug delivery, particularly using lipid nanoparticles, represents a promising strategy for improving the therapeutic management of C. trachomatis infections. These findings highlight the potential of delivery platforms to enhance antibiotic performance and support the development of more effective and innovative antimicrobial therapies.

articles.title: In Vitro Antibacterial and Anti-Biofilm Activities of Rifampicin-Based Combinations Against Clinical Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Isolates: High Synergy with Rifampicin-Colistin.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is an important opportunistic pathogen with intrinsic multidrug resistance (MDR) and strong biofilm-forming ability. This study evaluated the in vitro antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities of rifampicin (RIF)-based combinations against 50 clinical S. maltophilia isolates, with a particular focus on those exhibiting colistin (COL) resistance. Methods: Antimicrobial susceptibility, biofilm formation, and RIF-based combinations were evaluated using broth microdilution, crystal violet, and checkerboard assays, respectively. RIF/COL synergy was further assessed by time-kill assays and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of mature biofilms. Results: The isolates showed susceptibility to levofloxacin (74.0%) and tigecycline (66.0%), whereas high resistance rates were observed for RIF (98.0%), COL (92.0%), and fosfomycin (84.0%). Overall, 98.0% of the isolates were phenotypically classified as MDR, and 92.0% were biofilm producers, of which 93.5% were classified as strong biofilm producers. Among the RIF-based combinations, RIF/COL exhibited the highest synergistic activity (90.0%), followed by RIF/tigecycline (20.0%). Time-kill kinetics demonstrated potent and sustained RIF/COL synergy against three representative isolates, achieving ≥2 log10 CFU/mL reductions starting at 4-8 h post-incubation. SEM revealed more pronounced structural alterations in established biofilms and more evident cellular damage following RIF/COL treatment than following either monotherapy. Conclusions: These in vitro findings support the further investigation of RIF/COL as a potential therapeutic combination against MDR S. maltophilia, particularly for isolates exhibiting high-level COL resistance and in the treatment of established biofilms.

articles.title: Anandamide Reduces the Capsaicin-Evoked Pain by Regulating TRPV1 Protein Levels.
articles.abstract: Background: Anandamide (AEA) is a lipid mediator of the endocannabinoid system that plays a key role in pain perception by regulating multiple molecular targets, including transient receptor potential vanilloid type 1 (TRPV1). This vanilloid receptor is abundantly expressed in nociceptive neurons (nociceptors) and plays a crucial role in mediating pain responses. Methods: We used mouse behavioral tests, cell culture, and Western blot assays to test whether AEA regulates acute pain induced by TRPV1 activation and TRPV1 total protein levels. Results: Our results demonstrate that AEA downregulates the capsaicin-evoked pain response and TRPV1 protein levels in nociceptors. Furthermore, in a transiently heterologous TRPV1 expression system, we found that AEA induces ubiquitination of TRPV1 and its degradation via the proteasome pathway, independent of calcium influx. We also found that AEA induced an upregulation of BiP protein levels, a key endoplasmic reticulum chaperone and stress sensor, without changes in other ER stress sensors. Finally, we explored whether the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG) and the phytocannabinoid β-caryophyllene (BCP) modulate capsaicin-evoked pain, finding that 2-AG is less effective than AEA in reducing pain behavior, whereas BCP shows effects similar to AEA in reducing capsaicin-evoked pain. Conclusions: These results highlight AEA and BCP as regulators of TRPV1 protein levels and of the painful response mediated by this molecular pain target.

articles.title: Evaluation of BPA-Bearing TAT-Lipopeptide-Modified Liposomes for Boron Neutron Capture Therapy from Cell-Associated Boron Delivery to In Vivo Tolerability.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Boron neutron capture therapy requires the efficient delivery of sufficient amounts of 10B to tumor cells. In this study, we evaluated a liposomal boron-delivery system based on the B5-TAT-lipopeptide, which contains five boronophenylalanine (BPA) residues within its peptide portion and is anchored to the liposomal membrane through a hydrophobic lipid moiety. Methods: B5-TAT-lipopeptide 5% liposomes with a particle size of approximately 100 nm were prepared, and boron delivery to CT26 murine colon carcinoma cells was evaluated. Results: At an exposure concentration of 25 ppm boron, B5-TAT-lipopeptide 5% liposomes achieved a cell-associated boron level of approximately 4.5 µg B per 1 × 106 cells. Separately, sodium mercaptoundecahydro-closo-dodecaborate (BSH)-encapsulated B5-TAT-lipopeptide 5% liposomes achieved approximately 11 µg B per 1 × 106 cells when evaluated at an exposure concentration of 50 ppm. Following thermal neutron irradiation, B5-TAT-lipopeptide 5% liposome-treated cells showed marked loss of clonogenic survival, with surviving fractions of approximately 0.12 and 0.01 after 15 and 45 min of irradiation, respectively. In the preliminary in vivo tolerability study, rapid intravenous administration of B5-TAT-lipopeptide 5% liposomes without encapsulated BSH at 10 mg B/kg resulted in the death of all treated mice within 5-10 min, whereas no mortality occurred following the administration of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), free BSH, or BSH-encapsulated PEGylated liposomes. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate substantial cell-associated boron delivery and neutron-induced clonogenic cell killing by B5-TAT-lipopeptide-modified liposomes while revealing a critical limitation in acute in vivo tolerability under the examined administration conditions.

articles.title: A Comparative Assessment of Smart Nanoselenium Hybrid Plurosomes for Augmenting Repaglinide Delivery Against Breast and Liver Cancer Treatment: D-Optimal Statistical Design, In Vitro Cytotoxicity, Biomarkers Assessment, and In Silico Studies.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Nanotherapeutics integrated with drug repurposing represent an emerging approach to overcome ongoing cancer treatment resistance, particularly in breast cancer (BC) and hepatoblastoma (HB). This study comparatively evaluated an optimally designed smart anticancer nanoselenium hybrid repaglinide (RG)-loaded plurosomes (SHPs) against MDA-MB-231 and HepG2 cell lines. Methods: SHPs were fabricated by the thin-film hydration method and optimized using D-optimal design to investigate the impact of formulation parameters, including Pluronic® amount, sonication time, and hydrophilic-lipophilic balance of Pluronic® on entrapment efficacy (EE%), particle size (PS), and zeta potential (ZP). Results: The optimum formulation (OP.SHP) exhibited high EE% (70.50 ± 1.86%), desired nanosize (242.90 ± 13.77 nm), and excellent stability (ZP = -66.40 ± 2.12 mV). The thermal profile of OP.SHP confirmed successful RG entrapment. The in vitro drug release profile demonstrated a pH-dependent behavior with enhanced drug release at pH 5.5 (91.29 ± 5.67% over 10 h) and a slower release rate at pH 7.4 than the RG suspension. The MTT assay showed cell line-dependent cytotoxicity, with OP.SHP showing stronger antiproliferative activity against MDA-MB-231 (IC50 = 107.50 µg/mL) than HepG2 cells (IC50 = 215.40 µg/mL), compared with RG suspension. Additionally, cell-cycle analysis revealed S and G2/M phase accumulation in MDA-MB-231 cells and S phase accumulation in HepG2 cells, indicating cell-cycle disruption. Furthermore, the Annexin-V/PI assay showed apoptotic-necrotic cell death in BC and predominant apoptotic cell death in HB cells. Notably, OP.SHP treatment markedly reduced Bcl-2 levels and significantly increased caspase-3 levels. Molecular docking analysis showed good binding affinity of RG toward AMPK and Bcl-2 (-8.7 and -8.0 kcal/mol, respectively). Conclusions: Lastly, OP.SHP demonstrated significant antitumor activity against both cell lines, highlighting its potential as a nanotherapeutic strategy for cancer treatment.

articles.title: Development and Characterization of Lysozyme-Loaded Gum Arabic as Buccal Films.
articles.abstract: Methods: Lysozyme-loaded gum arabic (GA) films were developed using a solvent-casting method and optimized through a 23 full factorial design to evaluate the effects of GA, citric acid (CA), and propylene glycol (PG) on film performance. Dependent variables included breaking hardness, mucoadhesivity, film thickness, moisture content, surface free energy (SFE), water uptake percentage, and disintegration time. A comprehensive set of evaluations was performed, including mechanical testing, mucoadhesion measurements, moisture and hydration analysis, disintegration time and surface free energy determination. Results: Mechanical testing revealed adequate flexibility, with breaking hardness values of a minimum of 10.8 N in the optimized formulation. Moisture content remained within an acceptable range, reaching approximately 1.5%, which contributed to suitable flexibility and handling. Disintegration testing showed rapid hydration behavior, with the optimized film disintegrating in an average of 2.98 min. Statistical analysis identified significant effects of GA, CA, and PG concentrations on several properties individually or interacting with each other, enabling the selection of an optimal combination that balanced mechanical integrity and mucoadhesivity. Conclusions: Overall, the optimized GA-based films demonstrate strong potential as a new effective mucoadhesive carrier for lysozyme delivery.

articles.title: Tween 80 Loading Nonmonotonically Modulates Curcumin Oral Exposure from Piperine-Containing TPGS-Based Amorphous Solid Dispersions.
articles.abstract: Objectives: This study investigated how polysorbate 80 (Tween 80; TW80) loading affects the biopharmaceutical performance of curcumin (CUR) amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs), focusing on the relationship between apparent dissolution and oral exposure. Methods: ASDs were prepared by rotary evaporation with piperine (PIP) as a bioenhancer and D-α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol 1000 succinate (TPGS) as an amphiphilic carrier. The CUR/PIP/TPGS mass ratio was fixed at 1:0.25:8, with 0, 1, 2, or 4 mass equivalents of TW80, yielding CPT, CPT-TW1, CPT-TW2, and CPT-TW4, respectively. CUR-excipient interactions and excipient self-assembly were examined using FT-IR, NMR, and pyrene fluorescence spectroscopy. Non-sink dissolution in water, PXRD of recovered precipitates, colloidal characterization, cell-associated CUR in MDCK cells, and rat pharmacokinetics were evaluated to assess relationships between in vitro performance and systemic exposure. Results: Spectroscopic findings supported noncovalent CUR-excipient interactions, while fluorescence measurements suggested mixed-excipient aggregation. Combining TPGS and TW80 markedly increased apparent CUR solubility. Higher TW80 loadings enhanced apparent dissolution, whereas colloidal size changed nonmonotonically. TW80-containing formulations yielded recovered solids with lower relative crystallinity indices than TW80-free CPT. ASDs increased cell-associated CUR relative to crystalline and amorphous CUR. However, oral exposure did not follow the dissolution ranking. CPT-TW1 produced the highest AUC0-t (281.2 ± 33.9 ng·h/mL), approximately 1.8-fold that of CPT (p < 0.01). Despite greater apparent solubilization, CPT-TW2 and CPT-TW4 yielded lower AUC0-t of 157.4 ± 17.2 and 109.2 ± 24.7 ng·h/mL, respectively. Conclusions: TW80 loading nonmonotonically affected oral CUR exposure. Higher apparent dissolution in water did not predict higher systemic exposure. Altered colloidal partitioning is a possible explanation requiring direct validation under biorelevant conditions. Surfactant loading should be optimized based on absorption-relevant performance rather than maximized solely to enhance apparent dissolution.

articles.title: Efficient Copper-Mediated Radiosynthesis of 6-[18F]Fluoro-L-DOPA ([18F]FDOPA) in a Microreactor.
articles.abstract: Objectives: The diagnostic radiopharmaceutical 6-[18F]Fluoro-L-DOPA ([18F]FDOPA) is a versatile positron emission tomography (PET) tracer used to image dopaminergic dysfunction in Parkinson's disease, brain tumors, and neuroendocrine disorders. Despite its broad clinical applications, [18F]FDOPA production remains challenging. The electron-rich aromatic structure has traditionally necessitated electrophilic [18F]F2 labeling, resulting in low molar activity and potentially increasing the risk of pharmacological effects. Copper-mediated radiofluorination of organoboron precursors using nucleophilic [18F]fluoride provides a promising alternative but remains constrained by lengthy preparation time and high precursor consumption. Here, we developed a microscale copper-mediated radiosynthesis of [18F]FDOPA using a chip-based microreactor. Methods: A comprehensive set of reaction parameters, including type and amount of phase-transfer catalyst and base, solvent and additive composition, precursor and copper reagent quantity, concentration of deprotectant, and reaction temperature and time, was systematically evaluated using high-throughput microscale experiments.
