articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors are a standard therapy for hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative breast cancer and are frequently administered as long-term therapy. While their efficacy is comparable, differences in symptom burden, need for supportive interventions, and interaction liability may substantially influence patient experience, adherence, and quality of life in real-world practice. Evidence based on patient-reported outcomes (PROs) addressing supportive care needs remains limited. Methods: A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based observational study was conducted among 155 women with HR+ breast cancer treated with abemaciclib, ribociclib, or palbociclib plus endocrine therapy, or endocrine therapy alone (control). Patient-reported symptoms, perceived deterioration, and responses indicating additional medication use were analyzed. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for individual symptom outcomes using Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. Exploratory pooled questionnaire-response outcomes were evaluated using patient-clustered logistic generalized estimating equations (GEE), without adjustment for potential confounders. BMI-stratified pooled-response analyses were considered exploratory. Results: Distinct patterns of patient-reported symptoms were observed across treatment groups. Abemaciclib was associated with higher odds of diarrhea and burdensome abdominal pain, whereas ribociclib was associated with higher odds of burdensome stomatitis/mucositis. Both agents were associated with increased reporting of burdensome nausea/vomiting. In exploratory GEE analyses, affirmative symptom responses were less frequent with ribociclib (OR 0.586, 95% CI 0.381-0.900; q = 0.022) and palbociclib (OR 0.353, 95% CI 0.230-0.541; q < 0.001), but not significantly different with abemaciclib (q = 0.073), compared with endocrine therapy alone. Responses indicating additional medication use were more frequent with abemaciclib (OR 2.192, 95% CI 1.380-3.484; q = 0.003), but not significantly different with ribociclib or palbociclib. BMI subgroup findings were exploratory and showed differences in symptom reporting during abemaciclib therapy. Conclusions: CDK4/6 inhibitors were associated with distinct patterns of patient-reported symptoms and supportive care needs. These findings highlight the importance of individualized symptom monitoring, structured medication review, and multidisciplinary supportive care during long-term breast cancer treatment.

articles.title: Aqueous Extracts from Leaves and Rhizomes of Posidonia oceanica (L.) Delile Suppress Extracellular Trap Formation in PMA-Challenged RAW 264.7 Macrophages.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Macrophage extracellular traps (ETs) contribute to host defense but, when excessively produced, participate in chronic inflammation, thrombosis, and tissue injury. Increasing attention is being directed toward identifying natural products capable of modulating macrophage ET formation and limiting ET-associated inflammatory responses. Methods: Aqueous extracts from green leaves (GLE) and rhizomes (RE) of Posidonia oceanica were evaluated for their effects on phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced extracellular trap (ET) formation in RAW 264.7 macrophages. ET-associated changes were assessed by immunofluorescence microscopy, extracellular DNA quantification, and dot blot analysis of released histones. Nitric oxide release and intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were also examined. Results: Both extracts reduced ET release, extracellular DNA levels, and histone H4 citrullination, while attenuating ROS production and nitric oxide release. Conclusions: P. oceanica GLE and RE attenuated PMA-induced ET formation in RAW 264.7 macrophages and modulated selected inflammatory and oxidative-stress-associated readouts. These findings support further investigation of P. oceanica biomass-derived extracts as potential modulators of ET-associated inflammatory disorders.

articles.title: Anemopaegma arvense Leaf Extract Attenuates Lipid Accumulation in Adipocytes, and Caenorhabditis elegans, and Reduces Weight Gain and Hypertriglyceridemia in Rats.
articles.abstract: Background: Obesity and hypertriglyceridemia are complex metabolic conditions that arise from the expansion of white adipose tissue and dysfunction in lipid metabolism. Given the limitations of conventional therapies, plant-derived extracts have been investigated as promising alternative strategies. Objectives: The present study aimed to characterize the phytochemical profile of the hydroethanolic extract from Anemopaegma arvense leaves (HEAa), assess its toxicological safety, and investigate its effects on metabolic phenotype safety related to lipid accumulation using complementary biological models. Methods: HEAa was chemically characterized by LC-DAD-MS, and its toxicological profile was assessed using complementary in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo models. Its effects on lipid-related metabolic phenotypes were assessed in adipocytes, Caenorhabditis elegans, and Wistar rats with high-fructose diet (HFrD)-induced body-weight gain and hyperlipidemia after 70 days of treatment. Results: HPLC-DAD-MS analysis revealed a chemically diverse profile composed mainly of flavonol glycosides, hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives, lipid-derived compounds, triterpenoids, megastigmane glycosides, and pheophorbide a; rutin was confirmed by comparison with an authentic standard. HEAa showed no hemolytic activity in human erythrocytes and did not reduce viability in C. elegans under the tested conditions. In 3T3-F442A adipocytes and C. elegans, HEAa produced modest reductions in neutral lipid accumulation. In high-fructose-fed Wistar rats, repeated HEAa administration reduced body-weight gain by approximately 53% and serum triglycerides by approximately 56% compared with untreated high-fructose-fed animals. Increases in ALT and AST levels were observed following prolonged exposure. Conclusions: HEAa modulated lipid accumulation and obesity-related metabolic phenotypes across complementary experimental models, with effects on body-weight gain and hypertriglyceridemia in rats fed a high-fructose diet. These findings support further investigation of A. arvense as a botanical candidate for metabolic disorders, nevertheless, the increases in hepatic enzymes highlight the need for additional studies to define its long-term safety.

articles.title: Integrated Experimental and Computational Discovery of the Oxazole-Thiadiazole-Sulfonamide Hybrids as Dual α-Amylase and α-Glucosidase Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: Background: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major global health concern. Inhibition of α-amylase and α-glucosidase is an established approach to controlling postprandial glucose levels. In this study, we aimed to synthesize oxazole-thiadiazole-sulphonamide derivatives (1-14) and evaluate their inhibitory activity against both enzymes. Methods: Fourteen derivatives were synthesized and characterized using 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and high-resolution electron ionization mass spectrometry (HR-EI-MS). Their inhibitory activities were evaluated using acarbose as the reference inhibitor. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis and molecular docking studies were performed to investigate the influence of aromatic substitution and explore potential enzyme-ligand interactions. Results: Compound 5 had the strongest inhibitory activity, displaying values of IC50 6.20 ± 0.30 µM for α-amylase and 6.70 ± 0.20 µM for α-glucosidase, in comparison with 10.50 ± 0.20 µM and 11.10 ± 0.30 µM, respectively, for acarbose. The other derivatives showed varying inhibitory activities. Docking analysis provided computational insights into possible interactions within the enzyme binding sites. Conclusions: Compound 5 was the most potent derivative in the series against both enzymes and represents a promising in vitro candidate for further biochemical, mechanistic, and safety evaluation.

articles.title: Ferulic Acid Ameliorates Blood Deficiency Syndrome Associated with Rebalancing G2/M-Related Cell Cycle Programs: Insights from Integrated Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analyses.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Blood deficiency syndrome (BDS) shows disturbed hematopoietic and immune homeostasis under conditions of chronic stress. Ferulic acid (FA), the principal bioactive constituent of the dried root of Angelica sinensis (Oliv.) Diels, is used widely to relieve BDS symptoms, yet its mechanism remains unclear. We examined the therapeutic effects and possible mechanisms of FA in benzene-induced BDS. Methods: We established a benzene-induced BDS mouse model to evaluate the pharmacological effects of FA. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were performed on splenic tissues, followed by Western blot validation. The effects of FA on cell-cycle distribution were further explored in K562 cells. Results: FA improved behavioral performance, restored peripheral blood indices, alleviated pathological damage, and partially normalized abnormal cytokine levels. Multi-omics integration revealed aberrant activation of G2/M-related cell-cycle pathways in BDS, which FA reversed. Among the identified candidates, UBE2C stood out as a hub node tied to G2/M regulation. In K562 cells, FA altered the G2-phase distribution without much loss of viability. Conclusions: Overall, FA ameliorates BDS in a manner tied to rebalancing of the G2/M phase, highlighting UBE2C as a potential candidate regulatory node associated with its hematopoietic protective effects.

articles.title: Novel Inhibitory Effect of Benztropine on Early Adipogenesis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Benztropine, a muscarinic acetylcholine receptor antagonist used to treat Parkinson's disease, has been used clinically for decades, and weight loss has been reported during its use; however, its role in adipocyte differentiation remains unclear. Methods: Lipid accumulation was quantified by Oil Red O (ORO) staining. Adipogenic mRNA and protein levels were examined by reverse transcription-quantitative PCR and Western blotting. β-Catenin depletion, subcellular fractionation, and T-cell factor/lymphoid enhancer-binding factor (TCF/LEF) reporter assays were used to further examine the contribution of β-catenin. Results: Benztropine inhibited lipid accumulation in 3T3-L1 cells in a dose-dependent manner without reducing cell viability. Intracellular triglyceride content was lowest at 15 μM benztropine and after treatment during days 0-3 of differentiation. It reduced the mRNA and protein levels of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ), CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein α (C/EBPα), fatty acid synthase (FASN), and fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4). The anti-adipogenic effect of benztropine was most pronounced during the early stage of differentiation, where it suppressed C/EBPβ expression, followed by PPARγ and C/EBPα. Mechanistically, benztropine enhanced glycogen synthase kinase-3β phosphorylation at Ser9 and elevated β-catenin levels during early differentiation. Moreover, β-catenin depletion partially reversed the suppressive effects of benztropine on adipogenic genes and proteins. Benztropine also promoted cytoplasmic β-catenin accumulation and reduced TCF/LEF-dependent reporter activity. Conclusions: Collectively, these findings suggest that benztropine is a novel inhibitor of early adipocyte differentiation and has the potential to control early adipose tissue expansion.

articles.title: Novel Aroyl Pyrrole Derivatives as Antiproliferative Agents Against Breast and Colorectal Cancer Cells: Design, Synthesis and Biological Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background: The development of resistance to conventional therapies remains one of the major challenges in the treatment of breast and colorectal cancers, highlighting the urgent need for novel anticancer agents with improved efficacy. In the present study, a series of novel aroyl pyrrole derivatives was designed and synthesized, evolving from the previously identified hit compound 1a, in order to investigate the influence of structural modifications on antitumor activity. Methods: The antiproliferative activity of all compounds was evaluated in vitro against two human breast cancer cell lines (MCF7 and MDA-MB231) and two colorectal cancer cell lines (HT-29 and RKO). Result: Among the synthesized derivatives, compound 3 emerged as the most active analog, displaying antiproliferative activity at low micromolar concentrations and significantly improved potency compared with the parent compound 1a in all tested cell lines. Furthermore, 3 did not show any significant cytotoxicity toward non-transformed HaCaT keratinocytes and normal dermal fibroblasts, suggesting a remarkable degree of selectivity for tumor cells. Flow cytometric analysis demonstrated that both 1a and 3 induced cell-cycle arrest at the G0/G1 phase in all four cancer cell lines, indicating inhibition of cell-cycle progression as one of the mechanisms underlying their antiproliferative activity. Furthermore, both compounds induce cell death in a small percentage of cells through a caspase-3/7-independent mechanism. Conclusions: Overall, these findings identify 3 as a promising compound for the development of novel pyrrole-based anticancer agents and provide useful information on structure-activity relationships for the future optimization of this chemical scaffold.

articles.title: Three New Compounds from the Endophytic Fungus Trichoderma oligosporum in Croton tiglium, with Anti-Inflammatory Activity and Molecular Dynamics Studies.
articles.abstract: Background: Endophytic fungi are prolific sources of structurally diverse and biologically active compounds. However, anti-inflammatory constituents of Trichoderma oligosporum, an endophyte of the medicinal plant Croton tiglium, remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to isolate and characterize anti-inflammatory compounds from this fungus. Methods: Compounds were isolated from T. oligosporum and characterized by 1D/2D NMR and HRMS. Nitric oxide (NO) production was measured in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, with dexamethasone as control; cytotoxicity was assessed by CCK-8 assay. Compound 2 was further studied by ELISA, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting, and potential targets were probed by molecular docking and dynamics simulations. No preregistration was required, as no humans or animals were studied. Results: Three new compounds, oligosporins D-F (1-3), and 17 known compounds (4-20) were isolated. Compounds 1-3 inhibited NO production with IC50 values of 40.05 ± 4.92, 30.56 ± 4.74, and 51.88 ± 4.69 µM (dexamethasone, 40.43 ± 3.59 µM), while 14 and 19 were less potent; none was cytotoxic. Compound 2 reduced pro-inflammatory mediator secretion and down-regulated iNOS, TNF-α, and IL-6 mRNA. It also attenuated LPS-induced phosphorylation of IκBα and NF-κB p65 and restored IκBα expression. In all simulations, compound 2 remained bound within or near the iNOS heme pocket (MM-GBSA, -16.77 to -27.64 kcal/mol). Conclusions: Oligosporins D-F (1-3) are new compounds from T. oligosporum, with compound 2 being the most promising anti-inflammatory candidate. It apparently acts at least partly by inhibiting iNOS-mediated NO production and NF-κB activation. These findings warrant further investigation of T. oligosporum as an anti-inflammatory source.

articles.title: Multi-Source Transcriptomic and Structural Prioritization of Adansonia digitata Phytochemicals in Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a major therapeutic challenge, and the molecular targets potentially associated with the cardiovascular activity of Adansonia digitata phytochemicals remain incompletely characterized. This study integrated phytochemical, transcriptomic, disease-gene, network, and structural evidence to prioritize candidate phytochemical-MI target associations. Methods: Ten polyphenols were selected from published LC-MS/QTOF data. Targets predicted using SwissTargetPrediction and PharmMapper were integrated with MI-associated evidence from the GSE66360 (circulating endothelial cell), GSE325257 (cardiac targeted gene-expression), and DisGeNET. An initial composite analysis generated a 19-gene discovery module for network and structural prioritization. A complementary source-resolved sensitivity analysis independently evaluated the three MI evidence sources. Selected interactions were examined by molecular docking, 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA binding free-energy estimation. Results: Sensitivity analysis identified 189 genes supported by at least two MI evidence sources, including 21 predicted Adansonia digitata targets. Four genes (GSK3B, NOS3, SOD2, and TGFBR1) were shared between the 19-gene discovery and 21-gene sensitivity modules. Gene Ontology analysis identified 36 significantly overrepresented biological-process terms (FDR < 0.05). Docking supported the selection of chlorogenic acid and rutin for simulation with MMP2 and NOS3. MM/PBSA calculations indicated that chlorogenic acid exhibited more favorable estimated binding energies compared to rutin, especially in the case of MMP2. However, these differences were not statistically validated. Conclusions: The complementary integration strategies prioritized candidate Adansonia digitata phytochemicals and MI-associated targets and generated testable hypotheses for further investigation. These computational findings are hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation of target engagement, biological activity, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy in MI models.

articles.title: Hyssopus cuspidatus Boriss. Attenuates Myocardial Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury by Modulating the Keap1-Nrf2-GPX4 Axis: Identification of 4,5-Dicaffeoylquinic Acid as a Keap1-Binding Constituent.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms and potential active constituents of SXCF (the active fraction of Hyssopus cuspidatus Boriss.) against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MIRI). Results: SXCF pretreatment significantly reduced myocardial infarct size, ameliorated histopathological damage, and suppressed oxidative stress and inflammation in I/R mice. Network pharmacology integrated with lipidomics suggested that SXCF primarily targets lipid peroxidation. SPR further demonstrated that 4,5-dicaffeoylquinic acid, a candidate active constituent of SXCF, directly binds to Keap1 with high affinity (KD = 1.86 μM), which may interfere with Keap1-mediated Nrf2 regulation and facilitate Nrf2 nuclear translocation. This was accompanied by the upregulation of GPX4 and SLC7A11, downregulation of ACSL4, and reduced 4 HNE production, suggesting the involvement of the Keap1-Nrf2-GPX4 axis and effective inhibition of lipid peroxidation. Methods: UPLC HRMS was used to characterize the chemical composition of SXCF and identify its absorbed blood constituents. A mouse myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) model was established to evaluate the cardioprotective effects of SXCF. Network pharmacology combined with targeted lipid mediator profiling was applied to predict and verify its regulatory effects on cardiac lipid metabolism. Molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were utilized to identify direct binding targets, while immunofluorescence, Western blot, and qRT PCR were performed to validate key molecules of the Keap1-Nrf2-GPX4 axis. Conclusions: SXCF alleviates MIRI by suppressing lipid peroxidation. Its candidate active constituent, 4,5-dicaffeoylquinic acid, directly binds to Keap1 and may interfere with Keap1-mediated regulation of Nrf2, potentially engaging the Keap1-Nrf2-GPX4 axis to attenuate ferroptosis-associated lipid peroxidation. This study provides a potential therapeutic strategy and material basis for the treatment of MIRI.

articles.title: Screening and Evaluation of Computationally Predicted JAK1-Binding Candidates from Multi-Source Chemical Space Using Deep Learning and Generative Models.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) is a key mediator in inflammatory and autoimmune signaling pathways and represents a validated therapeutic target. Despite the availability of several JAK inhibitors, challenges in safety and efficacy persist, necessitating further computational prioritization of candidate molecules. Methods: We developed an integrated virtual screening workflow combining ensemble deep learning scoring (KPGT, KarmaDock, DrugCLIP), ADMET-AI filtering, and AutoDock Vina (v1.2.3) docking. The workflow was applied to the NPBS Atlas natural-product database and to molecules generated by 3DSMILES-GPT. Selected candidates were further evaluated by molecular dynamics simulations, DFT calculations, and synthetic accessibility assessment, with Filgotinib used as a reference compound. Results: Three natural-product-derived and three AI-generated molecules were prioritized. Among them, the MM-PBSA-estimated binding free energies were -26.251 kcal/mol for NPBS_111591, -19.858 kcal/mol for 3DSMILES_17365, and -19.593 kcal/mol for 3DSMILES_38767, compared with -29.253 kcal/mol for the reference compound Filgotinib. These MM-PBSA values were obtained under the same computational protocol and can provide relative computational comparisons, but pharmacological potency still requires validation by IC50 or biochemical binding assays. Conclusions: The study prioritizes computationally predicted JAK1-binding candidates and provides a multi-stage in silico workflow for further experimental evaluation.

articles.title: Metformin Attenuates Cardiac Developmental Toxicity in High-Glucose-Exposed Zebrafish Larvae: Oxidative Stress, Hif-1α-Associated Metabolic Gene Alterations, and Wnt Signaling Changes.
articles.abstract: Background: Maternal hyperglycemia is associated with embryonic developmental abnormalities and congenital heart defects, yet the mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. We examined high-glucose-induced cardiac developmental injury in zebrafish and whether metformin co-administered with high glucose is associated with protection. Methods: Wild-type AB and Tg(myl7:EGFP) zebrafish (Danio rerio) embryos were exposed to control medium, high glucose (150 mM), or high glucose plus metformin (0.75, 3.0, or 6.0 mM); metformin alone was not tested. Hatching and survival rates, cardiac morphology and function, larval locomotor activity, oxidative-stress markers, and cardiac developmental and pathway transcripts/proteins were assessed. Results: Under high-glucose exposure conditions (150 mM), hatching and survival were reduced, cardiac morphology/function and locomotor activity were altered, hand2, gata4, tbx1, and tbx5 were downregulated, Gata4 was decreased, oxidative stress was increased, and Hif-1α expression and downstream metabolic targets were increased. Wnt-related readouts were heterogeneous: Gsk3β Ser9 phosphorylation, β-catenin and Daam1 decreased, whereas Dvl2 increased. Metformin was associated with improved survival, cardiac phenotypes, and locomotor outcomes, together with partial molecular restoration. As an osmolarity-matched control was not included, these phenotypes cannot be attributed exclusively to glucose-specific effects. Conclusions: High-glucose exposure conditions are associated with cardiac developmental injury and pathway dysregulation, and metformin shows protective associations. These findings are not causal, do not distinguish glucose-specific effects from hyperosmotic stress, and require osmolarity-matched controls, functional metabolic assays, and Hif-1α/Wnt perturbation studies.

articles.title: Nanostructured Lipid Carriers for Enhancement of Oral Delivery of Ebastine: In Vitro and In Vivo Investigation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ebastine is a second-generation non-sedative antihistamine with potent anti-inflammatory activity. The therapeutic efficacy of ebastine is limited by its low water solubility. Accordingly, this study aimed to formulate nano lipid-based systems to enhance the anti-inflammatory potential of ebastine. Methods: Nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) loaded with ebastine were formulated using the micro-emulsification technique. The prepared systems were characterized for particle size (PS), zeta potential (ZP), morphological features using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), entrapment efficiency (%EE), and in vitro drug release. The in vivo anti-inflammatory efficacy was also evaluated employing the carrageenan-induced paw edema model. Results: The constructed NLCs demonstrated negatively charged spherical nanoparticles with average particle sizes ranging from 146.7 nm to 293.0 nm. Ebastine was effectively trapped in the NLCs, with the recorded %EE ranging from 96.4% to 97.5%. All the fabricated NLCs revealed a sustained ebastine release behavior over 8 h compared to the aqueous drug dispersion. In vivo performance evaluations demonstrated a significant improvement in the anti-inflammatory efficacy of ebastine-loaded NLCs compared to unprocessed ebastine aqueous dispersion. This was manifested in the significant reduction of the rats' paw edema, with the % edema inhibition reaching 31.3%, 40.2%, and 35.2% for F1, F2, and F3, respectively. However, without a blank NLC control, the isolated effect of ebastine could not be fully distinguished from that of the carrier. Additionally, histopathological examinations revealed a remarkable reduction in the inflammation score in thin and thick skin sections for NLC groups compared to the untreated negative control group. Notably, F2 and F3 showed significant improvement in thin-skin inflammation scores. Conclusions: The tested NLCs potentially demonstrated an improved anti-inflammatory efficiency compared to the free drug. The overall findings introduced NLCs as a promising nanoplatform for enhancing the pharmacodynamic efficacy of ebastine.

articles.title: KDM4B Regulates Replication Fork Stability During Replication Stress in Concert with Poly(ADP-ribose) Metabolism in Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase-1 (PARP1) and poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG) coordinately regulate poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR) metabolism, which is essential for maintaining genome integrity during DNA replication. We investigated the role of the histone demethylase KDM4B in replication-fork protection and whether KDM4 inhibition could be exploited therapeutically in prostate cancer. Methods: The role of KDM4B in replication stress was examined in prostate cancer cells using genetic and pharmacological approaches. KDM4B interactions with PARG, stalled replication forks, and DNA fork structures were assessed using biochemical and molecular assays. Replication-fork stability, chromatin-associated proteins, PARylation, and DNA damage were evaluated following KDM4 inhibition. The therapeutic effects of combined KDM4 and PAR metabolism inhibition were assessed using the KDM4 inhibitor B3 together with the PARP inhibitor olaparib or the PARG inhibitor PDD00017273. Results: KDM4B interacted with PARG and localized to replication stress-associated ssDNA regions, where its depletion increased H3K9me3 accumulation and impaired PARG and XRCC1 accumulation. KDM4B directly bound fork-like DNA structures in vitro, and PARylation enhanced this interaction. Genetic depletion of KDM4B or pharmacological KDM4 inhibition disrupted replication stress responses, altered PAR signaling, and increased replication-associated DNA damage. Proteomic analysis using a synthetic Y-DNA probe revealed changes in the association of replication- and repair-related proteins following KDM4 inhibition. Combined treatment with B3 and either olaparib or PDD00017273 produced synergistic cytotoxicity in prostate cancer cells, particularly in the context of TP53/RB1 deficiency, with pronounced activity of the B3-PDD00017273 combination in HRR-proficient PC3 cells. Conclusions: These findings identify KDM4B as a regulator of replication stress responses and support a functional interplay between KDM4B and PAR metabolism in maintaining replication fork integrity. The synergistic cytotoxicity observed with combined KDM4 and PARP/PARG inhibition provides a rationale for further preclinical investigation, although the efficacy and tolerability of these combinations remain to be established in vivo.

articles.title: Interleukin-9 Promotes Liver Fibrosis in Schistosomiasis Japonica by Regulating Retinoic Acid Expression.
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the molecular mechanism by which interleukin-9 (IL-9) mediates liver fibrosis in schistosomiasis japonica through disruption of retinoic acid (RA) homeostasis, and to determine the protective effect of exogenous RA intervention against hepatic fibrosis in schistosomiasis japonica. Methods: Eighteen mice were randomly assigned to three groups: normal control (NC), Schistosoma japonicum (S. japonicum) infection (SJ), and RA intervention (SJ + RA). After 9 weeks of infection, liver fibrosis indicators were measured by qRT-PCR, Western blotting, ELISA, and immunohistochemistry. In cell experiments, hepatic stellate cells (HSC) were stimulated with IL-9, and an HSC-mast cell transwell co-culture system was established; HSC activation markers were examined, and key genes in the RA synthesis and metabolic pathways were identified by RNA-seq and verified by qRT-PCR. In addition, exogenous RA was applied to TGF-β1-activated HSC to investigate the inhibitory effect of RA on HSC activation. Results: Animal experiments showed that S. japonicum infection significantly upregulated the IL-9 mRNA expression in mouse liver tissues, increased the infiltration of IL-9-positive cells in the egg granuloma areas, and markedly reduced the hepatic RA content. Cell experiments showed that IL-9 stimulation alone did not directly induce HSC activation; however, in the HSC-mast cell co-culture system, IL-9 significantly upregulated the expression of HSC activation markers. RNA-seq analysis combined with qRT-PCR verified that, under HSC-mast cell co-culture conditions, the lipid droplet-associated proteins PLIN2 and PLIN3 were downregulated, with a more pronounced decrease in PLIN3, whereas RDH10, the rate-limiting enzyme of RA synthesis, was upregulated, approaching but not reaching statistical significance. Furthermore, in vivo and in vitro rescue experiments confirmed that exogenous RA supplementation effectively inhibited HSC activation and alleviated the liver fibrosis induced by S. japonicum infection. Conclusions: IL-9 suppressed PLIN2/3 expression and impaired RDH10-mediated RA expression via mast cell paracrine signaling. The resulting decline in local hepatic RA concentration disrupted the quiescent state of HSC, ultimately inducing aberrant HSC activation and thereby promoting the progression of liver fibrosis in schistosomiasis japonica.

articles.title: Design and Discovery of Potent Benzofuran Oxadiazole MAT2A Inhibitors: Synthesis, Structure Activity Relationships, and Molecular Modeling.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Methionine adenosyltransferase 2A (MAT2A) has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancers harboring methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP) deletion. However, the development of potent, drug-like MAT2A inhibitors with favorable pharmacokinetic profiles remains challenging. This study aimed to design, synthesize, and evaluate a library of benzofuran-based oxadiazole derivatives as novel MAT2A inhibitors and to elucidate their molecular basis of action through integrated computational studies. Methods: A series of benzofuran-based oxadiazole derivatives (10a-10j and 16-19) was designed, synthesized, and characterized by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). All compounds were evaluated for MAT2A inhibitory activity, with AZ-28 used as the reference inhibitor. The most active compounds were subjected to molecular docking, 200 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and in silico ADME/toxicity prediction. No preregistration was applicable, and no animals were used in this study. Results: The synthesized compounds exhibited a broad range of MAT2A inhibition, with IC50 values from 0.0116 ± 0.0020 to 28.77 ± 1.79 μM, benchmarked against AZ-28 (IC50 = 0.0419 ± 0.0032 μM). Compounds 10g (IC50 = 0.0116 ± 0.0020 μM), 10a (IC50 = 0.0883 ± 0.0060 μM), and 19 (IC50 = 0.158 ± 0.015 μM) were the most potent. Docking revealed favorable binding orientations within the MAT2A active site, supported by hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic interactions. MD simulations showed stable protein-ligand complexes with favorable RMSD profiles, and binding free-energy calculations supported complex stability. DFT analyses (HOMO-LUMO and MEP) provided insight into electronic properties and reactive sites. Furthermore, in silico ADME and toxicity assessments provided preliminary insights into the drug-likeness and pharmacokinetic properties of the studied compounds. Nevertheless, these computational predictions remain preliminary and require experimental validation. Conclusions: Compounds 10g, 10a, and 19 are promising MAT2A inhibitors, with 10g identified as the most favorable lead. These computational predictions remain preliminary and require experimental validation. Further pharmacokinetic, toxicological, and in vivo studies of 10g are warranted.

articles.title: Deuterium Oxide Labeling and Single-Cell Stimulated Raman Scattering Imaging for Rapid Antifungal Response Assessment in Seven Yeast Species from China.
articles.abstract: Background: Fungal infections cause over 1.5 million deaths worldwide annually, and timely antifungal susceptibility testing (AST) is important for guiding treatment of invasive fungal infections. Methods: We evaluated deuterium oxide (D2O) labeling combined with single-cell stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) imaging in seven clinical yeast isolates of non-albicans Candida and non-Candida yeasts from the China Hospital Invasive Fungal Surveillance Net, one each of Candida tropicalis, Candida parapsilosis, Candida guilliermondii, Candida haemulonii, Cryptococcus neoformans, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and Wickerhamomyces anomalus. Twelve isolate-drug combinations were examined using fluconazole, voriconazole, micafungin, or amphotericin B. An exploratory Raman-based MIC was defined as the lowest tested concentration showing a statistically significant change in intracellular C-D signal relative to the drug-free control. Test concentrations were selected around MICs obtained using Sensititre YeastOne (SYO). Results: Eleven of 12 Raman-based MICs were within one twofold dilution of the corresponding SYO MIC (91.7%). The C. guilliermondii-micafungin Raman-based MIC differed by two dilutions. This numerical agreement is distinct from categorical agreement. Azole exposure increased C-D signals, whereas micafungin and amphotericin B decreased them in the isolates tested. The complete workflow includes overnight culture followed by a 6-8 h analytical interval; prior isolation requires additional time. Conclusions: These observations support further evaluation of an exploratory metabolic-response assay, but do not establish equivalence to growth-based MICs or clinical validity. Independent-replicate analysis and blinded testing of larger isolate collections are required.

articles.title: A Single-Blind, Randomised, Placebo-Controlled Phase 1 Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Inhaled Londamocitinib (AZD4604) Following Single Ascending and Multiple Doses in Healthy Japanese and Chinese Participants.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study seeks to evaluate the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of londamocitinib, an inhaled selective Janus kinase 1 (JAK-1) inhibitor, in healthy Japanese and Chinese participants after administration of single and multiple doses. Methods: A two-part, single-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 study was conducted, which included healthy male and female adult Japanese and Chinese participants who received single ascending doses (1 mg to 4 mg) or multiple doses of 3 mg twice daily of inhaled londamocitinib for 7 days. Results: A total of 32 Japanese and 24 Chinese participants were enrolled and dosed. No severe or serious adverse events were noted, and londamocitinib exhibited an acceptable safety and tolerability profile. After single and multiple doses, londamocitinib was rapidly absorbed, with maximal plasma concentration (Cmax) reached at a median time ranging from 0.07 to 0.1 h post-dose, and post-maximal plasma concentrations declined in a biphasic manner. In Japanese participants, Cmax increased with dose in an approximately dose-proportionate manner, and total drug exposure (AUCinf) increased in a less than dose-proportionate manner following single doses. In Chinese participants, dose proportionality was not explored. Accumulation of londamocitinib following twice-daily dosing was not different in Japanese and Chinese participants, ranging from a 3.50- to 3.54-fold increase in the area under the curve within the dosing interval (AUCtau) and a 1.63- to 1.89-fold increase in Cmax. Steady state was achieved after approximately 6 days based on geometric mean and individual trough concentrations. Conclusions: Londamocitinib's pharmacokinetic, safety and tolerability profiles in Japanese and Chinese participants were consistent with previous results in healthy participants. The observed PK profiles do not suggest clinically meaningful ethnic differences requiring dose adjustment.

articles.title: Phytochemical Profile and Anti-Inflammatory Potential of an Ethanolic Semi-Purified Fraction from Myrtus communis L. Leaves Formulated as a Nanoemulsion.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study characterized an ethanol-eluted, semi-purified fraction (F4) from Myrtus communis L. leaves and compared its anti-inflammatory activity in free and nanoemulsified forms. Methods: F4 was obtained by C8 fractionation, examined by colorimetric assays, targeted LC-MS (SIM) and COX-2 docking, and incorporated into an oil-in-water nanoemulsion. Oral activity at 200 and 400 mg/kg was assessed in male Wistar rats with carrageenan-induced paw edema (seven groups; n = 6/group). The primary endpoint was the individual area under the curve (AUC) of edema over 1-5 h. Results: Targeted LC-MS tentatively annotated ten compounds. The total phenolic content of F4 was 186.75 ± 0.43 mg GAE/g, and apigenin had the most favorable predicted COX-2 docking score (-8.1 kcal/mol). The nanoemulsion measured 119.07 ± 16.28 nm on day 0 and showed no phase separation under stress tests. Free F4 and F4 nanoemulsion (F4 NE) reduced AUC versus the inflamed control, and F4 NE reduced AUC versus the blank nanoemulsion (Holm-adjusted p < 0.0001). Compared with free F4, nanoemulsification decreased mean AUC by 37.7% and 42.9% at 200 and 400 mg/kg (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0362 for both comparisons). After baseline adjustment, the difference persisted at 400 mg/kg (-2.94 mL·h; 95% CI -5.16 to -0.72; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0304) but not at 200 mg/kg (-1.61 mL·h; 95% CI -4.27 to 1.06; Holm-adjusted p = 0.2053). Conclusions: Orally administered F4 had anti-inflammatory activity, and nanoemulsification produced improved anti-inflammatory efficacy under the tested conditions, as shown by the lower cumulative edema. Bioavailability was not assessed; pharmacokinetic studies are needed to determine whether it underlies this effect.

articles.title: Pharmacological Effects of Bidirectional Solid-State Fermentation Product of Irpex lacteus and Panax notoginseng on Mice with Lupus Nephritis.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a severe complication of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and remains a critical challenge in clinical treatment. This study aimed to investigate the early-intervention effects and underlying mechanisms of Panax notoginseng fermented by Irpex lacteus (FS) in MRL/lpr mice with LN, to provide a theoretical basis for the medicinal development of FS and clinical intervention for LN. Methods: MRL/lpr mice were administered low-dose and high-dose FS for 8 consecutive weeks. Therapeutic efficacy of FS was systematically evaluated by detecting renal function indicators, autoantibody levels, and inflammatory factor expression. Meanwhile, Western blot (WB) was performed to detect the expression of key proteins in the renal PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathway, and 16S rRNA sequencing was used to analyze structural changes in intestinal microbiota. Results: Pharmacodynamic results revealed that, compared with the model group and raw Panax notoginseng group, high-dose FS significantly improved renal function in LN mice, reduced the levels of urine protein, creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, autoantibodies and inflammatory factors (p < 0.05). Observations from representative histological specimens suggested amelioration of renal pathological manifestations including glomerular proliferation, inflammatory infiltration and renal fibrosis. Mechanistic analyses revealed associations between FS treatment and reduced phosphorylation of proteins within the renal PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathway (p < 0.05), as well as partial shifts in gut-microbiota composition suggestive of improved intestinal microecology. Conclusions: FS exerts anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory and renal-protective effects. Our observations suggest associations between FS treatment, altered PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway activity and shifts in gut-microbiota composition related to the gut-kidney axis. This study provides important theoretical and experimental evidence for the medicinal development of FS and targeted early-intervention strategies for lupus nephritis.

articles.title: An Integrated NONMEM-Based Framework for Ticagrelor Exposure-PRU Modeling and Patient-Level Outcome Prediction Assessment.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ticagrelor reduces ischemic events in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) but may increase bleeding in susceptible patients. We used a population PK and PK/PD model to describe ticagrelor exposure and platelet reactivity unit (PRU) dynamics and assessed whether model-predicted PRU improved prediction of subsequent outcomes in a patient-level analysis. Methods: We collated published evidence from 39 ticagrelor clinical studies (172 group-level datasets). The final population PK and indirect-response PK/PD models for ticagrelor, AR-C124910XX, and PRU were implemented in NONMEM with a two-compartment structure, three transit absorption compartments, and prespecified covariate relationships. Model-predicted PRU from recorded prescription exposure was linked to subsequent outcomes in a de-identified UK Biobank cohort using a prespecified 90-day landmark analysis. Cox models with clinical variables, recorded medication exposure, and model-predicted PRU were compared; a 30-day landmark analysis was used for sensitivity analysis. Results: The final model retained a two-compartment structure with three transit absorption compartments and quantified age, disease status, concomitant aspirin, and fasting effects on exposure. The indirect-response model linked combined parent-metabolite molar concentration to continuous PRU dynamics. In 731 UK Biobank participants, the 90-day ischemic, bleeding, and all-cause death analyses included 112, 48, and 129 events, respectively. Adding model-predicted PRU did not show stable incremental discrimination; all paired-bootstrap intervals for C-index and Brier-score increments crossed zero. Conclusions: We established a NONMEM-based framework linking ticagrelor dosing, exposure, and PRU dynamics to patient-level outcome prediction assessment. Although incremental predictive benefit was not established in the current cohort, the framework provides a basis for further evaluation using paired measured PK, PRU, and clinical outcome data before clinical application.

articles.title: Resveratrol-Induced Relaxation of the Human Saphenous Vein in Patients with and Without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: The Role of Nickel-Sensitive Pathways and Phrixotoxin-Sensitive Vascular Kv4 Channels.
articles.abstract: Background: Graft stenosis and graft failure remain frequent complications of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). People with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represent a significant proportion of patients requiring CABG surgery, as T2DM induces vascular damage and impairs vasorelaxation. Resveratrol (RSV), a naturally occurring polyphenol with potent vasorelaxant properties, has emerged as a potential adjuvant for graft preservation solutions. While multiple pathways contribute to its effects, RSV-induced relaxation in endothelium-denuded segments is driven by direct action on vascular smooth muscle tissue, involving various voltage-dependent potassium (Kv) channels and sodium-calcium exchanger type 1 (NCX-1). Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the mechanism of RSV-induced relaxation in the human saphenous vein (HSV) from patients with and without T2DM, focusing on the roles of specific 4-AP-sensitive Kv channels, particularly margatoxin-sensitive (Kv1.2 and Kv1.3) and phrixotoxin-sensitive (Kv4.1-Kv4.3) subtypes, as well as the nickel-sensitive NCX-1. Methods: Samples of HSVs were taken after CABG surgery in two national cardiovascular clinics. Pharmacological experiments were conducted using isolated organ baths. To test the involvement of Kv1.2, Kv1.3, Kv4.1-Kv4.3, and the nickel-sensitive NCX-1 pathway in RSV-induced relaxation, the following blockers were utilized: 4-aminopyridine (4-AP), margatoxin (MgTox), phrixotoxin (PhTox), and nickel. Protein expression was investigated via Western blot. Results: A total of 112 HSV segments obtained from 49 patients (27 with T2DM; 22 non-diabetic controls (NDM)) were analyzed. RSV caused a concentration-dependent relaxation of the HSV, which was significantly less effective in the T2DM group than in the NDM group (pD2 = 4.79 ± 0.05 vs. pD2 = 5.04 ± 0.05, respectively, p = 0.001). 4-AP significantly antagonized RSV-induced relaxation of the HSV in both groups. MgTox did not block the relaxant response in either group, though a distinct variation in maximal efficacy (Emax) was noted in the T2DM group. Notably, PhTox and nickel significantly attenuated RSV-induced relaxation in the NDM group but exerted no significant effect in the T2DM group. Conclusions: RSV induces concentration-dependent relaxation in endothelium-denuded HSV segments from both NDM and T2DM patients. In non-diabetic patients, this relaxation is partially mediated by 4-AP-sensitive and PhTox-sensitive Kv channels, alongside nickel-sensitive pathways, likely corresponding to NCX-1. Conversely, these specific pathways appear compromised and do not contribute to RSV-induced relaxation in patients with T2DM. The involvement of alternative 4-AP-sensitive K channels, including other subtypes of Kv channels, cannot be ruled out in either patient group.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics and Effect of Novel Sydnonimine on NO and cGMP Accumulation In Vivo.
articles.abstract: Background: Sydnonimines are mesoionic heterocyclic NO donors with vasodilatory activity. Molsidomine, a clinically approved sydnonimine, has limited blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, restricting its use for cerebrovascular disorders. This study characterizes the lead compound BBP2023 as a potential NO donor with putative cerebral action. Methods: In silico ADME profiling (RDKit) of 14 sydnonimines, rat pharmacokinetics of oral BBP2023 (11 mg/kg) vs. molsidomine (10.4 mg/kg), HPLC-MS/MS of NO/cGMP, and docking against four human sGC PDB entries were performed. Results: BBP2023 showed high lipophilicity (logP 1.58), low TPSA (69.78 Å2) and predicted high BBB permeability. After oral dosing, BBP2023 was rapidly absorbed (plasma Tmax 0.17 h, Cmax 389 ng/mL, AUC_last 235 h·ng/mL) and extensively distributed, with highest exposure in liver (AUC_last 1457 h·ng/mL, ~6-fold plasma), indicating primary hepatic metabolism. Brain penetration was confirmed (fr = 1.39, MRT 3.01 h). The active metabolite BBP2023 A appeared later (plasma Tmax 1.00 h, Cmax 22 ng/mL) and accumulated in the lungs (fr = 25.31, AUC_last 1569 h·ng/mL) and brain (fr = 3.65, MRT 4.16 h). Compared with molsidomine, BBP2023 achieved higher brain exposure (availability 1.4 vs. 0.2, Cmax 852.5 vs. 142.3 pmol/mL) and faster brain Tmax (≤0.25 h vs. 1 h). BBP2023 significantly increased NO and cGMP in the brain (131.00 ± 26.39 nM/g and 1070.83 ± 92.04 pM/g, respectively), whereas molsidomine predominantly elevated heart NO. Docking and MM-GBSA calculations suggested possible interactions of BBP2023 and its metabolites with the sGC stimulator site and associated the intact sydnonimine ring with more favorable calculated scores. Conclusions: BBP2023 acts as a NO donor with favorable pharmacokinetics, effective BBB penetration, and brain NO/cGMP accumulation, supporting its further development for cerebrovascular disorders.

articles.title: Synthesis, Antiproliferative Activity and In Silico Conformational Analysis of Triazole-Tethered Vindoline-Chalcone Hybrids Targeting the Vinblastine Site of Microtubules.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cancer is one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide. However, due to limitations in clinical treatment of malignancies, there is a continuous need for the development of more potent novel drugs with enhanced activity and selectivity towards tumours. Methods: In this context, we synthesised a focused library of chalcone-vindoline hybrids incorporating a 1,4-disubstituted 1,2,3-triazole linker using a modular strategy combining sequential Sonogashira coupling and CuAAC reactions. The same synthetic route afforded a zidovudine-derived vindoline hybrid, which served as a negative control to underscore the pivotal role of the chalcone moiety in mediating antiproliferative activity. To elucidate the contribution of the vindoline scaffold, two corresponding aryl-substituted chalcone analogues were also prepared. The synthesised hybrids and the reference compounds were evaluated against a panel of human adherent cancer cell lines (HeLa, SiHa, MCF-7, MDA-MB-231 and A2780) and non-malignant NIH/3T3 fibroblasts. Results: Vindoline hybrids incorporating trimethoxyphenyl chalcone moieties exhibited outstanding potency on all the cancer cell lines tested. By contrast, hybrids containing monomethoxy-substituted chalcone moieties with moderately reduced activity against malignant cells displayed a certain degree of cancer selectivity. A ferrocene-containing hybrid and the vindoline-free chalcones exhibited markedly lower antiproliferative activity, whereas another ferrocene hybrid featuring an alternative enone configuration and the zidovudine-derived vindoline hybrid were inactive. Molecular modelling results indicate that the vindoline hybrids might bind to the inter-dimer vinca crevice of tubulin oligomers and that the two segments exert a mutually stabilising effect on the binding of the other. Conclusion: Collectively, these findings provide a framework for future rational optimisation of this promising class of anticancer agents.

articles.title: Ethanol Extract of Huang-Jin-Shuang-Shen Enhances Oxaliplatin Responses in Gastric Cancer Models: Associations with FBLN1 and Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Background: Platinum-based chemotherapy, particularly oxaliplatin (OXA), is a primary treatment modality for advanced gastric carcinoma. However, the development of apoptotic resistance and enhanced DNA repair mechanisms frequently compromises its enduring clinical benefit. Objectives: The present research aims to evaluate whether an ethanol extract of Huang-Jin-Shuang-Shen (HJSS-E) can modulate cellular sensitivity to oxaliplatin and to characterize the associated molecular pathways. Methods: Potential interacting proteins were screened through an integration of DARTS-based proteomics and transcriptomic database mining (TCGA). The subsequent biological effects were examined employing RNA sequencing, fluorescent organelle probes (Rhod-2 AM and JC-1), murine tumor models, patient-derived organoids (PDOs), and multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) at single-cell resolution. Results: HJSS-E enhanced OXA-associated DNA damage and apoptosis in gastric cancer cells and improved treatment responses in xenograft and patient-derived organoid models. Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS) and Cellular Thermal Shift Assay (CETSA) identified Fibulin-1 (FBLN1) as a candidate target. Combination treatment was associated with altered Ryanodine Receptor 2 (RYR2)/Sirtuin 3 (SIRT3) expression, reduced ATP content and NAD+/NADH ratios, and increased mitochondria-associated Rhod-2 fluorescence. Salvianolic acid A (SAA) interacted with recombinant FBLN1 in SPR assays and reproduced selected cellular effects of HJSS-E. Conclusions: HJSS-E potentiates the antitumor efficacy of OXA in preclinical gastric cancer models, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction and coordinated alterations in RYR2/SIRT3 expression. FBLN1 emerges as a candidate molecular mediator of this response.

articles.title: Systemic Safety and Neuroprotective Potential of Chronic ∆9-THCA-Enriched Extract Administration: Divergent Effects on Molecular Neuroprotection and Physical Endurance in Aging Models.
articles.abstract: Background: Aging is characterized by inflammaging, a progressive decline in metabolic homeostasis, and increased neuroinflammation. While the endocannabinoid system (ECS) regulates these processes, its tone diminishes with age. This study investigated the systemic safety and therapeutic potential of a full-spectrum, ∆9-THCA-enriched Cannabis extract in naturally aged rats. Methods: Aged Sprague-Dawley rats received intermittent oral doses (5 days on/2 days off) of a ∆9-THCA-enriched extract (0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 mg/kg) for six weeks. Assessments included body weight monitoring, physical endurance (treadmill), and neuromotor coordination (rotarod). Post-mortem evaluations encompassed systemic histopathology, serum biochemistry, and hippocampal immunohistochemistry for microglial (Iba-1), astrocytic (GFAP), and apoptotic (caspase-3) markers. Results: The extract demonstrated excellent systemic safety, with hepatic and renal markers remaining within physiological ranges. Treatment significantly attenuated age-related weight loss, with the 2.0 mg/kg dose achieving the most robust preservation (p < 0.001). In the hippocampus, the extract induced a reversal of neuroinflammation mediated by Iba-1, reducing Iba-1-positive microglial density by 93.5-97.9% across all doses (p < 0.001). Although the reduction was substantial at all doses, greater inter-individual variability was observed in the OLD-0.5 group. The extract also significantly attenuated apoptotic signaling (p = 0.029). Conversely, a dose-dependent reduction in peak physical endurance was observed, driven by increased task refusal rather than neuromotor impairment. Principal Component Analysis confirmed a phenotypic shift toward metabolic and neuroinflammatory stability at the cost of maximal aerobic power. Conclusions: Chronic intermittent administration of a ∆9-THCA-enriched extract reconfigures the aged phenotype, prioritizing metabolic maintenance and neuroprotection. These findings suggest full-spectrum cannabinoids serve as a viable geroprotective for neuroinflammatory stress, although their functional impact warrants careful consideration in the context of frailty.

articles.title: Toward Non-Hormonal Treatment of Endometriosis: Selective Antiproliferative and Pro-Apoptotic Effects of a Boron-Curcumin-Piperine Combination on Eutopic Endometrial Cells from Women with Endometriosis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Current medical treatments for endometriosis are largely hormonal and are limited by side effects and recurrence. We investigated whether a combination of sodium pentaborate pentahydrate, curcumin, and piperine selectively inhibits eutopic endometrial cells from women with endometriosis. Methods: Stromal- and glandular-enriched primary cultures were established from endometrial biopsies of four women with surgically and histologically confirmed endometriosis and four women without endometriosis. Cells were treated with the combination (50-500 μg/mL) for 24-72 h. Viability was measured by MTS assay, and half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC50) were estimated for each donor. Apoptosis was assessed by annexin V/propidium iodide flow cytometry at each donor's approximate IC50. Results: Viability decreased in a dose- and time-dependent manner. At 48 h, IC50 values were approximately two-fold higher in control-derived than in endometriosis-derived cells for both glandular (321.3 ± 89.6 vs. 160.4 ± 40.1 μg/mL) and stromal (351.8 ± 59.4 vs. 179.0 ± 29.9 μg/mL) cells (selectivity indices 2.00 and 1.97), with complete separation between groups (Cohen's d 2.3 and 3.7; Mann-Whitney p = 0.029, the minimum attainable with four donors per group). The combination increased apoptosis compared with untreated cells from the same donor in both glandular (54.5 ± 17.2% vs. 8.7 ± 4.9%; p = 0.022) and stromal (55.2 ± 8.0% vs. 8.4 ± 6.5%; p < 0.001) cells, with no difference between cell types (p = 0.95). Conclusions: This non-hormonal combination selectively reduced the viability of eutopic endometrial cells from women with endometriosis and induced apoptosis in these cells in vitro, with comparable potency in the enriched stromal and glandular fractions. These preliminary findings warrant validation in lesion-derived cells and in vivo models.

articles.title: The Impact of Metformin on Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Thyroid Axis Activity and Thyroid Autoimmunity: A Protocol for Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Metformin is one of the most frequently used insulin-sensitizing drugs. Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and other insulin-resistant states often coexist with thyroid pathology, and many patients with thyroid dysfunction and/or autoimmunity receive this agent. Despite theoretical premises, studies assessing the impact of metformin on thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), thyroid hormones, and thyroid antibody titers have provided inconsistent results. Objective: This systematic review will identify, critically appraise, and synthesize the available evidence on the effects of metformin treatment on hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis activity and thyroid autoimmunity among adults receiving metformin for T2D or polycystic ovary syndrome. Methods: Primary studies and grey literature examining the impact of metformin on HPT axis activity and thyroid autoimmunity will be included. Searches will be performed in MEDLINE via PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and ClinicalTrials.gov registry, with no date or language restrictions. Google Scholar will be used exclusively during the preliminary search to identify relevant articles and inform search strategy development. After duplicate removal, two independent reviewers will conduct title and abstract screening in Rayyan, followed by full text assessment in JBI SUMARI according to the inclusion criteria. Disagreements will be resolved through preliminary discussion between the reviewers, and a third reviewer will be consulted for a final decision if necessary. Data extraction will be performed independently by two reviewers using a standardized extraction form. Where appropriate, random-effects meta-analysis will use mean differences or standardized mean differences for continuous outcomes, with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals. Heterogeneity will be assessed using I2 and τ2, alongside prediction intervals. Small-study effects will be assessed when at least 10 studies are available. Prespecified subgroup analyses will examine thyroid status, autoimmunity, diagnosis, treatment, and study design; sensitivity analyses will assess robustness. The review will be reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. The certainty of the evidence will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. The protocol has been registered in the Open Science Framework.

articles.title: Thiazolyl-Methylthio-1,3,4-Thiadiazolyl-Quinazolin-4(3H)-ones Hybrids: Synthesis, In Silico Profiling, Cytotoxicity, Cellular Death Evaluation, and Effects on Irradiation-Associated DNA Damage.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Combining heterocyclic fragments provides a strategy for developing compounds for exploratory anticancer evaluation. This study aimed to synthesize and characterize five thiazolyl-methylthio-1,3,4-thiadiazolyl-quinazolin-4(3H)-one compounds (5a-e), assess their properties in silico, and investigate the selected ones for cytotoxicity and their effects on irradiation-associated DNA lesions. Methods: Structures were characterized by IR, HRMS, and 1H- and 13C-NMR spectroscopy. Computational studies included physicochemical and ADMETox predictions, multi-platform target prediction, and molecular docking to A2A, Erβ, and CDK5. Compounds 5a and 5b were evaluated for cytotoxicity and cell-death profiles on one colorectal cancer (CRC) cell line (HT-29), two breast cancer (BC) cell lines (MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231), and one healthy fibroblast cell line (BJ), using cisplatin (Cis) as a reference. DNA lesions were assessed by the Comet assay in both breast cancer models before, immediately after, and 24 h after 4 Gy irradiation. Results: Compounds 5a-e were obtained in yields of 45.17-83.27%. Compounds 5a and 5b had lower 24-h IC50 values than cisplatin in MCF-7 cells, but higher values in the other tested cell lines. Compound 5b showed higher selectivity indexes than both 5a and cisplatin across the cancer models, although its values of 1.14-1.34 indicated modest selectivity. Cell-death profiles differed between treatments, with larger necrotic fractions following 5a or 5b treatment in MCF-7 cells. Both compounds were associated with higher post-irradiation lesion scores than untreated irradiated controls. Scores increased further at 24 h in MCF-7 cells but decreased in MDA-MB-231 (triple-negative) cells. Pre-irradiation scores were also elevated in treated MCF-7 cells. Computational profiling identified comparatively more favorable predicted solubility for 5a and 5b. Cross-platform ADMET comparison consistently indicated low Caco-2 permeability, CYP3A4 inhibition, potential liver-injury risk, and high plasma-protein binding, while several absorption, transporter, and safety endpoints remained discordant. Target predictions showed weak cross-platform convergence. Docking provided the strongest, although moderate, structural support for A2A binding by 5a-d. Conclusions: The findings support further investigation of 5a and 5b, particularly their effects on irradiation-associated DNA lesions. Priorities include improving potency and selectivity, validating in silico predictions, and evaluating radiosensitizing potential through clonogenic survival studies.

articles.title: Novel Photodynamic Methods for the Preparation of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Autovaccines.
articles.abstract: Background: The aim of this pilot study was to evaluate the potential of Pseudomonas aeruginosa autovaccines obtained by a photodynamic method as a possible approach to improving the prevention and treatment of P. aeruginosa infections. Methods: Autovaccine samples were produced using an original method based on photodynamic inactivation of candidate strains of P. aeruginosa with riboflavin mononucleotide and menadione sodium bisulfite as photosensitizers, followed by irradiation with ultraviolet light and light from a photopolymer lamp. The toxicity of the obtained vaccine samples was evaluated in experiments on white mice by assessing their general condition and body-weight dynamics after intraperitoneal and/or subcutaneous administration of the candidate preparations in comparison with a control (non-vaccinated) group. The protective properties of the autovaccines were assessed by survival rates of vaccinated animals after infection with a virulent culture of P. aeruginosa. Therapeutic efficacy was studied by analyzing the survival of experimental animals after intraperitoneal infection followed by administration of the vaccine according to different schedules at various stages of the disease. Results: The effectiveness of the photodynamic method for inactivation of candidate P. aeruginosa strains was evaluated in five series of autovaccines. No viable P. aeruginosa cells were detected in peritoneal samples collected from vaccinated animals under the investigated experimental conditions. No signs of acute toxicity or local adverse reactions were observed following administration of the vaccine preparations. Vaccinated animals demonstrated higher survival rates following experimental infection with virulent homologous P. aeruginosa strains compared with non-vaccinated controls, indicating protective activity of the autovaccines. Evaluation of the therapeutic properties of the autovaccines also demonstrated improved survival of experimentally infected animals, depending on the timing and vaccination regimen. Conclusions: The results of this pilot experimental study support the potential of the modified photodynamic method for the preparation of P. aeruginosa autovaccines. The obtained vaccine preparations demonstrated protective and therapeutic activity in a murine experimental model. However, further investigations are required to characterize their antigenic composition, evaluate the underlying immunological mechanisms and assess their safety and potential efficacy before considering clinical application.

articles.title: Pharmacogenomic Modulators of Drug Transport, Detoxification, Oxidative Stress and Inflammation: Insights from SLC22A2, GSTP1, SOD2 and TNF-α for precision medicine.
articles.abstract: Background: Interindividual variability in drug response remains a fundamental clinical problem, arising from the combined influence of genetic, physiological, and environmental factors. This review examines four pharmacogenomically significant genes, SLC22A2, GSTP1, SOD2 and TNF-α, involved in drug transport, detoxification, oxidative stress and inflammatory pathways.Method: Clinical evidence linking variants of these genes to altered drug responses, toxicity profiles and therapeutic outcomes was evaluated.Results: SLC22A2 (OCT2) influences renal uptake of metformin, cisplatin and aminoglycosides. Its variants modify treatment response, and increase individual susceptibility to nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. GSTP1 is a major Phase II metabolic enzyme. Its variants affect detoxification, oxidative stress and may cause chemotherapy resistance. SOD2 is an antioxidant enzyme that protects mitochondria from damage. Its variants alter ROS handling and increase risk of anthracycline cardiotoxicity and platinum-induced tissue injury. TNF-α variants amplify inflammatory cascades and are associated with variability in autoimmune drug response and immunotherapy-related inflammation.Conclusion: These genes act across interconnected pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic pathways, so studying their polymorphisms together can explain interindividual variability better than single-gene analysis. Combined genotyping of these genes has the potential to improve drug safety, toxicity prediction, and dosage optimization, although this benefit has not yet been demonstrated in prospective clinical trials.

articles.title: A Systems Level Logic Model of the Neuroinflammatory Response in Late Stage G93A SOD1 Mice.
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a pathological hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in both animal models and human patients, yet its systems-level behavior remains poorly characterized, due to sparse and heterogeneous data. To address this, a discrete Boolean logic model was developed comprising 33 nodes to qualitatively simulate neuroimmune interactions in the SOD1G93A mouse model of ALS, with a focus on RIPK1-mediated signaling. Cell-type specific sub-models for microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, T-cells, and motor neurons were constructed from literature-derived cytokine and phenotype data and integrated into a wider network of the neuroimmune response. Simulations in MaBoSS identified three stable states: homeostatic (82.9%), and two microglial dominated states (RIPK1 regulated inflammatory microglia (14.0%) and disease associated microglia (2.7%)). The model reproduced experimental perturbation outcomes, including TNF-α and IL6 knockouts on SOD1 backgrounds, and captured population-level trends in microglial and oligodendrocyte states. Unbiased node inhibition suggested oligodendrocyte death pathways regulated by pRIPK1 (p(Motor neuron survival) = 1.00) and pro-inflammatory phenotypes (A1, DAM; p(Motor neuron survival) = 0.58 and 0.36 respectively) as potent therapeutic targets, while cytokine-only strategies were less effective. Correlation analysis identified TNF-αHigh (r = -0.81), CCL2 (r = -0.72), IL6 (r = -0.71) and IFN-γ (r = -0.62) as candidate biomarkers of disease progression. Despite its qualitative nature, the model recapitulated known inflammatory dynamics and motor neuron trajectories, demonstrating the utility of logic-based modeling in translational ALS research. This framework provides a mechanistic platform for hypothesis generation, therapeutic prioritization, and biomarker evaluation in data-sparse neurodegenerative contexts.
